fields.doc: The inverse of [`m_UwSwimmingCapsuleOffset`](Self::m_UwSwimmingCapsuleOffset).

fields.name: m_SurfaceIdleSwimmingCapsuleOffset
fields.doc:
The capsule offset used while treading water at the surface: the **identity**. The surface
 movement core ([`UpdateSurfaceMovement`](input::swim::UpdateSurfaceMovement)) selects this
 one when the stick is neutral or the wanted horizontal speed is at most 0.1, so a
 near-stationary surface swimmer's capsule frame and orientation frame coincide.

fields.name: m_SurfaceIdleSwimmingCapsuleOffsetInv
fields.doc:
The inverse of
 [`m_SurfaceIdleSwimmingCapsuleOffset`](Self::m_SurfaceIdleSwimmingCapsuleOffset).

fields.name: m_SurfaceCrawlSwimmingCapsuleOffset
fields.doc:
The capsule offset used while crawling at the surface: `RotationX(-1.5707951)`, exactly a
 quarter turn about X, laying the capsule flat for the prone crawl pose. The surface movement
 core selects this one whenever the wanted horizontal speed exceeds 0.1, so a moving surface
 swimmer's capsule frame is pitched 90 degrees away from its orientation frame -- the matrix
 reaching
 [`PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation`](physics::PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation) is
 the capsule frame, not the facing frame, and a yaw/pitch/roll decomposition of it is at
 gimbal lock.

fields.name: m_SurfaceCrawlSwimmingCapsuleOffsetInv
fields.doc:
The inverse of
 [`m_SurfaceCrawlSwimmingCapsuleOffset`](Self::m_SurfaceCrawlSwimmingCapsuleOffset).

fields.name: m_CurrentSwimmingCapsuleOffsetInv
fields.doc:
The inverse of whichever capsule offset the movement core selected this frame, written just
 before it calls
 [`PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation`](physics::PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation).
 Recovers the orientation frame from the capsule frame.

fields.name: m_AnimatedTurnBaseDir
fields.doc:
The world-space ground-plane direction the animated turn starts from, latched when a turn
 act is dispatched (or, for the grapple and planted-explosive cases, re-latched from the
 character's current forward as the act begins).

fields.name: m_AnimatedTurnTargetDir
fields.doc:
The world-space ground-plane direction the animated turn ends at. The movement cores slerp
 from [`m_AnimatedTurnBaseDir`](Self::m_AnimatedTurnBaseDir) to this by the local time of the
 angle-correction animation segment, which is what makes a swim turn advance in act-sized
 steps rather than continuously.

associated_functions.name: Construct
associated_functions.doc:
`SSwimActionParams::SSwimActionParams`: initializes the parameters, including the fixed
 capsule offsets and their inverses.

fields.name: m_Time
fields.doc: Real elapsed milliseconds, advanced by every [`Update`](Self::Update) regardless of pause.

fields.name: m_RealTimeAtUpdate
fields.doc:
Real elapsed milliseconds as of the last [`Update`](Self::Update), advanced regardless of
 pause.

fields.name: m_RealTimeAtUpdateGame
fields.doc: The game-side counterpart of [`m_RealTimeAtUpdate`](Self::m_RealTimeAtUpdate).

fields.name: m_PauseTimeAtUpdate
fields.doc:
The value of [`m_RealTimeAtUpdate`](Self::m_RealTimeAtUpdate) latched when the clock
 enters pause; `GetRealTimeAtUpdate` returns it instead while paused.

fields.name: m_PauseTimeAtUpdateGame
fields.doc:
The value of [`m_RealTimeAtUpdateGame`](Self::m_RealTimeAtUpdateGame) latched when the
 clock enters pause.

fields.name: m_PauseTime
fields.doc:
Elapsed milliseconds that advance only while the clock is not stopped; `GetTime` returns it
 unless asked to ignore pause.

associated_functions.name: GetSPF
associated_functions.doc:
Returns [`PAUSED_SPF`](Self::PAUSED_SPF) while stopped (unless `ignore_pause`), the forced
 SPF when forcing a frame rate, and `m_SPF` otherwise.

associated_functions.name: Pause
associated_functions.doc:
Sets `m_Stop`; on the transition into pause, latches the real-time-at-update counters into
 their pause-time counterparts.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame tick. Measures the `QueryPerformanceCounter` delta and updates `m_SPF` (an
 exponential moving average), `m_RealSPF`, `m_FPS`, and `m_GameTimeMicro`.

kind.doc:
The seconds-per-frame value [`GetSPF`](Self::GetSPF) returns while the clock is stopped and
 `ignore_pause` is false.

The engine's fixed 15-phase CPU frame profiler (`g_CpuProfiler`): phase brackets record QPC
 begin/end pairs into a triple-buffered counter ring, and a once-per-frame update converts the
 completed ring slot into per-phase milliseconds with a rolling 30-frame peak.

 The machinery is dead: [`Update`](Self::Update) is compiled to an
 empty function, and the phase brackets that write [`m_Counters`](Self::m_Counters) are
 compiled out of `CGame::Update` and the game states, so every field stays zero. The consumers
 remain -- [`BorkReport`](bork_report::BorkReport)'s telemetry serialises [`m_Time`](Self::m_Time) via
 [`GetScopeName`](Self::GetScopeName), and `CGraphicsEngine::DispatchDraw` forwards
 [`m_Index`](Self::m_Index) to the draw task -- but they only ever read zeros.

fields.name: m_Time
fields.doc:
The last completed frame's milliseconds per phase, converted from
 [`m_Counters`](Self::m_Counters) by [`Update`](Self::Update).

fields.name: m_Peak
fields.doc: The rolling peak per phase over the 30-frame peak window.

fields.name: m_Index
fields.doc: The counter ring position; [`Update`](Self::Update) reads slot `(m_Index + 1) % 3`.

fields.name: m_Counters
fields.doc: QPC begin/end pairs, per phase, per ring slot: `[phase][ring slot][begin, end]`.

fields.name: m_LocalPeak
fields.doc:
The running peak within the current 30-frame window, promoted into
 [`m_Peak`](Self::m_Peak) when the window rolls.

associated_functions.name: Update
GetScopeName
associated_functions.doc:
The phase's display name from [`cpu_scope_names`] (`"FRAME"`, `"DRAW"`, `"UPDATE_ALL"`,
 ...). Does not read `self`.

kind.doc:
The fixed frame-phase ids of the engine's CPU profiler ([`CpuProfiler`]). Each phase is one
 slot in the profiler's per-frame time and counter arrays; the names come from the static table
 behind [`GetScopeName`](CpuProfiler::GetScopeName).

The engine's CPU profiler instance (`g_CpuProfiler`), a statically allocated object rather than a
 pointer: [`BorkReport::WriteMetrics`](bork_report::BorkReport::WriteMetrics) passes its address
 directly as `this` to [`CpuProfiler::GetScopeName`].

The static name table behind [`CpuProfiler::GetScopeName`]: one name string per
 [`CpuScopeId`] phase, indexed by the id.

fields.name: m_Weather
fields.doc: The live weather, also returned by [`GetWeather`](Self::GetWeather).

associated_functions.name: Apply
associated_functions.doc: Reads and writes both the time of day and the weather each cycle.

kind.doc:
The live weather state: a continuous scalar model.

 [`WeatherController`]'s per-frame update overwrites these scalars toward its own targets unless a
 force flag or a named weather event (see [`WeatherController::Init`]) holds them.

fields.name: m_SnowRatio
fields.doc:
The snow blend, in `0..1`.

 The offset is unconfirmed.

fields.name: m_RainIntensity
fields.doc:
The rain intensity, in `0..1`.

 The offset is unconfirmed.

fields.name: m_Severity
fields.doc: The storm severity, from roughly `0.1` (clear) to `4.0` (full storm).

associated_functions.name: SetSeverity
associated_functions.doc:
Sets `m_Severity` and clears the severity-update flag. The controller's per-frame update
 overwrites the result unless a force flag or weather event holds it (see [`Weather`]).

associated_functions.name: UpdateSeverityTarget
associated_functions.doc: Smoothly drives the severity toward `target` over `update_time` seconds.

associated_functions.name: Init
associated_functions.doc:
Subscribes the named weather events (the `EVENT_*` constants, plus `cloud_base` and
 `cloud_height`). A fired event holds its weather state; without one, the controller's
 per-frame update overwrites the [`Weather`] scalars.

kind.doc: Applies the pinned state instantly rather than blending toward it.
Pins rain (severity `4.0`, rain intensity `1.0`, snow `0`).
Hands control back to the ambient weather system.
Pins snow (severity `4.0`, snow ratio `1.0`).
Pins clear weather (severity `0.1`).

fields.name: m_CurrentTimeOfDay
fields.doc:
The current time of day, in hours. The render engine copies this out each frame for
 lighting.

associated_functions.name: SetTimeOfDay
associated_functions.doc:
Sets the time of day in hours: wraps to a 24-hour range, fires the per-hour event, and clamps
 against `m_PauseTimeOfDay`.

kind.doc:
A game object's set of attached effects and sounds (`CAttachedEffectContainer`, a base of weapons,
 the grappling hook, and other game objects), with the effect parameter sources that feed them.

fields.name: m_ParameterSources
fields.doc: The head of the parameter-source list.

fields.name: m_PlayingInstances
fields.doc: The head of the playing-instance list.

fields.name: m_CurrentTime
fields.doc: The container's accumulated time, advanced by [`UpdateAttachedEffects`](Self::UpdateAttachedEffects).

associated_functions.name: UpdateAttachedEffects
associated_functions.doc:
Advances the container by `dt`: for each playing instance, runs
 [`AttachedInstance::UpdateTransform`] and the instance update, and frees instances whose
 effects and sounds have all finished; then re-evaluates the parameter sources and pushes
 changed values to their sound and effect outputs.

kind.doc:
One playing attached effect or sound (`NAttachedEffectContainer::SAttachedInstance`): an offset
 and a transform function that resolves where it is attached (typically a bone or socket on the
 owner's model, such as a weapon muzzle), the effect and sound instances, and the resolved
 placement. The container links its playing instances through
 [`m_NextPlaying`](Self::m_NextPlaying).

fields.name: m_Offset
fields.doc: The instance's offset from its attachment point.

fields.name: m_TransformFunc
fields.doc:
Resolves the attachment's world placement: called with the result buffer, the owning
 container, this instance, and [`m_TransformExtraData`](Self::m_TransformExtraData).

fields.name: m_RotationMode
fields.doc: How the instance's rotation follows the attachment.

fields.name: m_TranslationMode
fields.doc: How the instance's translation follows the attachment.

fields.name: m_NextPlaying
fields.doc: The next playing instance in the owning container's list, or null.

fields.name: m_TransformInfo
fields.doc: The resolved placement, refreshed by [`UpdateTransform`](Self::UpdateTransform).

fields.name: m_MeasuredVelocity
fields.doc:
The per-update velocity of the placement's translation: the position delta multiplied by
 1/30, or zero for a transform that is not
 [`ETransformType_Transform3D`](TransformType::ETransformType_Transform3D).

fields.name: m_TransformExtraData
fields.doc: The opaque argument passed to [`m_TransformFunc`](Self::m_TransformFunc).

associated_functions.name: UpdateTransform
associated_functions.doc:
Re-resolves the instance's placement for `container`. When the rotation mode is
 [`ERotationMode_ATTACHED`](RotationMode::ERotationMode_ATTACHED) or
 [`ERotationMode_ATTACHED_RANDOM_ROLL`](RotationMode::ERotationMode_ATTACHED_RANDOM_ROLL), or
 the translation mode is
 [`ETranslationMode_ATTACHED`](TranslationMode::ETranslationMode_ATTACHED), it calls [`m_TransformFunc`](Self::m_TransformFunc) and copies
 the [`EffectTransformInfo`] it returns into
 [`m_TransformInfo`](Self::m_TransformInfo); it then applies the transform modes and derives
 [`m_MeasuredVelocity`](Self::m_MeasuredVelocity) from the translation delta.

kind.doc:
The world placement handed to a playing attached effect (`SEffectTransformInfo`): a transform,
 the velocity of the attachment, and what the transform is used for. Resolved per instance each
 update by the instance's transform function and copied whole into
 [`AttachedInstance::m_TransformInfo`].

fields.name: m_Transform
fields.doc: The world transform (in a union with a custom speaker mix for audio spatialization).

fields.name: m_Velocity
fields.doc: The attachment's velocity.

fields.name: m_Type
fields.doc: What the transform drives.

kind.doc:
How an attached instance's rotation follows its attachment
 (`CAttachedEffectContainer::ERotationMode`).
What an [`EffectTransformInfo`] transform drives (`SEffectTransformInfo::ETransformType`).

variants.name: ETransformType_Transform3D
variants.doc: A 3D world transform.

kind.doc:
How an attached instance's translation follows its attachment
 (`CAttachedEffectContainer::ETranslationMode`).

A thrown or placed explosive object (`CExplosive`, a `CGameObjectAmmunition<CDamageable>`): its
 physics body, trail effect, detonation timers, and the deferred launch that
 [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward) sets up for the physics body to apply later.

fields.name: m_WorldMatrixT1
fields.doc:
The explosive's world matrix as of the current simulation tick. Its translation row is the
 launch start position [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward) solves from.

fields.name: m_RelativeVelocity
fields.doc:
The velocity of the thrower when the explosive was launched, stored by
 [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward).

fields.name: m_DeferredPropelTowards
fields.doc:
Whether a launch is pending: set by [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward) and applied to the
 physics body with [`m_DeferredInitialVelocity`](Self::m_DeferredInitialVelocity) on a later
 update.

fields.name: m_DeferredInitialVelocity
fields.doc:
The solved launch velocity awaiting application to the physics body, written by
 [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward) from the virtual `VelocityToHitTarget`.

fields.name: m_TimeSinceThrow
fields.doc: Seconds since the explosive was thrown; [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward) resets it.

associated_functions.name: PropelToward
associated_functions.doc:
Launches the explosive toward `target_position`: when it has a physics body, stores
 `relative_velocity` in [`m_RelativeVelocity`](Self::m_RelativeVelocity), raises
 [`m_DeferredPropelTowards`](Self::m_DeferredPropelTowards), solves the launch velocity from
 its current position with the virtual `VelocityToHitTarget` into
 [`m_DeferredInitialVelocity`](Self::m_DeferredInitialVelocity), starts the trail effect,
 and resets [`m_TimeSinceThrow`](Self::m_TimeSinceThrow). The target point is the only aim
 input; the solver chooses the flight time.

associated_functions.name: VelocityToHitTarget
associated_functions.doc:
Solves the launch velocity from `start_pos` to `aim_pos`: clamps the target to
 `max_range`, chooses a flight time from the grenade weapon's arc tuning (flat, up, and down
 times blended by distance and elevation; roof targets use a height-based time), and solves
 with [`NWeaponUtil::Trajectory_GetVelocityToHitPosition`](equipment::weapon::NWeaponUtil::Trajectory_GetVelocityToHitPosition)
 under world gravity.

kind.doc:
A hand grenade (`CGrenade`, a [`Explosive`]): adds bounce counting, homing and smart-fuse
 targets, extra trail effects, and the landing position.

fields.name: m_CanUseUpgrades
fields.doc: Whether the grenade applies the thrower's grenade upgrades (homing and similar).

fields.name: m_InitialLandingPos
fields.doc:
The target position the grenade was thrown at, recorded by
 [`PropelToward`](Self::PropelToward).

associated_functions.name: PropelToward
associated_functions.doc:
The [`Explosive::PropelToward`] override: calls it, records `target_position` in
 [`m_InitialLandingPos`](Self::m_InitialLandingPos), plays the extra trail effects, and, with
 upgrades enabled and the homing upgrade owned, starts the homing-target search.

associated_functions.name: VelocityToHitTarget
associated_functions.doc:
The [`Explosive::VelocityToHitTarget`] override: wraps it and adds the thrower's relative
 velocity unless the grenade has a homing target or `exact_target_aiming` is set.

kind.doc:
The grappling-hook equipment item (`CGrapplingHook`, a `CGameObject`): owns the wires, the
 reel/tether state machine, and the cached fire target. A character's hook is held by its
 inventory ([`Inventory::m_GrapplingHook`](character::inventory::Inventory::m_GrapplingHook)).

fields.name: m_State
fields.doc:
The current state-machine state; see [`GrapplingHookState`]. The state records the *last*
 reel outcome as much as the current one: leaving a `GHS_REELED_*` attachment does not
 reliably return it to [`GHS_INACTIVE`](GrapplingHookState::GHS_INACTIVE) — readers such as
 `IsHookAimingState` and `ShouldShowAttachedUI` therefore combine it with
 [`m_ActiveWire`](Self::m_ActiveWire) rather than trusting it alone.

fields.name: m_HookFireInfo
fields.doc:
The latched fire target, filled by [`SetUpTarget`](Self::SetUpTarget) when the hook fires.
 [`GetLastGrappleTargetPos`](Self::GetLastGrappleTargetPos) reads its current world position,
 so the fire and its arm IK follow the latched target rather than the live aim slot.

fields.name: m_WaitForFireSignalTimeout
fields.doc:
The countdown (seconds) armed when a hook fire is committed, within which the fire
 animation must emit its release track message before the fire is abandoned. Set to `2.0`
 alongside [`m_WaitingForGrappleFire`](Self::m_WaitingForGrappleFire) by the fire
 dispatchers (`FireHookTowardsPos`, `TryFireHook`).

fields.name: m_WaitingForGrappleFire
fields.doc:
Whether a grapple-hook fire is committed and awaiting the fire animation's release track
 message: set when the fire dispatches (before the fire act plays and the wire spawns),
 cleared when the hook releases or the fire times out. The fire act's directional alignment
 of the character runs within this window.

fields.name: m_WaitingForTetherFire
fields.doc:
The dual-tether counterpart of
 [`m_WaitingForGrappleFire`](Self::m_WaitingForGrappleFire); the two are cleared
 together as one word.

fields.name: m_CachedReelTargetPosition
fields.doc:
The cached reel-in target position in world space. The reel-in aim IK turns the chest
 toward it while a wire is active. The offset is confirmed; the name is
 unconfirmed.

fields.name: m_ActiveWire
fields.doc:
The wire currently driving the reel/attach flow, or null when none is live. The state
 readers null-check this before interpreting [`m_State`](Self::m_State).

associated_functions.name: SetUpTarget
associated_functions.doc:
Latches the `player`'s (a `CPlayer`) aim slot `target_type` into `target_info`: reads the
 slot's [`m_AimPos`](aim::aim::PlayerAimControl::m_AimPos) and
 [`m_Target`](aim::aim::PlayerAimControl::m_Target) from the player's aim control, stores the
 position in the target object's space, and falls back to the aim control's current grapple
 game object only for [`TARGET_GRAPPLE`](TargetType::TARGET_GRAPPLE). Later changes to the
 aim slot do not move the latched target.

associated_functions.name: GetLastGrappleTargetPos
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the latched fire target's current world position
 ([`m_HookFireInfo`](Self::m_HookFireInfo)) and returns true.

associated_functions.name: TryFireHook
associated_functions.doc:
Computes the fire direction toward the latched target and hands it to
 [`DoActFire`](Self::DoActFire).

associated_functions.name: DoActFire
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the directional fire act for `aim_direction` on `holder`: picks the
 `ACT_GRAPPLE_FIRE_*` sector (or `ACT_GRAPPLE_TETHER_FIRE_*` for a dual tether) from the
 angle between the direction and the character. No wire is created here; the hook spawns on
 the fire animation's release track message.

associated_functions.name: OnPreSimUpdate
associated_functions.doc:
The pre-simulation hook update: dispatches the grapple input (fire, reel, dual tether,
 retract, release) and advances the reel and tether state.

associated_functions.name: OnPostCamUpdate
associated_functions.doc:
The post-camera hook update. On the fire animation's release frame it creates the wire
 ([`CreateNewWire`](Self::CreateNewWire)), pins the near end to the device, and starts the
 far end extending toward the latched target
 ([`WireEnd::SetExtend`](equipment::wire_end::WireEnd::SetExtend)).

associated_functions.name: CreateNewWire
associated_functions.doc: Spawns a new wire at `spawn_pos` and returns it through `result`.

associated_functions.name: RetractActiveWire
associated_functions.doc:
Retracts the active wire: destroys its physics constraint, detaches the near end, and
 notifies the HUD.

associated_functions.name: IsHookAimingState
associated_functions.doc:
Whether the hook is in its "aiming" state: an active wire that is not reeling in and not a
 custom wire; with the re-reel upgrade, reeling in also counts.

associated_functions.name: ShouldShowAttachedUI
associated_functions.doc:
Whether the HUD shows the attached-wire part of the grapple reticle: an active, attached
 wire while the hook is not in [`GHS_REELING_IN`](GrapplingHookState::GHS_REELING_IN),
 [`GHS_REELED_ATTACHED`](GrapplingHookState::GHS_REELED_ATTACHED),
 [`GHS_REELED_HANG`](GrapplingHookState::GHS_REELED_HANG), or
 [`GHS_REELED_UPSIDEDOWN`](GrapplingHookState::GHS_REELED_UPSIDEDOWN).

associated_functions.name: GetActiveWireAttachmentGraphicsWorldPosition
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the interpolated graphics world position of the active wire's attached far end for
 the render interpolation factor `dtf`. Returns false without an attached active wire.

associated_functions.name: PushWireDataToUI
associated_functions.doc: Pushes the wires' tension and attach-type data to the HUD (`CHUDUI::UpdateWireData`).

kind.doc:
The grappling hook's high-level state machine (`CGrapplingHook::m_State`). `SetState` is the
 mutator; the reel tasks (`NStateTask_ReelIn`) and the reeled-in controller
 (`NReeledInController`) drive the transitions. A reel-to-target starts in
 [`GHS_REELING_IN`](Self::GHS_REELING_IN) -- during which
 `NReeledInController::RotateToGrappleTarget` rotates the character's root toward the target as
 the reel pulls them in -- and completes into one of the `GHS_REELED_*` attachment states
 depending on the landing surface and pose. `GHS_CUSTOM_ACTIVE_WIRE` is a wire held open outside
 the reel flow (tethers).

A single grapple wire (`CGrapplingHookWire`, a `CGameObject`): two `CWireEnd`s (near/device and
 far/hook), the physics constraint, and the wire rendering. Only referenced through
 [`GrapplingHook::m_ActiveWire`] here; the layout is unmapped.

The in-air grapple fire motion state task (`NStateTask_InAirGrappleFireMotionTask`). Like the
 other `NStateTask` functions, it runs against the character's state context.

associated_functions.name: OnEnter
associated_functions.doc:
Enters the task, orienting the fire motion from the camera matrix
 (`CGameCameraManager::GetCameraMatrix`, read directly rather than through the aim slot) and
 the latched target ([`GrapplingHook::GetLastGrappleTargetPos`]).

kind.doc: `CBulletWeaponBase`: the base of the fast-projectile weapons. Its layout is unmapped.

associated_functions.name: Fire_Projectile
associated_functions.doc:
The bullet weapons' [`WeaponBase::Fire_Projectile`] override: spawns the bullet projectile
 and then calls [`WeaponBase::Fire_ProjectileBase`]. It is the only caller of
 [`NWeaponUtil::Trajectory_GetAngleToHitPosition`].

associated_functions.name: GetTuning
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the bullet weapon's tuning (`SBulletWeaponTunings`), which selects explosive and
 water behaviour for its projectiles.

kind.doc:
One muzzle fire point of a weapon model (`CWeaponData::SInternalFireInformation`): the muzzle
 transform relative to the weapon, the muzzle-flash effect bound to it, and the time since it
 last fired.

fields.name: m_Position
fields.doc:
The fire point's transform in weapon space. The shot origin is this matrix composed with
 the weapon's world matrix.

fields.name: m_FireEffect
fields.doc: The attached fire effect played at this fire point.

fields.name: m_TimeSinceLastFire
fields.doc: Seconds since this fire point last fired; reset to zero when the fire point is used.

kind.doc: The weapon ballistics helpers (`NWeaponUtil`).

associated_functions.name: Trajectory_GetAngleToHitPosition
associated_functions.doc:
Solves the launch pitch that carries a projectile of speed `velocity` from `start_pos` to
 `end_pos` under `gravity_factor` times world gravity, writing the high and low solutions.
 Returns whether a solution exists. Only the bullet weapons' fire path calls it.

associated_functions.name: Trajectory_GetVelocityToHitPosition
associated_functions.doc:
Solves the launch velocity that carries a projectile from `start_pos` to `end_pos` in
 `time` seconds under `gravity_factor` times world gravity.

kind.doc:
How a weapon orients its projectiles (`CWeaponBase::EProjectileFireDirectionMode`), read by
 [`WeaponBase::GetShotMatrix`] from [`WeaponBase::m_ProjectileTempFireDirection`], falling back to
 [`WeaponBase::m_ProjectileFireDirection`] while the temporary mode is unset.

variants.name: E_PROJECTILE_FIRE_DIRECTION_UNSET
variants.doc: No mode set; the reader falls back to the other mode field.

variants.name: E_PROJECTILE_FIRE_DIRECTION_AIM_POS
variants.doc: Fire from the muzzle toward the weapon's aim target.

variants.name: E_PROJECTILE_FIRE_DIRECTION_BARREL
variants.doc: Fire along the weapon's own barrel, ignoring the aim target.

kind.doc: `CSniperWeapon`: a precision-aim rifle. Its layout is unmapped.

associated_functions.name: SetAimMode
associated_functions.doc:
The [`WeaponBase::SetAimMode`] override: in [`AIM_PRECISION`](AimMode::AIM_PRECISION) it
 shows the HUD sniper overlay and hides the holder, and in
 [`AIM_NORMAL`](AimMode::AIM_NORMAL) it reverses both.

kind.doc:
`CTurretWeaponComponent`: a weapon component that rotates a turret toward its weapon's target.
 Its layout is unmapped.

associated_functions.name: UpdateTurretAiming
associated_functions.doc:
The per-tick turret update, called from the component's pre-simulation update: selects the
 turret's target (faction and heat checks, characters, vehicles, and rigid objects) and
 rotates the turret toward the owning weapon's aim target at a rate-limited speed, so the
 barrel lags the aim point.

kind.doc:
The animation-graph condition `C_IS_TRYING_TO_FIRE` (`CWeapoIsTryingToFireCondition`, the name
 is misspelt in the game). Its layout is unmapped.

associated_functions.name: Evaluate
associated_functions.doc:
Evaluates the condition for the character owning `instance` (a
 `NAnimationSystem::CStateMachineInstance`). True when the character holds a selected weapon
 in a wielding, dual-wielding, or mounted state (or is planting an explosive) and a fire input
 is present that the animation allows: the fire input with shooting allowed, the
 precision-aim input with precision aim possible and allowed, or the plant input while
 planting.

kind.doc:
The base class of every weapon (`CWeaponBase`, a `CPhysicsGameObject`): fire input and timing,
 ammunition, recoil, heat, aim target, tuning, and the list of physical guns
 ([`WeaponData`]) it drives. The weapon embeds a `CGameObject` subobject after its vtable
 pointer.

fields.name: m_IsFirstShot
fields.doc:
Whether the current shot is the first of a trigger pull; first shots use the tuning's
 first-shot recoil scale.

fields.name: m_IsFiring
fields.doc: Whether the weapon is firing.

fields.name: m_IsTryingToFire
fields.doc:
Whether the fire input currently requests a shot, after trigger sensitivity, semi-automatic
 gating, and forced fire.

fields.name: m_IsTriggerPulled
fields.doc: Whether the trigger input is past the tuning's pull threshold (with hysteresis once pulled).

fields.name: m_IsFiringCancelled
fields.doc: Whether firing is cancelled until the trigger is released.

fields.name: m_IsFeatheringTrigger
fields.doc: Whether the trigger input is above zero.

fields.name: m_FiredThisInput
fields.doc:
Whether the current trigger pull has already fired; semi-automatic weapons fire once per
 pull.

fields.name: m_NextWeaponToFire
fields.doc:
The index into [`m_lWeaponData`](Self::m_lWeaponData) of the gun that fires next, which
 [`GetFireFromPositionBase`](Self::GetFireFromPositionBase) reads to pick the muzzle. The
 tail of [`Fire_ProjectileBase`](Self::Fire_ProjectileBase) (`MarkNextWeaponComponentForFire`,
 inlined in this build) advances it modulo the gun count after each shot.

fields.name: m_LastWeaponToFire
fields.doc:
The index of the gun that fired last, recorded before
 [`m_NextWeaponToFire`](Self::m_NextWeaponToFire) advances.

fields.name: m_NoHeatOnFiring
fields.doc: Whether firing this weapon adds no heat (wanted level) to the user.

fields.name: m_ProjectileFireDirection
fields.doc: The weapon's persistent projectile direction mode.

fields.name: m_ProjectileTempFireDirection
m_ForceFireTimer
fields.doc: Seconds of forced fire remaining; the weapon fires regardless of input while positive.

fields.name: m_ForceFireCount
fields.doc:
Shots of forced fire remaining; decremented once per
 [`Fire_ProjectileBase`](Self::Fire_ProjectileBase) call.

fields.name: m_InputBufferTimer
fields.doc:
Seconds a blocked trigger pull stays buffered. A pull blocked by wall penetration or by the
 aim-angle check sets it to [`INPUT_BUFFER_TIME`](Self::INPUT_BUFFER_TIME), so the shot fires
 if the block clears within that window; a shot resets it to zero.

fields.name: m_TimeSinceLastFire
fields.doc: Seconds since the weapon last fired.

fields.name: m_ProjectileOffsetFromAimPos
fields.doc:
The radius of the spread ring [`GetShotMatrix`](Self::GetShotMatrix) offsets the aim point
 by, while [`m_ProjectileOffsetFireCount`](Self::m_ProjectileOffsetFireCount) shots remain.

fields.name: m_ProjectileOffsetFireCount
fields.doc: Shots remaining that use the spread ring; decremented once per shot.

fields.name: m_CurrentScatterValue
fields.doc:
The accumulated scatter, raised by each shot up to the tuning's maximum and scaling the
 shot's scatter rotation.

fields.name: m_CurrentRecoilPitchValueToRecover
fields.doc: The recoil pitch still to be recovered, raised by each shot.

fields.name: m_PhysicalRecoilStrength
fields.doc:
The physical recoil impulse strength; a non-zero value defers a physical recoil after each
 shot.

fields.name: m_RecoilYaw
fields.doc: The accumulated recoil yaw, kicked left or right at random by each shot.

fields.name: m_RecoilPitch
fields.doc: The accumulated recoil pitch, raised by each shot.

fields.name: m_CanBeOverheated
fields.doc: Whether the weapon overheats.

fields.name: m_IsOverheated
fields.doc: Whether the weapon is overheated and cannot fire.

fields.name: m_CurrentHeatValue
fields.doc: The heat level in `[0, 1]`; each shot adds heat and reaching 1 overheats the weapon.

fields.name: m_AimingWeaponIsPossible
fields.doc: Whether the weapon can be aimed at all; `CCharacter::IsAimingWeaponPossible` requires it.

fields.name: m_AimTargetPosition
fields.doc:
The weapon's aim target in world space, written each tick by
 [`UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel`](Self::UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel) from the point the
 holder passes in. [`GetShotMatrix`](Self::GetShotMatrix) aims every fire point of the
 weapon at it.

fields.name: m_IsAutoAimInPrecisionAimEnabled
fields.doc:
Whether aim assist stays on in precision aim. `CPlayer::SetAimMode` leaves the aim
 control's aim type untouched when entering precision aim with a weapon that sets this.

fields.name: m_EquipSlot
fields.doc: The inventory slot the weapon is equipped in.

fields.name: m_State
fields.doc: The weapon's state.

fields.name: m_IsPrecisionAimDisabled
fields.doc:
Whether precision aim is disabled for this weapon; the player's aim-input handling zeroes
 the aim timer while it is set.

fields.name: m_RequiresPreSimUpdates
fields.doc:
Whether the weapon is registered for pre-simulation updates; the fire path sets it and
 registers the weapon when a deferred action is queued.

fields.name: m_Tuning
fields.doc: The weapon type's tuning, or null.

fields.name: m_User
fields.doc:
The character using the weapon (a `boost::weak_ptr<CCharacter>`: object pointer and weak
 control block).

fields.name: m_IsWeaponPenetratingWallIfInAim
fields.doc: Whether the weapon blocks firing while its barrel penetrates a wall in aim.

fields.name: m_IsWeaponPenetratingCharacterIfInAim
fields.doc:
Whether the weapon's barrel penetrates a character in aim;
 [`GetShotMatrix`](Self::GetShotMatrix) skips the near-muzzle barrel fallback while set.

fields.name: m_IsLeanOverFirePossible
fields.doc:
Whether the holder can lean over an obstruction to fire, which lifts the wall-penetration
 block.

fields.name: m_lWeaponData
fields.doc: The weapon's physical guns, one [`WeaponData`] per gun.

associated_functions.name: GetGripPosition
associated_functions.doc: Writes the grip transform for the given `hand` (a `E_WEAPON_GRIP_HAND_*` value).

associated_functions.name: GetShotMatrix
associated_functions.doc:
Builds the launch transform for a shot from `weapon_data` into `shot_matrix`. The origin is
 the muzzle ([`GetFireFromPosition`](Self::GetFireFromPosition)); the direction points at
 [`m_AimTargetPosition`](Self::m_AimTargetPosition) (for a remote player, the network
 component's aim point). It falls back to 10 m along the barrel when the aim point is within
 about 0.3 m of the muzzle, in barrel fire-direction mode, or with `force_barrel_direction`.
 While projectile-offset shots remain it offsets the aim point by
 [`m_ProjectileOffsetFromAimPos`](Self::m_ProjectileOffsetFromAimPos) on a random ring, and
 it layers the scatter rotation on top unless `ignore_scatter`.

associated_functions.name: GetFireFromPositionBase
associated_functions.doc: The base implementation of the [`GetFireFromPosition`](Self::GetFireFromPosition) virtual.

associated_functions.name: Fire_ProjectileBase
associated_functions.doc:
The base implementation of the [`Fire_Projectile`](Self::Fire_Projectile) virtual: consumes
 ammunition, resets the fire timers, applies recoil, scatter, and heat, plays the fire effect
 on `weapon_data`, decrements the forced-fire and projectile-offset counts, and then advances
 the fire-point cursor of the gun at [`m_NextWeaponToFire`](Self::m_NextWeaponToFire) and the
 gun index itself.

associated_functions.name: IsWeaponAimingBase
associated_functions.doc: The base implementation of the [`IsWeaponAiming`](Self::IsWeaponAiming) virtual.

associated_functions.name: UpdateFromUserPostSim_ParallelBase
associated_functions.doc:
The base implementation of the
 [`UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel`](Self::UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel) virtual.

associated_functions.name: UpdateWeapon_Parallel
associated_functions.doc:
The per-gun fire-input update: cools heat, reads the trigger against the tuning's
 sensitivities, applies semi-automatic, forced-fire, wall-penetration, and aim-angle gating,
 and starts or stops fire on `weapon_data`.

associated_functions.name: GetAimTimerOverride
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the tuning's aim-timer override
 ([`WeaponTuning::m_aim_timer_override`]), or zero without tuning.

associated_functions.name: GetMagazineSize
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the tuning's magazine size ([`WeaponTuning::m_magazine_size`]), or zero without
 tuning.

associated_functions.name: ChangeBoneAttachement
associated_functions.doc:
Sets every weapon-state attach bone of gun `weapon_index` to `bone` (an
 `NBone::ESafeBoneIndex`).

associated_functions.name: GetCurrentBoneAttachement
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the attach bone of gun `weapon_index` for the weapon's current
 [`m_State`](Self::m_State), or an invalid-bone value when the index is out of range.

associated_functions.name: GetTransform
associated_functions.doc:
The `CGameObject::GetTransform` override: copies the first gun's
 [`WeaponData::GetWorldMatrixT1`] into `transform`. `game_object` is the weapon's
 `CGameObject` subobject, not the start of the weapon.

associated_functions.name: UpdateRender
associated_functions.doc:
The render-phase `CGameObject::UpdateRender` override. For each gun it interpolates
 [`WeaponData::m_WorldMatrixT0`] toward [`WeaponData::m_WorldMatrixT1`] by the render
 context's interpolation factor, applies the holstered scale when holstered, pushes the
 result to [`WeaponData::m_BaseModelInstance`], and updates the gun's animated-model
 skinning; it then renders the weapon's components. `game_object` is the weapon's
 `CGameObject` subobject, not the start of the weapon.

functions.name: GetFireFromPosition
functions.doc:
Writes the muzzle position for `weapon_data`: the gun's world matrix composed with its
 current fire point ([`WeaponData::m_InternalFirePositionCurrentIndex`]). The base
 implementation is [`GetFireFromPositionBase`](Self::GetFireFromPositionBase).

functions.name: Fire_Projectile
functions.doc:
Fires one shot from `weapon_data`. The base implementation is
 [`Fire_ProjectileBase`](Self::Fire_ProjectileBase); subclasses such as
 `CBulletWeaponBase` spawn their projectile and then call it.

functions.name: ConsumeAmmo
functions.doc: Deducts `count` rounds of ammunition for `weapon_data`.

functions.name: IsWeaponAiming
functions.doc:
Whether the weapon is being aimed: the base implementation
 ([`IsWeaponAimingBase`](Self::IsWeaponAimingBase)) returns
 [`m_IsTryingToFire`](Self::m_IsTryingToFire) or
 [`m_IsFeatheringTrigger`](Self::m_IsFeatheringTrigger). The character's aim-input
 handling refills its aim timer while this holds.

functions.name: SetAimMode
functions.doc:
Applies the holder's aim mode: normal or precision aim. `CPlayer::SetAimMode` calls it
 after changing the player's aim mode.

functions.name: UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel
functions.doc:
The per-tick weapon update from its user after simulation: validates `aim_position` and
 stores it as [`m_AimTargetPosition`](Self::m_AimTargetPosition), then processes the
 fire inputs. The base implementation is
 [`UpdateFromUserPostSim_ParallelBase`](Self::UpdateFromUserPostSim_ParallelBase).

functions.name: GetTuningBase
functions.doc:
Returns the weapon type's tuning block (`SWeaponTuningBase`), from which the fire code
 reads recoil, scatter, and spread ranges.

kind.doc:
The seconds a blocked trigger pull stays buffered in
 [`m_InputBufferTimer`](Self::m_InputBufferTimer).

fields.name: GetFireFromPosition
fields.doc:
Writes the muzzle position for `weapon_data`: the gun's world matrix composed with its
 current fire point ([`WeaponData::m_InternalFirePositionCurrentIndex`]). The base
 implementation is [`GetFireFromPositionBase`](Self::GetFireFromPositionBase).

fields.name: Fire_Projectile
fields.doc:
Fires one shot from `weapon_data`. The base implementation is
 [`Fire_ProjectileBase`](Self::Fire_ProjectileBase); subclasses such as
 `CBulletWeaponBase` spawn their projectile and then call it.

fields.name: ConsumeAmmo
fields.doc: Deducts `count` rounds of ammunition for `weapon_data`.

fields.name: IsWeaponAiming
fields.doc:
Whether the weapon is being aimed: the base implementation
 ([`IsWeaponAimingBase`](Self::IsWeaponAimingBase)) returns
 [`m_IsTryingToFire`](Self::m_IsTryingToFire) or
 [`m_IsFeatheringTrigger`](Self::m_IsFeatheringTrigger). The character's aim-input
 handling refills its aim timer while this holds.

fields.name: SetAimMode
fields.doc:
Applies the holder's aim mode: normal or precision aim. `CPlayer::SetAimMode` calls it
 after changing the player's aim mode.

fields.name: UpdateFromUserPostSim_Parallel
fields.doc:
The per-tick weapon update from its user after simulation: validates `aim_position` and
 stores it as [`m_AimTargetPosition`](Self::m_AimTargetPosition), then processes the
 fire inputs. The base implementation is
 [`UpdateFromUserPostSim_ParallelBase`](Self::UpdateFromUserPostSim_ParallelBase).

fields.name: GetTuningBase
fields.doc:
Returns the weapon type's tuning block (`SWeaponTuningBase`), from which the fire code
 reads recoil, scatter, and spread ranges.

kind.doc:
One physical gun of a weapon (`CWeaponData`, a `CCombinedAttachedEffectContainer`): its model,
 attach bones, muzzle fire points, cached world matrices, and fire effects. A weapon holds one per
 gun in [`WeaponBase::m_lWeaponData`]; a dual-wield weapon holds two.

fields.name: m_Owner
fields.doc: The weapon this gun belongs to.

fields.name: m_lBoneAttachementPerWeaponState
fields.doc:
The attach bone (an `NBone::ESafeBoneIndex`) this gun rides for each [`WeaponState`],
 indexed by [`WeaponBase::m_State`].

fields.name: m_InternalFirePositions
fields.doc: The gun's muzzle fire points, one per barrel.

fields.name: m_InternalFirePositionCurrentIndex
fields.doc:
The fire-point cursor: the index into
 [`m_InternalFirePositions`](Self::m_InternalFirePositions) that
 [`WeaponBase::GetFireFromPosition`] uses as the muzzle. The tail of
 [`WeaponBase::Fire_Projectile`] advances it modulo the fire-point count after each shot.

fields.name: m_AnimatedModel
fields.doc: The gun's animated model, when it has one; its skinning is updated in the render phase.

fields.name: m_BaseModelInstance
fields.doc:
The gun's base model instance (an `NModelSystem::CModelInstance`). The render update pushes
 the interpolated world matrix to it.

fields.name: m_WorldMatrixT0
fields.doc: The gun's world matrix as of the previous simulation tick.

fields.name: m_WorldMatrixT1
fields.doc:
The gun's world matrix as of the current simulation tick, refreshed from the attach bone by
 the model-instance attachment update. Sim-side readers such as the fire origin read it
 through [`GetWorldMatrixT1`](Self::GetWorldMatrixT1); the render update interpolates from
 [`m_WorldMatrixT0`](Self::m_WorldMatrixT0) toward it.

fields.name: m_TimeSinceLastFire
fields.doc: Seconds since this gun last fired; reset by [`WeaponBase::Fire_Projectile`].

fields.name: m_HolsteredScaleValue
fields.doc: The uniform scale applied to the gun's world matrix while holstered.

fields.name: m_IsLeadingWeaponFire
fields.doc:
Whether this gun leads a multi-gun first shot: [`WeaponBase::Fire_Projectile`] clears it on
 every gun and sets it on the firing one.

associated_functions.name: GetWorldMatrixT1
associated_functions.doc:
Returns [`m_WorldMatrixT1`](Self::m_WorldMatrixT1), scaled by
 [`m_HolsteredScaleValue`](Self::m_HolsteredScaleValue) when the owning weapon is
 [`E_WS_HOLSTERED`](WeaponState::E_WS_HOLSTERED). The result is written through `result`
 and returned.

kind.doc:
The weapon's list of [`WeaponData`] entries (an engine `TArray<CWeaponData*>`): begin, end, and
 capacity-end pointers followed by a user-allocated flag.

fields.name: m_Begin
fields.doc: The first entry.

fields.name: m_End
fields.doc: One past the last live entry.

fields.name: m_Last
fields.doc: One past the allocated capacity.

kind.doc:
The situation a weapon is in (`CWeaponData::EWeaponState`), stored on the weapon as
 [`WeaponBase::m_State`]. It selects the weapon's attach bone
 ([`WeaponData::m_lBoneAttachementPerWeaponState`] is indexed by it) and, when holstered, the
 holstered scale applied to the weapon's world matrix.

variants.name: E_WS_HOLSTERED
variants.doc:
Holstered on the body. `CWeaponData::GetWorldMatrixT1` and the render update scale the
 weapon's matrix by [`WeaponData::m_HolsteredScaleValue`] in this state.

variants.name: E_WS_NUM
variants.doc:
The number of weapon states, and so the length of
 [`WeaponData::m_lBoneAttachementPerWeaponState`].

kind.doc:
A weapon's tuning record (`SWeaponTuning`), an ADF resource shared by every instance of a weapon
 type and reached through [`WeaponBase::m_Tuning`]. Only the fields read by the mapped functions
 are bound.

fields.name: m_magazine_size
fields.doc: The magazine capacity. Negative means the weapon has no magazine limit.

fields.name: m_max_range
fields.doc:
The weapon's maximum aim range in metres. The player's aim control takes the largest of
 these over the wielded, wingsuit, and vehicle weapons as the weapon slot's maximum aim
 distance.

fields.name: m_aim_timer_override
fields.doc:
A per-weapon replacement for the character's aim-timer refill value; non-negative values
 override the character's aim settings (see [`WeaponBase::GetAimTimerOverride`]).

kind.doc:
A latched grapple target (`CWireEnd::SHookTargetInfo`): the target position, plus the target or
 game object it is relative to and the position in that object's space. The hook fills it from the aim state when it fires, and the wire end flies to and attaches at it.

fields.name: m_HomingHookTarget
fields.doc: The target the hook homes on, or null for a target-less (surface) latch.

fields.name: m_TargetPosition
fields.doc:
The world-space target position at the time it was latched.
 `CGrapplingHook::SetUpTarget` writes the aim slot's position here.

fields.name: m_WasInRange
fields.doc: Whether the aim slot was in range when the target was latched.

fields.name: m_TargetGameObject
fields.doc:
The target game object (a `boost::weak_ptr<CGameObject>`: object pointer and weak control
 block), or null.

associated_functions.name: SetupTargetFromTarget
associated_functions.doc: Latches `target` with `local_position` in the target's game-object space.

associated_functions.name: SetupTargetFromGameObject
associated_functions.doc: Latches the game object `game_object` (a `CGameObject`) with `local_position` in its space.

associated_functions.name: GetTargetWorldPosition
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the latched target's current world position, following the target object when there
 is one.

kind.doc:
One end of a grapple wire (`CWireEnd`). A `CGrapplingHookWire` holds two: the near end at the
 device and the far end at the hook. An end extends toward a latched [`HookTargetInfo`], then
 attaches to a proxy (`CGrapplePointProxy`), not to a bare coordinate. The layout is unmapped.

associated_functions.name: SetExtend
associated_functions.doc:
Puts the end into its extending state: it flies from `start_pos` at `speed` toward
 `target_info`, as a ghost wire when `ghost_wire`.

associated_functions.name: Attach
associated_functions.doc:
Attaches the end at `hit_pos`: builds the attachment proxy from the ray hit `cast_info` (a
 `CCastRayInfo`) with `SetupProxyForAttachment` and moves the end to its attached state.

associated_functions.name: AttachToProxy
associated_functions.doc: Attaches the end to an existing attachment proxy (a `CGrapplePointProxy`).

associated_functions.name: AttachToCharacterBone
associated_functions.doc:
Attaches the end to bone `bone` of `character` at `local_offset`, through a new
 `CCharacterBoneAttachedPointProxy`.

fields.name: m_InterpolationMethod
fields.doc:
The frame-pacing method [`Update`](Self::Update) uses this frame, rechosen every frame:
 [`INTERPOLATION_METHOD_ACCUMULATED`](Self::INTERPOLATION_METHOD_ACCUMULATED) while a cutscene
 plays, [`INTERPOLATION_METHOD_SINGLE_STEP`](Self::INTERPOLATION_METHOD_SINGLE_STEP) otherwise,
 or [`m_InterpolationOverride`](Self::m_InterpolationOverride) when that is non-negative.

fields.name: m_PrevInterpolationMethod
fields.doc:
The method used on the previous frame; a change resets the accumulators. Set to
 [`INTERPOLATION_METHOD_PAUSED`](Self::INTERPOLATION_METHOD_PAUSED) when the frame takes the
 paused path.

fields.name: m_InterpolationOverride
fields.doc:
A console override for [`m_InterpolationMethod`](Self::m_InterpolationMethod);
 [`INTERPOLATION_OVERRIDE_NONE`](Self::INTERPOLATION_OVERRIDE_NONE) when unset.

fields.name: m_UpdateFlags
fields.doc:
The [`GameUpdateFlags`] bit set gating the phases of [`Update`](Self::Update): the sim
 step, the render-bookkeeping step, and the tools step.

associated_functions.name: Destructor
associated_functions.doc:
`CGame::~CGame`: tears down the message-box manager, the game resource cache and handler,
 the profiler utility, and the version display.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc: The top-level per-frame update: advances the sim and drives rendering. Returns false on exit.

associated_functions.name: UpdateRender
associated_functions.doc: Builds the per-frame update contexts and drives rendering.

associated_functions.name: UpdateGame
associated_functions.doc:
One sim tick: advances the game clock, updates the FPS counter, and dispatches to the
 active game state's update (install, init, frontend, load, or run). Called zero or more
 times per [`Update`](Self::Update) according to the frame-pacing mode.

kind.doc:
The [`m_InterpolationMethod`](Self::m_InterpolationMethod) chosen while a cutscene plays:
 the same accumulator, but [`UpdateGame`](Self::UpdateGame) runs once per whole step
 accumulated (capped), subtracting one per update.

The [`m_PrevInterpolationMethod`](Self::m_PrevInterpolationMethod) value written when the
 frame takes the paused path; it matches no method, so the next unpaused frame resets the
 accumulators.

The [`m_InterpolationMethod`](Self::m_InterpolationMethod) chosen during gameplay: the
 fractional sim step accumulates in `m_RunningFrameFraction` and [`UpdateGame`](Self::UpdateGame)
 runs at most once per render frame. The method names are descriptive; the engine uses bare
 integers.

The [`m_InterpolationMethod`](Self::m_InterpolationMethod) that derives the number of sim
 steps from `QueryPerformanceCounter` wall-clock time since the method was entered, running
 several [`UpdateGame`](Self::UpdateGame) calls per frame when rendering falls behind. Only
 reachable through [`m_InterpolationOverride`](Self::m_InterpolationOverride).

The [`m_InterpolationOverride`](Self::m_InterpolationOverride) value meaning no override:
 the method chosen each frame stands.

The intra-`Update` site at which the game's per-frame render bookkeeping starts: the
 [`E_GUF_RENDER`](GameUpdateFlags::E_GUF_RENDER) check (the `jz`) that normally gates `UpdateRender` (and everything
 after it) on the frame-pacing mode sits here.

The intra-`Update` site at which the render bookkeeping ends: `++m_RenderCount`, the last
 step of the `UpdateRender` tail.
`CGameStateRun`: the in-game state's static update functions.

associated_functions.name: UpdateRenderPaused
associated_functions.doc:
The render-side update the run state performs while the game is paused: drives the
 landscape, UI prerender, video, water simulation, and resource streaming, and waits for the
 CPU draw, without running the camera update.

kind.doc:
`CGame::EGameUpdateFlags`: the phases of [`Game::Update`] enabled by
 [`Game::m_UpdateFlags`].

flags.name: E_GUF_TOOLS
flags.doc: Runs the tools hooks at the end of the frame.

flags.name: E_GUF_UPDATE
flags.doc: Runs the sim step: the frame-pacing switch that calls [`Game::UpdateGame`].

flags.name: E_GUF_RENDER
flags.doc: Runs [`Game::UpdateRender`] after the sim step.

kind.doc:
The game world interface (`IGameWorld`), reached through the `Base::CSingle<IGameWorld>`
 instance pointer. The concrete object is `CGameWorld`, which owns the object manager, the
 world file, and the player-teleport state machine; the interface subobject is what every
 caller (bookmarks, teleport triggers, mission starts) goes through. Only the vtable is mapped.

associated_functions.name: TeleportPlayerImpl
associated_functions.doc:
`CGameWorld::TeleportPlayer`, the implementation behind the
 [`TeleportPlayer`](Self::TeleportPlayer) virtual: copies the request into
 the world's teleport state and arms the `TELEPORT_*` state machine
 [`UpdateTeleport`] services; starts the overlay fade-to-black when `use_fade` is set and
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE) is clear.

associated_functions.name: TeleportPlayerInstantImpl
associated_functions.doc:
`CGameWorld::TeleportPlayerInstant`, the implementation behind the
 [`TeleportPlayerInstant`](Self::TeleportPlayerInstant) virtual. Writes the
 character's transform through its world-transform virtual, calls
 `CCharacter::ForceNeutralState`, sets the character's teleported flag bit, and resets the
 camera through [`GameCameraManager::ResetCamera`](camera::game_camera_manager::GameCameraManager::ResetCamera),
 bracketed by the `game_teleporting_initiated` and `game_teleporting_completed` posted
 events.

associated_functions.name: IsTeleportingImpl
associated_functions.doc:
`CGameWorld::IsTeleporting`, the implementation behind the
 [`IsTeleporting`](Self::IsTeleporting) virtual: whether the teleport state
 machine is not idle.

functions.name: TeleportPlayer
functions.doc:
Queues a deferred player teleport that `CGameWorld::UpdateTeleport` services over the
 following frames through its `TELEPORT_*` state machine. `world` is the destination
 transform (the translation row places the character; the rotation sets the facing and
 resets the camera behind it). `state` is an optional character state to enter on
 arrival (null keeps the neutral state). With `use_load_state` the game enters the load
 game state so the destination streams in first, with a load screen if
 `use_load_screen`; without it the world must already be resident (the engine logs a
 warning past 500 m from the active camera). `use_fade` fades the overlay UI to black for
 `fade_out_time` seconds and back in over `fade_in_time`. `flags` is a bit set of
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION) and
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE). `teleport_done_event`, when
 non-null, is sent once the arrival completes. Asserts when a teleport is already in
 flight ([`IsTeleporting`](Self::IsTeleporting)). Main thread only.

functions.name: TeleportPlayerInstant
functions.doc:
Teleports the local player's character synchronously: initializes the character's
 transform to `world`, forces the neutral animation state, optionally enters `state`,
 resets the game camera behind the new transform, and re-enables the player and
 character. Fires `game_teleporting_initiated` and `game_teleporting_completed`, resets
 the current settlement, province, and region, and notifies the HUD. Aborts the active
 mission unless `flags` has
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION). No streaming: the
 destination must already be resident. Asserts when a deferred teleport is in flight.
 Main thread only.

functions.name: IsTeleporting
functions.doc: Whether a deferred [`TeleportPlayer`](Self::TeleportPlayer) is still being serviced.

kind.doc:
A teleport `flags` bit: keep the active mission running across the teleport.
 Without it the mission manager aborts the active mission as part of the teleport.

A teleport `flags` bit that [`Teleport::Teleport`] adds when the teleport object's
 [`m_LeavePlayerDisabled`](TeleportFlags::m_LeavePlayerDisabled) flag is set. Its effect in
 the teleport has not been traced.

A teleport `flags` bit (deferred teleports only): skip the fade-to-black even
 when `use_fade` is set.

fields.name: TeleportPlayer
fields.doc:
Queues a deferred player teleport that `CGameWorld::UpdateTeleport` services over the
 following frames through its `TELEPORT_*` state machine. `world` is the destination
 transform (the translation row places the character; the rotation sets the facing and
 resets the camera behind it). `state` is an optional character state to enter on
 arrival (null keeps the neutral state). With `use_load_state` the game enters the load
 game state so the destination streams in first, with a load screen if
 `use_load_screen`; without it the world must already be resident (the engine logs a
 warning past 500 m from the active camera). `use_fade` fades the overlay UI to black for
 `fade_out_time` seconds and back in over `fade_in_time`. `flags` is a bit set of
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_KEEP_MISSION) and
 [`TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE`](Self::TELEPORT_FLAG_NO_FADE). `teleport_done_event`, when
 non-null, is sent once the arrival completes. Asserts when a teleport is already in
 flight ([`IsTeleporting`](Self::IsTeleporting)). Main thread only.

fields.doc:
Teleports the local player's character synchronously: initializes the character's
 transform to `world`, forces the neutral animation state, optionally enters `state`,
 resets the game camera behind the new transform, and re-enables the player and
 character. Fires `game_teleporting_initiated` and `game_teleporting_completed`, resets
 the current settlement, province, and region, and notifies the HUD. Aborts the active
 mission unless `flags` has
