associated_functions.name: ApplySubsampleJitter
associated_functions.doc:
Post-multiplies the temporal sub-pixel jitter onto `proj`. Effective only when the resolve mode
 is [`AAMode::AA_SMAA_T2X`].

kind.doc:
The number of full-screen temporary textures in the post chain's slot ring
 (`s_FullscreenTempTextureCount`); effects advance the slot as
 `(slot + 1) % FULLSCREEN_TEMP_TEXTURE_COUNT`.

The slot-base the slot-returning effects' result textures live at in the manager's texture
 array: a stage's current result is `CTX[slot + RESULT_TEXTURE_SLOT_BASE]` (an entry of
 [`m_FullscreenLinearTempTexture`](Self::m_FullscreenLinearTempTexture)), where `CTX` is the
 manager argument the post block passes to the effect chain and `slot` is the effect's declared
 slot index.

The qword index of [`m_FullscreenSrgbTempTexture`](Self::m_FullscreenSrgbTempTexture) in the
 manager: the sRGB view of the slot's result is `CTX[slot + SRGB_RESULT_TEXTURE_SLOT_BASE]`.
 SMAA's edge detection and
 final blend read the current slot through it.

The render block for the post-effects pass. Its [`Draw`](Self::Draw) runs the
 HDR post chain in order: histogram generation, sun-halo pre-apply, blur (bokeh or plain), glare,
 depth of field, motion blur, the HDR-to-LDR tonemap, the player-damage vignette, anti-aliasing,
 sun halo, and the final fade.

 It threads a single result-texture slot index through the slot-returning effects
 ([`DepthOfFieldEffect`], [`MotionBlurEffect`], [`PlayerDamageEffect`], [`AntiAliasingEffect`]),
 moving between the
 [`FULLSCREEN_TEMP_TEXTURE_COUNT`](PostEffectsManager::FULLSCREEN_TEMP_TEXTURE_COUNT) full-screen
 temporary textures.

The sun halo. [`PreApply`](Self::PreApply) prepares it and sets the ready flag;
 [`Apply`](Self::Apply) composites it.

fields.name: m_Ready
fields.doc:
The ready flag: [`PreApply`](Self::PreApply) sets it when the halo is prepared, and
 [`Apply`](Self::Apply) early-outs when it is clear.

kind.doc:
The tone-mapping operator applied by the HDR-to-LDR composite in
 [`DepthOfFieldEffect::Apply`].

The stencil bits SMAA's edge detection writes and its blend pass tests (`g_EdgeStencilBitMask`,
 statically initialised in the module image).

Whether SMAA's edge-detection pass marks detected edges in the stencil buffer
 (`g_EnableEdgeStencil`, default set), so the blend pass runs only where the stencil matches.
The scale applied to [`jittered_samples`] (`g_JitterScaleFactor`).

The temporal anti-aliasing (SMAA T2X) sub-pixel jitter offsets in pixels, indexed by
 `[m_FrameIndex & 1][axis]` (`g_JitteredSamples`). [`AntiAliasingEffect::ApplySubsampleJitter`]
 scales them by [`jitter_scale_factor`] and divides by the target size.
The terrain detail render block *type* (`NGraphicsEngine::CTerrainRenderBlockDetail::CDetailRBType`).

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc: The type-level per-pass setup (the `IRenderBlockType::Setup` override).

kind.doc:
A 3x4 skinning-palette bone matrix. The layout differs per render block (empirically, by the
 block's vertex format/shader variant): some blocks store four 3-float columns with the
 translation in the final three floats, others three 4-float rows with the translation in each
 row's fourth element. The 3x3 rotation is orthonormal only under the correct reading. The skinning palette is an array of these, one per skeleton
 bone, built per frame by
 [`PoseProducer::MakeSkinningPalette`](animation::pose_producer::PoseProducer::MakeSkinningPalette).

The WaveWorks water render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CNvWaterHighEndRenderBlock`): the ocean
 surface at the higher water-quality settings, simulated and tessellated through NVIDIA WaveWorks
 (`gfsdk_waveworks.win64.dll`) rather than through the engine's own patch grid.

 Its block type registers itself as `"NvWaterHighEnd"` and owns the whole `NvWater*` shader family
 — `NvWaterShader_lod0[_tess]`, `NvWaterShader_lod1[_tess]`, `NvWaterBelow`,
 `NvWaterBelowShader_lod1`, `NvWaterLake`, and `NvWaterBox[_tess]` — selecting among them per draw
 from the tessellation cvar and the block's above/below-surface flag. It also owns the two
 constant buffers those permutations read: a 10-register buffer bound to **vertex and domain slot
 1** and a 15-register buffer bound to **fragment slot 1**.

fields.name: m_AltitudeSimulationPause
fields.doc:
When set, [`Draw`](Self::Draw) skips the ocean simulation step
 ([`WaveWorksSimulationStep`](WaveWorksSimulationStep)) and `UpdateSimulation` stops
 advancing [`m_RenderTime`](Self::m_RenderTime), freezing the simulated sea state. Driven by
 the camera's altitude above the water.

fields.name: m_UnderWater
fields.doc:
Whether the camera is below the ocean surface. [`Draw`](Self::Draw) selects the below-water
 vertex/fragment permutations when set, and [`Setup`](Self::Setup) stages the underwater
 tweak set (specular, transparency depth, refraction disturbance) instead of the above-water
 one.

fields.name: m_RenderTime
fields.doc:
The ocean simulation clock in seconds, advanced once per game frame by `UpdateSimulation`
 (`m_deltaTime * m_TimeScale` per step, skipped while
 [`m_AltitudeSimulationPause`](Self::m_AltitudeSimulationPause) is set). [`Draw`](Self::Draw)
 hands it to the simulation step as the simulation time, and [`Setup`](Self::Setup) bakes it
 into the vertex/domain constants as the shader time.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
Bakes the per-view WaveWorks matrices and stages both of the block type's constant buffers.

 The block keeps three 4x4 matrices of its own, all rebuilt here from the render context:
 - the WaveWorks **view** matrix, `Y/Z-swap · `[`RenderContext::m_View`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_View)
   (WaveWorks works in a Z-up frame, the engine in a Y-up one);
 - the WaveWorks **projection** matrix, a verbatim copy of
   [`RenderContext::m_ProjectionF`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_ProjectionF);
 - their product, the `g_ModelViewProjectionMatrix` the `NvWater*` vertex and domain shaders
   write clip position from.

 It then maps the vertex/domain constant buffer write-discard and writes that product into
 **registers 0..3**, followed by the top-down-camera offset/scale, wind direction, character
 world position, time, and Gerstner tuning through byte offset 148; and maps the fragment
 constant buffer, writing the WaveWorks view matrix into its registers 0..3 followed by the
 water colour, scattering, fog, and foam tuning. Neither buffer is written anywhere else, and
 [`Draw`](Self::Draw) restages nothing — it hands the same two block-held matrices straight to
 WaveWorks — so the whole family's view depends solely on the render context this call read.

 The body is selected by [`RenderContext::m_ActiveRenderPass`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_ActiveRenderPass):
 [`PRE_RP_WATER_CS_PRE`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_WATER_CS_PRE) only refreshes the block's cached camera info,
 [`PRE_RP_WATER_WAKES_PRE`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_WATER_WAKES_PRE) and
 [`PRE_RP_WATER_FOAM_PRE`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_WATER_FOAM_PRE) only set the blend state and the wake/foam viewport
 offsets, and every other pass takes the matrix-and-constant-buffer path described above.

 `sort_id` and `previous_sort_id` come from the draw-list walk in
 [`RenderPass::DoDraw`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderPass): the element's sort id, and
 `~0` on a block-type change. This override reads neither.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the WaveWorks ocean: the simulation step, the quadtree surface, the water-box surfaces,
 and the far LOD skirt.

 On the same three-way pass split as [`Setup`](Self::Setup), [`PRE_RP_WATER_CS_PRE`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_WATER_CS_PRE)
 runs the compute foam sub-pass and [`PRE_RP_WATER_FOAM_PRE`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_WATER_FOAM_PRE)
 the painted foam; every other pass takes
 the main body, which in order: advances the ocean simulation
 ([`WaveWorksSimulationStep`](WaveWorksSimulationStep)) unless the block's
 simulation-suppressed flag is set; binds the render context's render setup, the `NvWater*`
 program permutation for the current tessellation and above/below-surface state, and the water
 depth/stencil state; calls `GFSDK_WaveWorks_Simulation_SetRenderStateD3D11` and
 `GFSDK_WaveWorks_Quadtree_DrawD3D11` on the raw `ID3D11DeviceContext`, passing the two matrices
 [`Setup`](Self::Setup) baked as the view and projection the quadtree culls and picks LODs
 against; draws the registered water-box surfaces through `NWater::DrawWaterBoxSurface`; and
 restores the D3D state WaveWorks changed with `GFSDK_WaveWorks_Savestate_RestoreD3D11`. If the
 block's far-LOD flag is set it then draws the far skirt quad as a plain [`DrawIndexed`].

 The save and the restore of the WaveWorks savestate both happen inside this call, so no D3D
 state it captures outlives the call.

kind.doc:
The WaveWorks water render block *type*
 (`CNvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::CNvWaterHighEndRenderBlockType` singleton): the shared state
 behind every [`NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock`] draw — the `NvWater*` shader family, the two shared
 constant buffers, and the shared water textures
 [`Setup`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Setup)/[`Draw`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw) bind.

fields.name: m_TessellationOptions
fields.doc:
The tessellation option. It selects between the tessellated and untessellated shader
 permutations, and indexes the vertex-shader pair the draw binds.

fields.name: m_WaterModTexture
fields.doc:
The top-down water modulation texture, bound on vertex (or domain, when tessellating)
 slot 0 by [`Draw`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw).

fields.name: m_FoamTexture
fields.doc:
The foam detail texture, bound on fragment slot 5 by
 [`Setup`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Setup).

fields.name: m_WaterBumpTexture
fields.doc:
The water normal-detail (bump) texture, bound on fragment slot 4 by
 [`Setup`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Setup).

fields.name: m_DistantReflectionTexture
fields.doc:
The distant (backdrop) planar reflection texture. When
 `CWaterPatchManager::m_EnableScreenSpaceWaterReflection` is set,
 [`Draw`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw) re-binds fragment slot 2 to this in place of
 [`m_FullReflectionTexture`](Self::m_FullReflectionTexture).

fields.name: m_FullReflectionTexture
fields.doc:
The full planar reflection texture, bound on fragment slot 2 by
 [`Setup`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Setup).

kind.doc:
The per-draw render block instance info: the instance's constant buffers, LOD state, and world
 transforms.

associated_functions.name: GetMatrix
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the instance world transform for the given transform slot into `out` (also returned).
 The render blocks pass [`RenderContext::m_RenderFrameIndex`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderFrameIndex)
 as the slot for the current dispatch.

kind.doc:
The atmospheric-scattering / aerial-perspective render block. Its `Draw` reconstructs world
 position from depth via [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) -- for the whole
 screen, sky included -- and then ray-marches the sun shadow cascade and aerial perspective over
 the reconstructed positions.

fields.name: m_TowardsVector
fields.doc:
The direction toward the dominant celestial light (the sun, or the moon at night), fed to
 both the sky-lighting SH compute and the aerial-perspective fragment constants.

fields.name: m_HdrMultiplier
fields.doc: The HDR intensity multiplier applied to the scattering output.

fields.name: m_MinNightLuminance
fields.doc: The luminance floor applied at night.

fields.name: m_CloudCoverage
fields.doc: The cloud coverage factor fed to the sky-lighting SH compute.

fields.name: m_CloudAmbientColor
fields.doc: The cloud ambient colour fed to the sky-lighting SH compute.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the atmospheric-scattering pass. `rc` is the per-view render context; `info` the
 instance info. Reconstructs view rays from depth via
 [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) and samples the sun cascade.

kind.doc:
The tree-trunk/branch render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockBark`, registered name
 `"VegetationBark"`): the solid woody geometry of trees, as distinct from the leaf cards. Forward-lit
 vegetation.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the color-pass geometry. The clip transform is a CPU-baked world-view-projection staged
 on vertex `cb1` registers 0..3 via [`SetVertexProgramConstants`] before any draw-kind routing:
 `cb1[0..3] = M_model_camera_relative · m_OffsetViewProjection` for the non-instanced case, or
 `m_OffsetViewProjection` verbatim for the instanced/billboard cases (the per-instance model
 matrix is then applied in-shader). The global `m_VPGlobals` is bound at `cb0` for wind/time
 globals only, not the view-projection. One of three draw kinds is selected from the instance-data
 pointer in [`CRBIInfo`](RBIInfo): a non-instanced
 [`DrawIndexedWithBoundState`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedWithBoundState), a CPU-instanced
 [`DrawIndexedInstanced`] (per-instance stream at slot 2), or a GPU-indirect
 [`DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect)
 whose instance count lives in the type's `m_InstDrawParams` buffer. `m_RenderStatus` bits select
 bounce/GI, billboard, and geometry-program permutations.

 Besides the clip transform, `cb1` carries register 4 = the opacity/fade and UV parameters,
 registers 5..8 = the raw instance model matrix
 ([`RBIInfo::GetMatrix`] at
 [`m_RenderFrameIndex`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderFrameIndex)), and
 registers 9..12 = [`m_View`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_View). The draw
 kind is chosen from the instance data the `CRBIInfo` points at: with no instance data, a
 non-instanced draw; otherwise a CPU-instancing bit in its flags word selects the CPU-instanced
 draw when set and the GPU-indirect draw when clear.

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the depth-prepass and depth-and-velocity geometry. Same cb1-baked transform as
 [`Draw`](Self::Draw); the velocity pass
 ([`RP_Z_AND_VELOCITY_PASS`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_Z_AND_VELOCITY_PASS)) additionally bakes the previous frame's
 world-view-projection into `cb1` registers 5..8: `m_PreviousOffsetViewProjection` for the
 instanced kinds, or the instance's previous-frame matrix (at
 [`m_PreviousRenderFrameIndex`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_PreviousRenderFrameIndex))
 through `CRenderBlock::CalculateOffsetWorldViewProjectionMatrixPrev` for the non-instanced
 kind.

kind.doc: The bark render block *type* (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockBark::CRenderBlockBarkType`).

associated_functions.name: Create
associated_functions.doc: Creates the type's GPU resources ([`RenderBlockTypeBase::Create`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderBlockTypeBase::Create)).

associated_functions.name: SetupConstantBuffers
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the per-pass constant buffers (the `IRenderBlockType::SetupConstantBuffers` override): the global
 `m_VPGlobals`/`m_FPGlobals` at `cb0`, with the fragment `cb2` sized for the bark material
 constants on the colour pass.

kind.doc:
The skinned character render block (the [`Character`](character::character::Character) RBMDL block type). A character model is
 composed of one block per material; the same block objects are drawn for every pass, branching
 internally on [`RenderContext::m_RenderStatus`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderStatus)
 to select the shadow/depth-only path versus the full material path.

fields.name: m_SkinBatchesBegin
fields.doc: The `std::vector<CSkinBatch>` begin pointer.

fields.name: m_SkinBatchesEnd
fields.doc: The `std::vector<CSkinBatch>` end pointer.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The per-block setup (`IRenderBlock::Setup`). Binds the forward lighting resources through
 [`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources).

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the block for the current pass. Shadow passes (either
 [`RENDERSTATUS_SHADOWMAP`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderStatus::RENDERSTATUS_SHADOWMAP) bit of
 [`RenderContext::m_RenderStatus`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderStatus))
 take a depth-only path with the depth vertex shaders; other passes run the full material
 setup.

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc: Draws the block for the Z/velocity prepass.

associated_functions.name: SetMatrixPalette
associated_functions.doc:
Uploads one batch's bone matrices to the vertex-program palette constants: for each batch
 slot, copies `matrices[BatchToSkeletonLookup[slot]]` into the constant registers starting
 at `register`. Called from the block's internal `DrawBatches` before each batch's draw.

kind.doc:
The skinned character skin render block (the `CharacterSkin` RBMDL block type): the skin-shaded
 variant of [`RenderBlockCharacter`], with the same batch and pass structure.

fields.name: m_SkinBatchesBegin
fields.doc: The `std::vector<CSkinBatch>` begin pointer.

fields.name: m_SkinBatchesEnd
fields.doc: The `std::vector<CSkinBatch>` end pointer.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The per-block setup (`IRenderBlock::Setup`). Binds the forward lighting resources through
 [`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources).

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc: Draws the block for the current pass; see [`RenderBlockCharacter::Draw`].

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc: Draws the block for the Z/velocity prepass.

associated_functions.name: SetMatrixPalette
associated_functions.doc: See [`RenderBlockCharacter::SetMatrixPalette`].

kind.doc:
The deferred-lighting render block. Its `Draw` method dispatches either the clustered (tiled)
 lighting pass or a pass-through fallback.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Selects between the block's two lighting paths on a single condition:
 [`DrawPassThrough`](Self::DrawPassThrough) when
 [`RenderEngine::IsWireframeEnabled`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderEngine) reports
 wireframe, [`DrawClustered`](Self::DrawClustered) otherwise. Normal shaded rendering therefore
 always takes the clustered path.

associated_functions.name: DrawClustered
associated_functions.doc:
The clustered-lighting entry point: runs the "LightAssignment" pass (rasterizing light proxy
 geometry into the froxel light-lookup target) and the "ClusteredLighting" pass (shading from
 it). Called from `Draw` when wireframe is disabled.

associated_functions.name: DrawPassThrough
associated_functions.doc:
The wireframe-only lighting path, reached from [`Draw`](Self::Draw) exclusively when
 [`RenderEngine::IsWireframeEnabled`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderEngine) is set, so
 it does not run during normal shaded rendering. Like the clustered path it recovers a
 clip-to-view basis via [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4).

kind.doc:
The grass/foliage render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockFoliage`, registered name
 `"VegetationFoliage"`): forward-lit ground cover and small plants, drawn in `RP_VEGETATION_OPAQUE`.
 The bulk is grass drawn GPU-indirect.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the color-pass geometry. The clip transform is staged per draw on vertex `cb2`: register 0
 the camera-relative world matrix (from [`CRBIInfo`](RBIInfo)'s matrix, translation minus
 `m_CameraPosition`), registers 4..7 a per-draw copy of `m_OffsetViewProjection` (byte-identical to
 the global `cb0[29..32]`), so the vertex shader composes `clip = world · OffsetVP` from `cb2`
 rather than reading `cb0`. `SetupConstantBuffers` binds `cb0 = m_VPGlobals` but only for globals.
 One of three draw kinds is selected from the instance-data flags: a CPU-instanced
 [`DrawIndexedInstancedNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedInstancedNoMutex) (instance count a CPU `u16`), the dominant grass path
 [`DrawIndexedInstancedIndirectNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirectNoMutex) (instance count in the type's GPU-only `m_InstDrawParams` args
 buffer, populated by the vegetation draw-indirect compute pass), or a non-instanced
 [`DrawIndexedNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedNoMutex). The pass is forward-lit: the type's `Setup` binds the clustered-lighting
 constant buffer, the light-cluster index texture, GI, reflection, and sun-shadow-cascade
 resources to the fragment stage.

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the depth-prepass, shadow, velocity, and reflective-shadow geometry. Stages the same
 `cb2` transform as [`Draw`](Self::Draw) — register 0 the camera-relative world matrix, registers
 4..7 a copy of
 [`m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection)
 — plus the fade/detail scalars at registers 8..10; on the velocity pass
 ([`RP_Z_AND_VELOCITY_PASS`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_Z_AND_VELOCITY_PASS)) it
 additionally stages the previous frame's offset view-projection at registers 11..14, which the
 vertex shader differences against the current one to produce the motion vector. Selects between a
 CPU-instanced [`DrawIndexedInstancedNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedInstancedNoMutex),
 a GPU-indirect
 [`DrawIndexedInstancedIndirectNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirectNoMutex)
 fed by two vertex texture buffers, and a non-instanced
 [`DrawIndexedNoMutex`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawIndexedNoMutex), on the same instance-data flags [`Draw`](Self::Draw) routes on.

kind.doc:
The foliage render block *type* (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockFoliage::CRenderBlockFoliageType`).
 IDA labels its `Setup` as `CRenderBlockTypeWindow::Setup`; the vtable
 and body (the wind and interaction parameter upload) identify it.

associated_functions.name: SetupConstantBuffers
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the per-pass constant buffers (the `IRenderBlockType::SetupConstantBuffers` override): `m_VPGlobals` at vertex
 `cb0`, a vertex `cb2`, and `m_FPGlobals` at fragment `cb0`.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The type-level per-pass setup (the `IRenderBlockType::Setup` override): uploads the vertex wind and
 interaction parameters, selects the depth/shadow, reflective-shadow, or colour program
 permutations from `m_RenderStatus`, and for the forward-lit colour passes binds the forward
 lighting resources ([`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources)).

kind.doc:
The low-resolution particle compose block: blends the low-resolution particle buffer
 ([`m_SceneTexture`](Self::m_SceneTexture)) over the full-resolution scene with a premultiplied
 (`ONE`, `INV_SRC_ALPHA`) fullscreen draw, using the paired depth textures for the bilateral
 edge test. Drawn from the `RP_POSTEFFECTS` pass list ahead of the post-effects chain.

fields.name: m_SceneTexture
fields.doc:
The low-resolution buffer composited over the scene (fragment slot 0). Despite the name, it
 holds the low-resolution particle rendering, not the scene.

fields.name: m_LowResDepthTexture
fields.doc: The low-resolution depth texture (fragment slot 2).

fields.name: m_HighResDepthTexture
fields.doc: The full-resolution depth texture (fragment slot 1).

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the compose: binds the low-resolution colour and the two depths, enables
 premultiplied blending, and issues the fullscreen geometry.

kind.doc:
The light-glow render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockLightGlow`, registered name
 `"LightGlow"`): a screen-space sprite for a point/spot light corona, drawn in
 `CModelInstanceManager::HaloTransparentPass` (`RP_MODEL_HALO_POST`). The shape is a fixed
 billboard quad (`SLightGlowVertex`); placement is driven entirely on the CPU. The draw reads the
 light world position and colour/scale from [`CRBIInfo`](RBIInfo), projects it through the render
 context's translation-bearing view-projection, converts the result to pixel coordinates, and
 uploads the screen-space sprite corners and scale to vertex constant buffer `cb1` registers 0..4
 and 5 before issuing a non-instanced [`DrawIndexed`].

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the screen-space light-glow sprite. The block's own vertex shader applies the
 CPU-staged corners in `cb1` with no further transform, so the sprite position is fixed by the
 render context's camera at the moment of this draw.

kind.doc:
The occluder render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockOccluder`, registered name `"Occluder"`): a
 unit-cube depth proxy scaled per scene occluder, injected once per frame into
 [`RP_Z_OCCLUDERS`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_Z_OCCLUDERS) to prime the main camera depth buffer so later Z and G-buffer passes early-Z reject
 occluded geometry. Depth-only (null fragment program), and write-only: nothing reads the primed
 depth back on the CPU. The CPU software-occlusion system consumes the same occluder source data
 through its own path and is not fed by this GPU depth pass.

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the occluder-box depth geometry. The non-instanced path bakes
 `WVP = (world - camera_offset) · m_OffsetViewProjection` (via
 [`CalculateOffsetWorldViewProjectionMatrix`](graphics_engine::render_pass::CalculateOffsetWorldViewProjectionMatrix))
 into vertex `cb1`
 registers 0..3, register 4 a depth bias, then [`DrawIndexed`] per box. The instanced path
 (`gfx.occluders.use_instancing`) instead reads the global `m_VPGlobals` view-projection at `cb0`
 with per-instance world rows from a vertex stream and issues one [`DrawIndexedInstanced`].
 `Draw`/`Setup` tail-call this and its `SetupZ`.

kind.doc: The road-junction render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockRoadJunction`).

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The per-block setup (`IRenderBlock::Setup`). Binds the forward lighting resources through
 [`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources).

kind.doc:
The screen-space ambient-occlusion render block. Its `Draw` reconstructs view-space position from
 depth via [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) and carries a temporal history
 across frames, indexed by a counter the block advances per invocation.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the ambient-occlusion pass, reconstructing from depth and accumulating into the
 temporal history.

 One call runs five phases, each binding its own render setup, and they do not share a
 resolution: the [`SSAOPass`](graphics_engine::ssao::SSAOPass) sizes its depth targets at the
 render resolution scaled by `m_Resolution` and its occlusion and history targets at half that
 again, while the final composite goes to the full-resolution scene target.

 1. A linear-depth pack into the current slot of the depth targets, followed by a whole-texture
    mip generation over it (the targets carry five mip levels).
 2. The occlusion generation into the first of the two occlusion targets, reconstructing
    view-space position from the packed depth using the render context's own projection terms
    and an inverse-transpose of its camera transform -- not through
    [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4).
 3. A separable bilateral blur, when the pass's blur flag is set: two draws ping-ponging between
    the two occlusion targets, so the blurred result ends up back in the first. Neither draw is
    idempotent -- each reads and writes the same pair of textures.
 4. The temporal resolve, when [`m_EnableTemporalFilter`](graphics_engine::ssao::SSAOPass) is
    set, into the current slot of the history targets, sampling the previous slot. This is the
    only phase that calls [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4), uploading the
    composed clip-to-world basis as vertex constants 1..4 of constant buffer 2. Unless the pass
    is on its first frame it is preceded by a second separable blur pair, over the previous
    history slot.
 5. The composite into the alpha channel of the scene target (colour mask 8, depth test on),
    followed by the inlined history advance.

kind.doc:
The screen-space decal render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockSSDecal`): one projected decal
 box, drawn with the permutations set up by [`RenderBlockTypeSSDecal`].

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Stages the decal's own constants and issues its box geometry as a single [`DrawIndexed`].

 On the vertex side it bakes the instance's offset world-view-projection at slot 1 registers
 0..3 and the decal's orthonormal box basis at registers 4..7. On the fragment side it stages
 the decal's colour, fade, and masking tuning at slot 1 registers 4..11, and at **register 12**
 the screen-space UV scale the render context carries — the factor that maps a `[0, 1]` viewport
 UV onto the used region of the shared scene depth texture, which the permutations multiply
 their reconstruction UV by before sampling it. It also sets the colour mask from the decal's
 own channel flags.

 The depth→view-space basis this consumes is whatever
 [`RenderBlockTypeSSDecal::Setup`](RenderBlockTypeSSDecal::Setup) staged for the pass; nothing
 here restages it.

kind.doc:
The screen-space reflection render block. Its `Draw` reconstructs world position from depth via
 [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) and ray-marches a scene colour capture
 taken earlier in the frame.

fields.name: m_WorkingWidth
fields.doc:
The block's own working resolution for the blur: the size the separable blur dispatches and
 constants are derived from.

fields.name: m_ComputeBlur
fields.doc: Selects the blur path: the two-draw separable blur when set, the compute blur when clear.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the screen-space reflection pass.

 One call runs, in order: a scene-colour capture draw; the ray-march draw, which is the only
 phase that calls [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) (uploaded as vertex
 constants 1..4) and which writes the block's reflection-colour and reflection-alpha targets
 through a stencil test; and then a separable blur of those two targets, on one of two mutually
 exclusive paths selected by [`m_ComputeBlur`](Self::m_ComputeBlur).

 The pixel-shader path is two fullscreen draws ping-ponging the colour/alpha pair against a
 second pair, so the blurred result lands back in the first pair. The compute path is two
 [`Dispatch`](graphics_engine::draw::Dispatch) calls over the same two pairs, running the
 `screenspacereflectionblur` compute program (thread group 256x1x1):

 - The first blurs horizontally, dispatched `ceil(width / 256)` by `height` groups.
 - The second blurs vertically, dispatched `ceil(height / 256)` by `width` groups, with the
   source and destination pairs exchanged so the result again ends up in the first pair.

 [`m_WorkingWidth`](Self::m_WorkingWidth) and [`m_WorkingHeight`](Self::m_WorkingHeight) are the
 block's own working resolution. They are
 also uploaded as `x` and `y` of compute constant 0, whose `w` is the axis flag that tells the
 program which way to blur (1.0 horizontal, 0.0 vertical) by transposing its thread-id-to-texel
 mapping; there is no origin or offset term in either constant buffer, and the program addresses
 its textures directly by `SV_DispatchThreadID`, so the region it covers is always the whole
 texture from texel zero. `z` of that constant is the gloss threshold below which a texel is
 copied through unblurred.

 The blur kernel is a bilateral one over up to 13 taps, `-6..+6` texels along the blur axis,
 weighted down by the linear-depth difference to the centre texel and truncated to as few as 3
 taps as gloss rises. Its reach across the texture is therefore 6 texels, and the compute path
 stages that halo through group-shared memory (a 256-wide tile plus a 6-texel skirt on each
 side, clamped to the texture bounds).

kind.doc:
The screen-space subsurface-scattering render block for skin. Its `Draw` reconstructs from depth
 via [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) and blurs the lit skin in screen
 space.

fields.name: m_DrawMode
fields.doc: Selects the draw path: the single-draw path when set, the full diffusion chain when clear.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws the subsurface-scattering pass, on one of two mutually exclusive paths selected by
 [`m_DrawMode`](Self::m_DrawMode): a single-draw path, and the full diffusion chain (a
 screen-space gather into the SSS targets, then six separable blur draws ping-ponging between
 them). Each path builds the depth-reconstruction basis with exactly one
 [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4) call, before its first render-setup
 bind, and uploads it as vertex constants 1..4.

kind.doc: A base VolumetricTerrain render block instance (`CRenderBlockTerrain`): one per terrain tile/sector.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The per-block colour-pass setup (`IRenderBlock::Setup`): binds the tessellation programs,
 including the hull program [`HullClipType`](Self::HullClipType) selects.

associated_functions.name: SetupZ
associated_functions.doc:
The per-block depth-pass setup (`IRenderBlock::SetupZ`), selecting the hull program the same
 way as [`Setup`](Self::Setup).

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the tile's tessellated geometry. The depth prepass and the colour pass both draw through
 this entry.

associated_functions.name: DrawZ
associated_functions.doc:
The depth-only draw entry (`IRenderBlock::DrawZ`); compiled to an empty
 function.

associated_functions.name: UpdateSortID
associated_functions.doc:
Rebuilds the block's sort identifier from the camera translation. Called by the base terrain
 patch system's per-patch update fragment (`TerrainPatchUpdate`).

associated_functions.name: UpdateAlpha
associated_functions.doc:
Advances the tile's LOD-blend alpha by `delta` when LOD blending is enabled, then updates the
 global terrain mask ([`UpdateGlobalMask`](Self::UpdateGlobalMask)).

associated_functions.name: SetAlpha
associated_functions.doc: Sets the tile's LOD-blend alpha and fade direction, then updates the global terrain mask.

associated_functions.name: UpdateGlobalMask
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the tile's value into the global terrain visibility mask that the LOD-clip hull
 programs sample.

associated_functions.name: HullClipType
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the hull-clip type that selects the hull program `Setup`, `SetupZ`, and `Draw` bind
 (`m_HullProgram[clip + 4*scheme]`). The result is always
 [`TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_DISABLED`](TerrainHullClipType::TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_DISABLED),
 [`TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_BETWEEN_LODS`](TerrainHullClipType::TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_BETWEEN_LODS), or
 [`TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_UNDER_WATER`](TerrainHullClipType::TERRAIN_HULL_CLIP_UNDER_WATER).

 The LOD clip's hull samples the global terrain mask (the `VisibilityMask` texture bound from
 `SGlobalRBTerrainContext`) at the patch's four corners. When every corner reads below 0.05, a
 finer-LOD tile has fully faded in over that footprint, and the hull zeroes the tessellation
 factors, which discards the patch. The water clip discards patches below the cached water
 level when the camera is above water. The disabled clip discards nothing.

 Tiles above the base LOD (`m_PatchLOD > 9`) always resolve to the LOD clip. Base-LOD tiles
 resolve to the water clip when the tile is at the context's high-detail LOD and the camera is
 above water, or when the render context's
 [`m_RenderStatus`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderStatus) carries
 [`RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderStatus::RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS).
 Otherwise they resolve to the disabled clip. The exception is that base-LOD tiles also resolve
 to the LOD clip when `CWaterPatchManager::m_EnableWaterRenderPass` is clear. The same
 selection runs in every pass (depth prepass and color alike).

kind.doc:
The terrain detail render block (`NGraphicsEngine::CTerrainRenderBlockDetail`, engine name
 "TerrainDetail"): the procedurally-generated detail rock skin — cliff walls, cave ceilings, and
 near-field rock detail scattered on the base terrain. Its vertices/indices/texels are produced
 each frame by the compute pipeline in the sibling terrain-setup block into shared structured
 buffers, and drawn GPU-indirect via a single [`DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect`] (the colour pass runs
 plain vertex+fragment, no tessellation). The vertex shader reads a patch-local vertex and
 transforms it by a CPU-baked `cb1` (vertex slot 1) whose rows are `T_patch · m_OffsetViewProjection`,
 where `T_patch` translates by the patch origin expressed relative to the camera; the resulting
 clip is the standard `m_OffsetViewProjection · (world - m_CameraPosition)`. `cb1` is staged by the
 block's per-patch `Setup` (via [`SetVertexProgramConstants`] on vertex slot 1) immediately before
 each `Draw`.

fields.name: m_WorldPatchX
fields.doc:
The patch origin's world X. The vertices are patch-local in X relative to this; the baked `cb1`
 folds `(m_WorldPatchX - m_CameraPosition.x)` into its translation row.

fields.name: m_WorldPatchZ
fields.doc: The patch origin's world Z (see `m_WorldPatchX`).

fields.name: m_DetailPatchIndex
fields.doc: The patch's index into the terrain setup type's detail draw list.

fields.name: m_DetailLod
fields.doc: The patch's detail LOD (0 or 1), the minor index into the detail draw list.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the colour-pass draw: a single
 [`DrawInstancedIndirect`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawInstancedIndirect) over the
 compute-generated detail geometry, reading its arguments from the 16-byte slot
 `m_DetailLod + 2 * m_DetailPatchIndex` of
 [`RenderBlockTypeTerrainSetup::m_DetailDrawList`], using the `cb1` transform staged by `Setup`.

kind.doc:
One volumetric-terrain patch instance (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockTerrainPatch`): the
 per-patch render block the terrain patch system enqueues onto the terrain basemesh passes, one
 per quadtree patch. Partial: only the placement and sort fields are mapped.

fields.name: m_Position
fields.doc:
The patch's world-space placement origin. Together with
 [`m_Size`](Self::m_Size) it spans the patch's footprint; the patch's
 512 m tile indices ([`m_TileX`](Self::m_TileX)) derive from the same
 placement.

fields.name: m_Size
fields.doc: The patch's world-space side length (quadtree level dependent).

fields.name: m_PatchLOD
fields.doc: The patch's quadtree LOD level.

fields.name: m_TileX
fields.doc: The patch's 512 m world tile X index (offset by half the 32,768 m world).

fields.name: m_TileZ
fields.doc: The patch's 512 m world tile Z index.

fields.name: m_SortID
fields.doc:
The block's sort identifier, rebuilt per frame by
 [`UpdateSortID`](Self::UpdateSortID): bits 32..47 carry the squared
 camera tile distance (in 512 m tiles), bits 61+ a tessellation/LOD class, and the low 32
 bits the block pointer. The block's `GetSortID` returns it verbatim, so terrain patches
 sort by tessellation class, then tile distance.

associated_functions.name: UpdateSortID
associated_functions.doc:
Rebuilds [`m_SortID`](Self::m_SortID) from the camera translation:
 recomputes the camera-relative tile deltas and packs the squared tile distance and
 tessellation class. Called by the terrain patch system's per-frame update.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Issues the patch's geometry for the active render pass, keyed on
 [`m_ActiveRenderPass`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_ActiveRenderPass):

 - The near tessellating passes,
   [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR)
   and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR),
   draw GPU-indirect via
   [`DrawInstancedIndirect`](graphics_engine::draw::DrawInstancedIndirect). The per-patch
   instance count comes from the terrain patch system's GPU compute output, so no instance count
   is known CPU-side. Each stages a one-`float4` control constant on vertex slot 3
   (`{ m_DetailPatchIndex, mode, 0, 0 }`, with `mode` 2 for the tessellating pass and 3 for the
   other) and binds the shared global detail index/vertex texture buffers before the indirect
   draw.
 - [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_FAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_FAR)
   and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR)
   draw the tail index range (`[m_SplitIndex, m_IndexCount)`) with a plain [`DrawIndexed`].
   [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_FAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_FAR)
   and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_COLOR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_COLOR)
   draw the head range (`[0, m_SplitIndex)`). The split partitions the patch's index buffer
   between the two families.
 - [`PRE_RP_REFLECTION_MESH`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_REFLECTION_MESH)
   and the reflective-shadow passes
   ([`PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_SUN_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_SUN_NEAR),
   [`PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_SUN_FAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_SUN_FAR),
   and [`PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_CAMERA`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::PRE_RP_SHADOW_REFLECTIVE_CAMERA))
   draw the full index range with a plain [`DrawIndexed`].
 - Any other pass returns without drawing.

 The vertex transform for every path is the global view-projection: the type-level
 `SetupConstantBuffers` binds `m_VPGlobals` at vertex `cb0` (the rows carrying
 [`m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection)),
 and the per-patch streamed constant buffer at vertex `cb1`; the tessellating passes additionally
 carry `m_OffsetViewProjection` in the hull/domain constants baked once per frame.

kind.doc:
The additive fog-volume render block *type* (the
 `NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockAddFogVolume::CRenderBlockTypeAddFogVolume` singleton, type name
 `"AddFogVolume"`): the shared vertex/fragment programs, unit vertex buffer, and sampler for the
 additive fog-volume blocks that `CFogManager` draws through its own render passes.

 This type is never registered. `CRenderBlockAddFogVolume::InitType` constructs it, stores it in
 this singleton, calls its `Create`, and returns without calling `CRenderBlockFactory::AddType`.
 Its only caller is the `CFogManager` constructor, which does not register it either. The type
 therefore never enters the global
 [`RenderBlockTypeRegistry`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderBlockTypeRegistry), and a walk
 of the registry does not reach it. `CRenderPass::DoDraw` still dispatches its `IsEnabled` through
 the vtable exactly as it does for a registered type. This singleton is the only way to reach it.
 See [`RenderBlockTypeParticle`](RenderBlockTypeParticle), which is unregistered in the same way.

functions.name: Create
functions.doc:
Creates the type's GPU resources (shaders, buffers) against the given
 `SResourceContext`. Each type's `RegisterType` calls this at startup with the render
 engine's own resource context.

functions.name: Destroy
functions.doc: Destroys the type's GPU resources.

functions.name: Recreate
functions.doc:
Recreates the type's GPU resources against the given `SResourceContext`.
 `CRenderEngine::RecreateRenderBlockTypes` calls this on every registered type with the
 render engine's own resource context (the settings-change path). Several types,
 including the terrain setup types, implement it as a no-op; for those, only
 [`Destroy`](Self::Destroy) followed by [`Create`](Self::Create) rebuilds the resources.

functions.name: GetTypeName
functions.doc: Returns the type's display name (e.g. `"VolumetricTerrain"`, `"TerrainPatch"`).

functions.name: GetHash
functions.doc: Returns the type's name hash (the registry sort key).

functions.name: IsEnabled
functions.doc:
Whether render passes draw blocks of this type: `CRenderPass::DoDraw` dispatches this
 per type run (vtable slot [`IsEnabled`](Self::IsEnabled)) and skips every block whose
 type reports disabled. The base implementation is compiled to a
 constant `true`.

functions.name: Enable
functions.doc:
Enables drawing of this type's blocks. The base implementation is
 compiled to a no-op (the enabled flag was optimized out).

functions.name: Disable
functions.doc:
Disables drawing of this type's blocks. The base implementation is
 compiled to a no-op (the enabled flag was optimized out), so a type's
 [`IsEnabled`](Self::IsEnabled) implementation alone decides whether its blocks draw.

kind.doc:
The atmospheric-scattering render block type object: the scattering LUT textures and the
 sky-lighting SH coefficient targets the block's compute pass writes each frame (in

fields.name: m_TransmittanceTexture
fields.doc: The atmospheric transmittance LUT (compute slot 0).

fields.name: m_IrradianceTexture
fields.doc: The atmospheric irradiance LUT (compute slot 1).

fields.name: m_InscatteringTexture

fields.name: m_SHLightingGreenCoeffs

fields.name: m_SHLightingBlueCoeffs
fields.doc: The sky-lighting SH blue-coefficient texture (fragment slot `0x18`).

fields.name: m_HiResTextureWidth
fields.doc:
The full-resolution fog target width, in pixels, latched from the last
 [`ResizeTextures`](Self::ResizeTextures) call.

fields.name: m_HiResTextureHeight
fields.doc:
The full-resolution fog target height, in pixels; see

associated_functions.name: ResizeTextures
associated_functions.doc:
Recreates the fog-volume textures for a `width` x `height` render target: the full-resolution
 `fogvolume_texture_0` colour target and its volume texture, plus a coarse volumetric-depth
 buffer that is resized to *half* of `width` x `height`. Invoked from the graphics engine's
 registered resolution-change callback, so it re-runs whenever the scene render targets are
 recreated (a resolution change), not per frame.

kind.doc:
The particle render block *type* (the `CRenderBlockParticle::CRenderBlockTypeParticle` singleton):
 the shared state and shaders for every particle render block, including the flags that decide
 whether a particle draw is routed to the low-resolution particle pass.

 This type is never registered. `CRenderBlockParticle::InitType` constructs it, stores it in this
 singleton, calls its `Create`, and returns without calling `CRenderBlockFactory::AddType`, which
 every other render block's `InitType`/`RegisterType` eventually does. The type therefore does not
 appear in the global
 [`RenderBlockTypeRegistry`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderBlockTypeRegistry), and a walk
 of the registry does not reach it. `CRenderPass::DoDraw` still dispatches its `IsEnabled` through
 the vtable exactly as it does for a registered type. This singleton is the only way to reach it.

 Two types skip registration: this one and
 [`RenderBlockTypeAddFogVolume`](RenderBlockTypeAddFogVolume). The evidence is a walk of every
 construction site of `IRenderBlockType` in the image (the calls to its constructor plus the sites
 that inline it, which are exactly the writers of
 [`RenderBlockTypeInstances`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderBlockTypeInstances)), with each
 site checked against `CRenderBlockFactory::AddType`.

fields.name: m_LowResRendering
fields.doc:
When set, a particle render block whose effect opts in and that falls below the low-resolution
 distance threshold routes its draw to the low-resolution particle pass (later composited back
 up by the low-res upsampling pass); when clear, that particle routes to the full-resolution
 transparent pass instead. Set from the particle-quality graphics setting. The per-block routing
 (`CRenderBlockParticle::GetRenderDetails`) selects the pass index from this flag ORed with
 [`m_ForceLowResRendering`](Self::m_ForceLowResRendering).

fields.name: m_ForceLowResRendering
fields.doc:
Forces every particle render block onto the low-resolution particle pass regardless of the
 per-effect opt-in or the distance threshold, ORed with
 [`m_LowResRendering`](Self::m_LowResRendering).

The type-level per-pass setup (the `IRenderBlockType::Setup` override). Binds the forward lighting
 resources through
 [`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources).

kind.doc:
The screen-space decal render block *type*
 (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockSSDecal::CRenderBlockTypeSSDecal`): the per-pass setup shared by
 the twelve `ssdecal*` fragment permutations, which project a decal's textures onto whatever the
 scene depth buffer says is behind the decal's box volume.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the decal render state (alpha blend, depth test with depth writes off, back-face cull),
 the shared vertex program and vertex declaration, and stages the pass's **depth→view-space
 reconstruction basis on fragment slot 1, registers 0..3**.

 The basis is `Scaling(2, -2, 1)` with the translation row `(-1, 1, 0, 1)` — the viewport-UV to
 NDC map — post-multiplied (row-vector convention) by the inverse of
 [`RenderContext::m_View`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_View) with its
 translation row replaced by `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, times
 [`RenderContext::m_ProjectionF`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_ProjectionF).
 The fragment shaders feed it the interpolated projective screen coordinate divided by its `w`
 (a UV normalized over the *viewport*) together with the sampled scene depth, and divide the
 result by `w` to recover the camera-relative world position the decal box is tested against.

 It is staged once per pass, not per draw: [`RenderBlockSSDecal::Draw`] restages every other
 fragment constant the permutations read but never this one.

 The whole body is conditional on the render context's pass flags, so the depth-only and
 velocity passes stage nothing.

associated_functions.name: SetupConstantBuffers
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the render context's global constant buffers to vertex and fragment slot 0 and declares
 the pass's instance-constant slots: vertex slot 1 at **8** `float4` rows (base row 0), fragment
 slot 1 at **13** rows (base row 0), and slots 2 and 3 unused on both stages.

 Those are exactly the rows the permutations declare: the shared `ssdecal` vertex program
 declares `cb1[7]` and the twelve fragment permutations declare `cb1[13]`. Because
 [`SetFragmentProgramConstantBufferSize`] rounds a declared row count up to the next pool size
 class, the buffer actually bound to fragment slot 1 for this pass holds **16** rows and
 [`SetupRenderStates`] uploads all sixteen — the three rows past the declared thirteen carry
 whatever the shared staging array holds.

kind.doc: The `RenderBlockSkidmarks` render block *type* (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockSkidmarks::CRenderBlockTypeSkidmarks`).

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The type-level per-pass setup (the `IRenderBlockType::Setup` override). Binds the forward lighting
 resources through
 [`LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources`](graphics_engine::light_manager::LightManager::SetupForwardLightingResources).

kind.doc:
The terrain render block *type* (the `CRenderBlockTerrain::CRenderBlockTypeTerrain` singleton).
 Its `SetupConstantBuffers` uploads the per-LOD-slot hull/domain tessellation constant buffer —
 which bakes the dispatch's
 [`RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection),
 camera position, and tessellation factors — into
 [`m_HDTypeConstants`](Self::m_HDTypeConstants), caching it per slot
 keyed on the frame the upload was made for.

fields.name: m_DebugMode
fields.doc:
The debug visualization mode. When `<= 0`, `Setup` selects the normal shading fragment
 programs; when `> 0`, it selects the debug fragment program at index `m_DebugMode + 13`
 instead (LOD colours, tessellation, and similar overlays; the program array holds 21
 entries, so 1..=7 are valid).

fields.name: m_HDTypeConstants
fields.doc:
The constant-buffer handle array, per-LOD-slot, whose entries the type's
 `SetupConstantBuffers` bakes the tessellation constants into.

fields.name: m_WasCBApplied
fields.doc:
Per-LOD-slot cache stamp: the
 [`RenderContext::m_RenderFrameNo`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_RenderFrameNo)
 of the frame whose tessellation constants were last uploaded into that slot's constant buffer.
 `SetupConstantBuffers` re-uploads a slot only when the current frame's stamp differs, so the
 baked view-projection is written once per frame and reused for every draw of that slot within
 the frame.

fields.name: m_NoDraw
fields.doc: When set, `Draw` returns before issuing any draw call, suppressing every base-terrain block.

fields.name: m_EnableBackPatchCulling
fields.doc:
Enables back-patch culling in the reflection passes. When set, `SetupConstantBuffers` bakes a
 cull flag (gated on [`RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderStatus::RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS)) into the hull/domain constant buffer alongside the
 normalized forward vector of the camera manager's render camera and the
 [`m_BackPatchCullThreshold`](Self::m_BackPatchCullThreshold), so the hull
 shader discards patches whose facing is beyond the threshold relative to that view direction.

fields.name: m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling
fields.doc:
Enables frustum patch culling in the color pass. When set (and the active pass is not a shadow
 cascade,
 [`RP_TERRAIN_APPLY_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAIN_APPLY_NEAR),
 or [`RP_TERRAIN_APPLY_FAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAIN_APPLY_FAR)),
 `SetupConstantBuffers` bakes a cull flag into the
 hull/domain constant buffer so the hull shader discards patches outside the baked
 [`m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection)
 frustum.

fields.name: m_ShowDebugCulling
fields.doc:
Debug flag: when set, `Setup` leaves the cull face at `NONE` in the color pass (rather than
 `BACK`), so patches the hull shader would otherwise cull are still rasterized — a visualization
 of what patch culling removes.

fields.name: m_EnableCullByDetail
fields.doc:
Enables the per-detail cull term baked into the hull/domain constant buffer by
 `SetupConstantBuffers`.

fields.name: m_TessellationFactorInner
fields.doc: The inner tessellation factor baked into the hull/domain constant buffer.

fields.name: m_TessellationFactorEdge
fields.doc:
The edge tessellation factor baked into the hull/domain constant buffer. The hull shader scales
 each patch's edge tessellation from this by the patch's projected screen-space size; when the
 resulting factor falls to zero or below, the tessellator discards the patch.

fields.name: m_TessellationFactorMinSpacing
fields.doc:
The minimum screen-space spacing target for tessellation, baked as its reciprocal into the
 hull/domain constant buffer. Smaller values raise the tessellation factor a given projected
 patch size resolves to.

fields.name: m_TessellationFactorSphere
fields.doc: The sphere (curvature) tessellation factor baked into the hull/domain constant buffer.

fields.name: m_TessellationFactorNormalDiff
fields.doc: The normal-difference tessellation factor baked into the hull/domain constant buffer.

fields.name: m_BackPatchCullThreshold
fields.doc:
The facing threshold for
 [`m_EnableBackPatchCulling`](Self::m_EnableBackPatchCulling), baked into the
 hull/domain constant buffer. A patch is culled when its facing relative to the render camera's
 forward vector falls beyond this value.

kind.doc:
The volumetric-patch terrain render block *type* (the
 `NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockTerrainPatch::CRenderBlockTypeTerrainPatch` singleton): the tessellated
 cliff/overhang variant of [`RenderBlockTypeTerrain`], with the same per-slot constant-buffer caching.

fields.name: m_DebugMode
fields.doc:
The debug visualization mode. When `<= 0`, `Setup` selects the normal shading fragment
 programs; when `> 0`, it selects the debug fragment program at index `m_DebugMode + 60` instead
 (LOD colours, tessellation, and similar overlays).

fields.name: m_HDTypeConstants
fields.doc: The constant-buffer handle array, per-LOD-slot.

fields.name: m_WasCBApplied
fields.doc:
Per-LOD-slot cache stamp; see [`RenderBlockTypeTerrain::m_WasCBApplied`]. Sits after
 [`m_HDTypeConstants`](Self::m_HDTypeConstants).

fields.name: m_HullProgramHolders
fields.doc:
The hull-program holders, indexed by clip type (each holder is two pointers; the first is
 what `Setup` passes to `SetHullProgram`). The type's `Setup` inlines the clip selection. The
 near passes
 ([`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR)
 and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR))
 bind index 0 (no clipping). Every other tessellating pass
 ([`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_FAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_FAR)
 and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR))
 binds index 2 — the LOD clip, whose hull discards patches that a finer-LOD tile's global
 mask footprint covers. Index 1 is the disabled-clip variant the (compiled-out) debug flag
 would select, and index 3 the detail-clip variant.

fields.name: m_ShowMaterial
fields.doc:
When set, `Setup` binds the material-inspection fragment program instead of the shading one,
 overriding the debug-mode and tint selection.

fields.name: m_NoDraw
fields.doc: When set, the render block's draw is suppressed.

fields.name: m_EnableBackPatchCulling
fields.doc:
Enables back-patch culling in the reflection passes. When set, `SetupConstantBuffers` bakes a
 cull flag (gated on [`RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderStatus::RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS)) into the hull/domain constant buffer alongside the
 normalized forward vector of the camera manager's render camera and the
 [`m_BackPatchCullThreshold`](Self::m_BackPatchCullThreshold), so the hull
 shader discards patches whose facing is beyond the threshold relative to that view direction.

fields.name: m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling
fields.doc:
Enables frustum patch culling in the color pass. When set (and the active pass is neither a
 shadow cascade nor one of the passes from
 [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR)
 through
 [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_COLOR)),
 `SetupConstantBuffers` bakes a cull flag into the
 hull/domain constant buffer so the hull shader discards patches outside the baked
 [`m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection)
 frustum.

fields.name: m_ShowDebugCulling
fields.doc:
Debug flag: when set, `Setup` leaves the cull face at `NONE` in the color pass (rather than
 `BACK`), so patches the hull shader would otherwise cull are still rasterized — a visualization
 of what patch culling removes.

fields.name: m_EnableCullByDetail
fields.doc:
Enables the per-detail cull term baked into the hull/domain constant buffer by
 `SetupConstantBuffers`.

fields.name: m_BackPatchCullThreshold
fields.doc:
The facing threshold for
 [`m_EnableBackPatchCulling`](Self::m_EnableBackPatchCulling), baked into
 the hull/domain constant buffer. A patch is culled when its facing relative to the render
 camera's forward vector falls beyond this value.

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The type-level per-pass setup for the color-family passes: binds the pass's vertex, hull,
 domain, and fragment programs (the depth-family passes route to `SetupZ` via the render
 status). The hull-clip selection is inlined here: the near passes
 ([`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_TESSELLATE_NEAR)
 and [`RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderPassId::RP_TERRAINPATCH_BASEMESH_NEAR))
 bind [`m_HullProgramHolders`](Self::m_HullProgramHolders) index 0, and the other
 tessellating passes bind index 2.

associated_functions.name: SetupConstantBuffers
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the type-level constant buffers for a tessellating pass and, once per frame per
 constant-buffer slot (the slot comes from the render status and active pass; the stamp is
 [`m_WasCBApplied`](Self::m_WasCBApplied)), bakes the hull/domain constants that the terrain
 hull and domain programs read at `cb1`:

 - `float4` 0: `xyz` = the normalized forward vector of the camera manager's *render* camera
   (its `m_TransformF` third basis vector), `w` = `1.0` when the pass carries
   [`RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderStatus::RENDERSTATUS_REFLECTIONS) and [`m_EnableBackPatchCulling`](Self::m_EnableBackPatchCulling) is set,
   else `0.0`. The hull program discards a patch when all three of its control-point normals
   are beyond [`m_BackPatchCullThreshold`](Self::m_BackPatchCullThreshold) relative to that one
   direction, so the test approximates the view vector for the whole patch by the camera axis.
 - `float4` 1..4: `rc->m_OffsetViewProjection`, the camera-relative view-projection the hull
   program's frustum test projects each control point (expanded by the patch radius along its
   normal) through; a patch whose expanded bounds fall entirely outside one clip plane is
   discarded.
 - `float4` 5: `rc->CameraPosition` in `xyz`, with
   [`m_EnableCullByDetail`](Self::m_EnableCullByDetail) converted to a float in `w`.
 - `float4` 6: the camera position again, with the type's tessellation distance in `w`.
 - `float4` 7..8: the tessellation factors (inner, edge, `1 / min-spacing`, sphere, normal
   difference), then `m_BackPatchCullThreshold`, then the frustum-cull flag — `1.0` unless the
   active pass is a shadow cascade or one of the passes named under
   [`m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling`](Self::m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling), and `0.0` whenever
   [`m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling`](Self::m_EnableFrustumPatchCulling) is clear — and a
   half-resolution flag fixed at `1.0`.

 The buffer is then bound at hull and domain `cb1`, and the global view-projection constants at
 vertex `cb0`.

kind.doc:
The terrain setup render block *type* (`CRenderBlockTerrainSetup::CRenderBlockTypeTerrainSetup`):
 owns the structured buffers the terrain compute passes fill (patch, triangle, quad, and detail
 draw lists) and the compute programs that fill them.

fields.name: m_DetailDrawList
fields.doc:
The detail draw list: the per-patch, per-detail-LOD 16-byte indirect draw-argument slots the
 terrain compute passes write and [`RenderBlockTerrainDetail::Draw`] draws from.

kind.doc: The `RenderBlockWeather` render block *type* (`NGraphicsEngine::CRenderBlockWeather::CRenderBlockTypeWeather`).

associated_functions.name: Setup
associated_functions.doc:
The type-level per-pass setup (the `IRenderBlockType::Setup` override). Binds the forward lighting
