associated_functions.doc:
Sets the heat level on `target`: clears any previous target's heat, tops the target's heat
 points up to the level's threshold, records the target, and fires the level's heat-change
 (and vocal) events. `level` is clamped to `0..=m_LevelCap` unless `ignore_cap`.
 `force_initial_heat_lock` restarts the initial-heat lock timer.

associated_functions.name: ClearHeat
associated_functions.doc:
Drops the heat to zero: zeroes the target's heat points and timers, clears the pursuer,
 ambient, and vehicle lists, fires the current level's heat-cleared event (and the vocal
 unless `silent`), and restarts the initial-heat lock.

associated_functions.name: SetLevelCap
associated_functions.doc:
Sets [`m_LevelCap`](Self::m_LevelCap), clamped to `0..=MAX_LEVEL`, and if the current level
 exceeds it, lowers the level to the cap and trims the target's heat points to just below the
 next threshold. It clamps negative caps to zero, so it cannot set
 [`LEVEL_CAP_NONE`](Self::LEVEL_CAP_NONE); `CHeatManager::Reset` does.

associated_functions.name: GetHeatTarget
associated_functions.doc: The current heat target (the character carrying the heat), or null when none.

kind.doc: The [`m_LevelCap`](Self::m_LevelCap) value meaning no cap. Set by `CHeatManager::Reset`.
The number of heat levels above zero: valid levels are `0..=MAX_LEVEL`.
`CButtonMapping::EButtonInteraction`: how a mapping's actions must be pressed.

variants.name: BINT_TWO_BUTTON_HOLD_AND_TAP
variants.doc:
[`m_Action1`](MappingInfo::m_Action1) held while [`m_Action2`](MappingInfo::m_Action2) is
 tapped.

variants.name: BINT_SINGLE_BUTTON_RELEASE
variants.doc: Fires on button release.

kind.doc:
`CButtonMapping`: the fixed table of semantic button mappings the button-hint and
 controls-screen UI resolve against, plus the action list for the bindings screen.

fields.name: m_AllInfo
fields.doc: One entry per [`Mapping`], [`NUM_MAPPINGS`](Mapping::NUM_MAPPINGS) in all.

associated_functions.name: Init
associated_functions.doc:
Calls [`PopulateMappings`](Self::PopulateMappings), then rebuilds the controls-screen
 action list.

associated_functions.name: PopulateMappings
associated_functions.doc:
Fills every [`m_AllInfo`](Self::m_AllInfo) entry from hardcoded data: the actions,
 interaction, `buttonhint_*` key hash, ability and upgrade gates, and flags. There is no data
 file behind the table.

kind.doc:
`CButtonMapping::EMapping`: a semantic button mapping, indexing
 [`ButtonMapping::m_AllInfo`]. The `MAPPING_*` values are grouped into per-context sections
 (generic, on foot, context-specific on foot, each vehicle class, UI, weaponized wingsuit, and
 mech); each section ends with an `END_*` marker slot that stays at the constructor default, and
 the `FIRST_*` / `LAST_*` constants give each section's inclusive bounds for the range queries.
 [`ButtonMapping::PopulateMappings`] hardcodes every entry.

`CButtonMapping::SMappingInfo`: one semantic mapping's actions, hint text, gates, and flags.
 The layout stores the two gate hashes as bare 32-bit hashes.

fields.name: m_Action1
fields.doc:
The primary action (the held one for a chord). The constructor default is
 [`Action::COUNT`], an invalid action, which the `END_*` marker slots keep.

fields.name: m_Action2
fields.doc: The tapped action of a chord, or [`Action::COUNT`] when unused.

fields.name: m_DescriptionKey
fields.doc: The hash of the `buttonhint_*` localization key.

fields.name: m_RequiredUpgrade
fields.doc: The upgrade that must be purchased and enabled for the mapping to be active, or zero.

fields.name: m_RequiredAbility
fields.doc: The ability that must be enabled on the player for the mapping to be active, or zero.

fields.name: m_Customizable
fields.doc: Whether the player can rebind the mapping.

fields.name: m_ShowInUIMapping
fields.doc: Whether the mapping is listed on the controls screen.

fields.name: m_PCOnly
fields.doc: Whether the mapping applies only to keyboard and mouse.

fields.name: m_ControllerOnly
fields.doc: Whether the mapping applies only to a gamepad.

kind.doc:
`CControllerUtility`: static helpers that relate controller input, the camera, and character
 orientation. Only some members are bound.

associated_functions.name: GetDeltaAngleFromOrientation
associated_functions.doc:
The signed XZ angle (degrees, -180..180) from the character's current world forward to
 `dir`. Read by the swim input tasks to pick between the forward crawl-start act and the
 directional 120-degree turn acts, by the AI turn/exit-vehicle behaviors, and by the
 locomotion aim-blend state's sampler weighting.

associated_functions.name: TransformInputDirToWorldDir
associated_functions.doc:
Transforms a camera-relative direction (`input_dir`, the negated camera forward) and a
 camera-relative input vector (`input`, the stick's X and Y axes) into a world direction.
 `input.x` is the lateral (strafe) axis and `input.y` the forward/back axis. The general
 helper for turning controller input into a world direction: fifteen call sites across the
 locomotion, swim, jump, melee, grapple, aim, and AI steering paths.

kind.doc:
An action ID, indexing [`action_name_table`]. The numbering is fixed at build time. The engine
 passes action IDs as plain integers.

The number of action ids: the length of [`action_name_table`], and the action value
 meaning "no action" in the button-mapping table.
The digital state of an [`InputDeviceEffector`].

variants.name: Idle
variants.doc: Idle, with no input this frame.

variants.name: Idle2
variants.doc: Idle, in the alternate idle slot.

variants.name: Clicked
variants.doc: Clicked this frame: a one-frame press edge.

variants.name: Pressed
variants.doc: Pressed or held.

variants.name: Released
variants.doc: Released this frame.

variants.name: Frozen
variants.doc: Held latched by [`Freeze`](InputDeviceEffector::Freeze), ignoring the device poll.

kind.doc: Maps action IDs to effector slots.

One input effector slot. The pointer [`InputActionMap::GetActionEffector`] returns is the head of a
 linked-list node whose extra id / next fields follow this struct; reading the effector itself uses
 only these fields.

 The `m_Value`, `m_State`, and `m_StateTime` offsets are confirmed against their uses.

fields.name: m_Value
fields.doc:
The analog value, e.g. trigger pressure or stick axis. [`Click`](Self::Click)
 sets it to `1.0`.

fields.name: m_ForceClick
fields.doc: Injects a click that survives the next device poll.

associated_functions.name: Click
associated_functions.doc:
Drives a one-frame press edge: sets `m_Value` to `1.0` and the state to
 [`EffectorState::Clicked`].

associated_functions.name: Press
associated_functions.doc: Sets `m_Value` and drives the [`EffectorState::Pressed`] state.

associated_functions.name: Freeze
associated_functions.doc: Latches into [`EffectorState::Frozen`], ignoring the device poll until cleared.

associated_functions.name: ForceClick
associated_functions.doc: Sets `m_ForceClick` so the click survives the next per-frame poll.

kind.doc:
The local player's action map: a write-side wrapper that drives effectors by [`Action`]. Invalid
 action IDs resolve to a shared null-effector sentinel, which the setters guard against.

associated_functions.name: GetActionEffector
associated_functions.doc:
The single-argument `CInputActionMap::GetActionEffector(int)` overload the wrapper's own
 setters use: resolves an action to its effector without a device index. The singleton
 pointer is the underlying `CInputActionMap` itself (established from `ForceSetPressed`,
 which passes it straight to the map's effector lookup). Returns the shared null-effector
 sentinel for invalid ids.

associated_functions.name: ForceSetPressed
associated_functions.doc: Drives an analog or held action: sets the effector's value and presses it.

associated_functions.name: ForceSetClicked
associated_functions.doc: Drives a one-frame click for an action: a press edge that survives the poll.

kind.doc:
The action-name table: [`Action::COUNT`] name-string pointers indexed by action id, iterated
 by the `CSteeringUtil` action/string map constructors.

An input device class (`Input::EDeviceType`), as passed to the device manager's device lookup
 and action mapping.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame device poll: reads all devices, refreshes their effector states, and then runs
 [`UpdateForceClicks`](Self::UpdateForceClicks). The poll overwrites effector values written
 before it runs.

associated_functions.name: UpdateForceClicks
associated_functions.doc: Applies the force-click flags latched on effectors so an injected click survives the poll.

kind.doc:
`SCharacterMovementSettings`: the per-character movement tuning resource (referenced from the
 character's movement-settings handle): the on-foot and swim blocks, followed by the plant
 settings (unmapped).
`SCharacterOnFootSettings`: the on-foot block of [`CharacterMovementSettings`].

fields.name: m_WalkSpeed
fields.doc: The walk/run speed threshold the start-act selection compares against.

kind.doc:
`SCharacterSwimSettings`: the swim block of [`CharacterMovementSettings`]. The offsets of the
 two turn-rate fields within the movement settings are confirmed.

fields.name: m_SurfaceSwimDirSlerpSpeed
fields.doc: The surface-swim velocity turn rate; `UpdateSurfaceMovement` scales it by [`SWIM_TURN_RATE_SCALE`](input::swim::SWIM_TURN_RATE_SCALE) degrees per second.

fields.name: m_SurfaceSwimFaceDirSlerpSpeed
fields.doc: The surface-swim facing turn rate: `UpdateSurfaceMovement` rotates the body toward the desired direction at this times [`SWIM_TURN_RATE_SCALE`](input::swim::SWIM_TURN_RATE_SCALE) degrees per second (overridden by [`SWIM_AIM_TURN_RATE`](input::swim::SWIM_AIM_TURN_RATE) while aiming or planting explosives).

kind.doc: The movement task that warps the character onto a physical anchor during a scripted warp.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update: lerps the character toward the anchor over the warp segment's local
 time, evaluates the orientation and displacement through
 [`NStateTask_LocoUtil`], and writes the target direction to the blackboard.

kind.doc: The locomotion input task active while precision-aiming on foot.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. When the player is in precision aim mode and aiming a weapon is
 possible it queues the precision-aim idle or move act from the blackboard speed; otherwise
 it dispatches like [`NStateTask_InputLocoMoveTask::Update`]: aim-relative move or stop-turn
 acts while [`Character::m_AimFlags`] has an aim bit set, run/steer move or stop acts
 otherwise.

kind.doc:
The locomotion move task active while the character is aim-relative (strafing). Mirrors
 [`NStateTask_InputLocoMoveTask`] but stays in the aim-relative acts as long as an aim bit is set.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Like [`NStateTask_InputLocoMoveTask::Update`] it re-reads
 [`Character::m_AimFlags`] each frame and dispatches to the strafe or run acts, so the task
 falls back to run/steer once the aim bits clear.

kind.doc:
The locomotion task active while the character stands still on foot (the `S_IDLE` state). It
 selects on-spot behaviour -- rotate-on-spot turns, aim-relative on-spot actions -- and drives the
 periodic idle variation: a per-character countdown (reset to a random ~8.5-12 s whenever the
 character's aim reference moves) that, once elapsed while the character is idle, calm, and not on
 a vehicle, queues [`ACT_TO_IDLE_ONE_OFF`](animation::symbol_table::EventIdSymbolTable::ACT_TO_IDLE_ONE_OFF)
 to play a one-off idle break.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame idle update. When the idle countdown at [`Character::m_IdleFidgetTimer`] (a
 `f32`) is negative and the character is idle, calm, and off-vehicle, it queues
 `ACT_TO_IDLE_ONE_OFF` and returns; otherwise it decrements the countdown (while idle) or
 resets it, then queues the applicable on-spot or start acts.

kind.doc:
The locomotion move task active when the character is on foot and *not* holding an aim. Its
 [`Update`](Self::Update) reads [`Character::m_AimFlags`] and dispatches
 to run/steer versus strafe locomotion.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Reads the blackboard move direction and speed, then branches on
 [`Character::m_AimFlags`] ([`m_AimingWeapon`](character::character::AimState::m_AimingWeapon) /
 [`m_AimingGrapple`](character::character::AimState::m_AimingGrapple)): with neither set it queues
 [`QueueMoveActions`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::QueueMoveActions) (run — the body steers toward the
 movement vector), otherwise it queues the aim-relative (strafe) acts. This branch selects
 between the run/steer and strafe movement styles on foot.

kind.doc:
The locomotion task that reads the movement effectors and writes the move direction to the
 character blackboard. Like the other `NStateTask` functions, `self` is the *character* -- the
 task types are namespaces over free functions that take the character as `this` (the blackboard
 at [`Character::m_Blackboard`] and the body-forward vector reading straight off it).

associated_functions.name: SetupTargetDir
associated_functions.doc:
Reads the move effectors via the action-map effector lookup, rotates the raw vector
 camera-relative (via the camera input matrix), and writes the previous and new move
 directions to the character blackboard. `target_dir` is in/out: the previous direction on
 entry, the new one on return. Below the input deadzone the *previous* direction (or the
 body forward) is re-written -- the blackboard move direction is always a unit vector and
 carries no input-held information.

kind.doc: The melee input task.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. When melee is possible and clicked (the player also needs the hammer
 ability), picks the melee target from the aim control, sets the character's link target and
 combat mental state, and queues the melee acts.

kind.doc:
Free helpers that queue the concrete locomotion animation acts. The queued act encodes the
 movement style: [`QueueMoveActions`](Self::QueueMoveActions) steers the body
 toward the movement direction, while the aim-relative variants keep the body facing the aim and
 play directional strafe animations.

associated_functions.name: QueueMoveActions
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the run/steer acts (`ACT_MOVE_NO_AIM` and friends). The body turns to face the
 movement direction, so directional input rotates the whole character (third-person on-foot
 steering).

associated_functions.name: QueueAimRelativeMoveActions
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the aim-relative (strafe) acts. It derives the facing reference from the weapon-aim
 target when [`m_AimingWeapon`](character::character::AimState::m_AimingWeapon) is set (or the
 grapple target for [`m_AimingGrapple`](character::character::AimState::m_AimingGrapple)),
 and falls back to the character's own current forward when neither is set, so without an aim
 reference the body keeps its current facing.

associated_functions.name: QueueTransitionToAimRelativeMoveActions
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the one-shot transition into the aim-relative (strafe) acts, played on the frame the
 character starts aiming.

associated_functions.name: EvaluateCharacterOrientation
associated_functions.doc:
Computes the character's new orientation for this frame; the body-yaw executor, called from
 [`NStateTask_MovementLocomotionTask::Update`]. With `track_face_dir` clear (and outside a
 gating animation segment) the rotation comes from the animation root motion
 (`CAnimationControl::GetDeltaRotation`) — the run-mode steer. With it set, the target face
 direction is read from the character blackboard
 ([`TARGET_FACE_DIR_ID`](blackboard::ObjectBlackboard::TARGET_FACE_DIR_ID)) and the body is yawed
 toward it: snapped directly when `snap_to_face_dir` is set (gated on the blend being
 finished when `wait_for_blend` is also set), otherwise rate-limited to `max_step_deg`
 degrees per call — the aim-mode camera tracking. `max_step_deg` must be positive on the
 tracking path (it divides by it). `dt` is only used for the attached-to-vehicle up-vector
 lerp.

associated_functions.name: EvaluateCharacterOrientationMS
associated_functions.doc:
The model-space variant of
 [`EvaluateCharacterOrientation`](Self::EvaluateCharacterOrientation), also
 called from the movement task and from the grapple reel-in controller. The bools are
 believed to match the world-space variant minus the blend gate; unverified.

associated_functions.name: EvaluateCharacterDisplacement
associated_functions.doc:
Computes this frame's movement direction from the animation root motion and the new body
 orientation. Called from [`NStateTask_MovementLocomotionTask::Update`], which normalizes
 `out_direction`, scales it by
 [`EvaluateCharacterSpeed`](Self::EvaluateCharacterSpeed), and writes the
 result as the character's physics velocity. `out_direction` therefore sets only the heading
 of the velocity; the speed envelope comes from the speed evaluation. The bools and
 `out_secondary` are unmapped.

associated_functions.name: EvaluateCharacterSpeed
associated_functions.doc:
Computes this frame's movement speed for the character: the magnitude of the animation
 control's raw root velocity -- so the speed envelope, including the ramp-up through the
 start acts, comes from the animation clips themselves. With `use_blackboard_override` set,
 the [`SPEED_OVERRIDE_ID`](blackboard::ObjectBlackboard::SPEED_OVERRIDE_ID) float replaces
 the result when present. Multiplied onto the
 normalized displacement direction by the movement task.

associated_functions.name: QueueStarts
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the directional run-start (wind-up) acts: measures the XZ angle from the body
 forward to the blackboard move direction, writes the residual angle correction, and queues
 the matching start act (forward/left/right/180, with stunt variants), choosing the
 walk-versus-run flavor by comparing `speed` against the settings' threshold. The start
 clips' root velocity ramping from zero is the on-foot acceleration.

associated_functions.name: QueueStops
associated_functions.doc:
Queues the stop acts for run-mode locomotion; taken by the input tasks when the blackboard
 speed is not positive or the stop validation triggers.

associated_functions.name: QueueStopTurns
associated_functions.doc:
The aim-mode variant of [`QueueStops`](Self::QueueStops): stop-and-turn acts
 that settle the body toward the aim.

associated_functions.name: GetAimMoveAngle
associated_functions.doc:
The XZ angle (degrees) from `move_dir` to the aim reference direction: the vector from the
 character to the player's aim-target position (or the camera forward while planting an
 explosive), both rotated into the character's local frame when the relevant state flag is
 set. Consumed by the aim-relative act dispatchers
 ([`QueueAimRelativeMoveActions`](Self::QueueAimRelativeMoveActions),
 [`QueueStopTurns`](Self::QueueStopTurns), and the on-spot turn queuers) to
 select directional acts and on-spot turns. `move_dir` is a by-value `CVector3f` in the
 source, passed by pointer under the x64 ABI.

kind.doc:
The movement actuator task active during a jump's ascending phase — the airborne analogue of
 [`NStateTask_MovementLocomotionTask`], on a *separate* code path that does not route through
 [`EvaluateCharacterOrientation`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterOrientation) or
 [`GetAimMoveAngle`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::GetAimMoveAngle).

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Computes a desired facing direction, rate-limits the body toward it,
 and writes the character orientation (the `SetOrientation` writes are inlined). The
 desired facing has two sources: when
 [`m_AimingWeapon`](character::character::AimState::m_AimingWeapon) is set it faces the weapon
 aim target (`CPlayerAimControl`'s stored target world position, which tracks the aim camera);
 otherwise it falls back to the current world-forward plus the stick-gated camera-relative steer
 from [`UpdateFallSteering`](UpdateFallSteering).

kind.doc:
The movement actuator task: applies this frame's locomotion to the character, computing the
 body orientation via
 [`EvaluateCharacterOrientation`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterOrientation) (or the MS
 variant) and the translation from the animation root motion.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc: The per-frame update.

kind.doc:
The movement actuator task for stunt locomotion on vehicles and in stunt areas, including the
 stunt step-up and step-down states.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Resolves the stunt area the character stands on (projecting and
 clamping onto its edges, or entering the next interaction-graph node), computes the
 orientation through
 [`EvaluateCharacterOrientation`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterOrientation) (or the
 MS variant) and the displacement through
 [`EvaluateCharacterDisplacement`](NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterDisplacement),
 inheriting the vehicle's speed, and writes the proxy's wanted velocity.

kind.doc:
`SCharacterAirMovementSettings`: the shared tuning block for the airborne movement families
 (parachute, wingsuit, and freefall). It covers the per-axis input/look yaw-pitch-roll mixing
 (`m_XInputYawPitchRollAmount`, `m_XLookYawPitchRollAmount`), the heading-to-velocity springs
 (`m_RotateCharYawToVelocity`), the camera-relative look steering (`m_LookSteer*`), the
 slingshot boost (`m_Slingshot*`), and the near-ground lift. The parachute and wingsuit settings
 embed one of these as their `m_AirControl`.

`SCharacterParachuteSettings`: the per-character parachute movement tuning block, embedded in
 `SCustomMovementSettings` alongside the other families' settings. The first fields are the
 angular motion limits and the reel-to-parachute transition; the rest is the shared
 [`CharacterAirMovementSettings`] used for the flight dynamics and the camera-relative look
 steering.
`SCharacterReelToParaSettings`: the settings for the reel-in-to-parachute transition.

`SCharacterRetractSShotSettings`: the settings for the parachute slingshot boost on reel-in
 retract.

`SCharacterSpring`: the per-axis spring tuning used throughout the air and parachute
 movement settings. A spring is expressed with `m_Constant` (the stiffness), `m_Damping`, and
 `m_Speed` (the per-second response); the air movement cores integrate the spring state per
 frame from these.

The input state task active while the character is parachuting. Delegates the per-frame
 movement to [`UpdateParachutePhysics`].

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Reads the parachute movement effectors (pitch/yaw inputs via the
 action map), calls [`UpdateParachutePhysics`] with the resulting input vector, then handles
 the cancel input that closes the parachute.

kind.doc:
`SParachuteActionParams`: the per-character parachute animation/physics state, embedded in
 `CCharacter` alongside the other movement families' action params. The four proxy matrices
 describe the parachute rig's pivot (the suspension point), the character, and the canopy, plus
 the blended steering proxy that interpolates between them; the floats track the parachute
 blend-in, bump timers, and the velocity-steering blend.

The input state task active while the character swims at the water surface. Unlike the on-foot
 locomotion family, the swim tasks do not route through
 [`NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterOrientation`](input::locomotion::NStateTask_LocoUtil::EvaluateCharacterOrientation)
 or the target-face-dir blackboard: body turning is dispatched as discrete animation acts, and
 the actual heading change is applied by the movement actuators below.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame update. Computes the camera-relative move direction (via
 `GameCameraManager::GetInputMatrix`) and, for the player, the direction to the aim-target
 position, then dispatches swim acts by the angle from the body forward
 ([`ControllerUtility::GetDeltaAngleFromOrientation`](input::controller_utility::ControllerUtility::GetDeltaAngleFromOrientation)):
 below [`SWIM_TURN_ACT_MIN_ANGLE`] the forward crawl-start act, from there up to
 [`SWIM_TURN_ACT_MAX_ANGLE`] the directional 120-degree turn acts
 (`ACT_SURFACE_SWIM_START_120R/L` while moving,
 `ACT_SURFACE_IDLE_QUICKTURN_120R/L` while idle and wielding a weapon, measured against the
 aim direction). When a turn is latched it writes the angle to the blackboard
 ([`SWIM_TURN_ANGLE_ID`](blackboard::ObjectBlackboard::SWIM_TURN_ANGLE_ID)) and stores the
 base/target direction pair in the character's swim action parameters for the actuator's
 segment-gated slerp. Also handles the surface-to-underwater dive transition (camera pitched
 down, sufficient depth, facing within 65 degrees of the move direction).

kind.doc:
The input state task active while the character swims underwater. Mirrors
 [`NStateTask_InputSurfaceSwimTask`]'s act dispatch, with `ACT_UW_SWIM_IDLE_TURN_120R/L` as the
 discrete turn acts and the surfacing transition in place of the dive.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc: The per-frame update.

kind.doc:
The movement actuator task for surface swimming; delegates to [`UpdateSurfaceMovement`] for the
 player and `UpdateSurfaceMovementNPC` otherwise.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc: The per-frame update.

kind.doc: The movement actuator task for underwater swimming; delegates to [`UpdateUnderwaterMovement`].

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc: The per-frame update.

kind.doc:
The fixed surface-swim facing turn rate (degrees per second) while aiming or planting
 explosives.
The upper bound (degrees) of the swim input tasks' turn-act angle range.

The absolute angle (degrees) from the body forward below which the swim input tasks queue the
 forward crawl-start act, and at or above which they queue a directional 120-degree turn act.

The factor the swim movement cores multiply a turn rate by to get degrees per second: the
 surface core scales the movement settings' swim slerp speeds by it, and the underwater core
 uses it as a fixed rate.
The landscape manager (`CLandscapeManager`). Opaque.

associated_functions.name: UpdatePatchSystem
associated_functions.doc:
Assembles the landscape patch system's cull frusta (see [`PatchFrustumId`] and
 [`PatchViewDesc::MAX_FRUSTUMS`]) from the occluder manager's main cull camera, the active
 shadow passes of the current frame parity, and the two reflective-shadow frusta, then runs
 the patch system update with them. Skipped unless the previous patch-system frame is
 complete or `force` is set.

kind.doc:
The argument block passed to a patch map's per-patch CPU update fragment. Partial: only the
 fields the base-terrain fragment ([`TerrainPatchUpdate`]) reads are mapped.

fields.name: m_ViewDesc
fields.doc: The view description for this update; see [`PatchViewDesc`].

fields.name: m_Header
fields.doc: The patch's header; see [`PatchHeader`].

fields.name: m_RenderBlock
fields.doc:
The patch's per-patch constant memory. For the base terrain maps this is the patch's
 `CRenderBlockTerrain` instance, constructed in place when the map was created.

fields.name: m_TypeContext
fields.doc:
The patch map's type context. For the terrain maps it is the render-pass pointer table the
 fragment submits into.

kind.doc:
The frustum ids `CLandscapeManager::UpdatePatchSystem` assigns to the entries of a landscape
 patch-system update ([`PatchViewDesc::m_FrustumIDs`]). The per-patch fragments route a patch to
 render passes by the id of each set [`PatchHeader::m_VisibilityBits`] bit.

variants.name: FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA
variants.doc: The occluder manager's main cull camera (entry 0); routes to the colour passes.

variants.name: FRUSTUM_ID_SHADOW_PASS_0
variants.doc:
The first shadow pass. Shadow pass `i` (for each active cascade of the current frame
 parity, at most eight) uses id `1 + i`, routing to the shadow passes.

variants.name: FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_0
variants.doc: The first reflective-shadow-map frustum.

variants.name: FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_1
variants.doc: The second reflective-shadow-map frustum.

variants.name: FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS
variants.doc:
A second run of the main cull camera (the final entry, sharing the main camera's cached
 BFBC parameters); routes to the depth prepass.

kind.doc:
A patch's bookkeeping header within a patch map (the Avalanche `patchsystem` dependency
 library's grid-of-patches streaming, used by the landscape systems: the base VolumetricTerrain
 patch maps `terrain_patch_lod9..12`, water, and vegetation). Partial: only the fields the
 terrain patch-update fragment reads are mapped.

fields.name: m_DynamicSize
fields.doc: The patch's dynamic memory size; reset to 0 when the patch finishes destruction.

fields.name: m_PatchX
fields.doc:
The patch's X coordinate in its map grid. The patch's world X derives as
 `(m_PatchX << m_Lod) + world_origin_x`, scaled by the world context's inverse XZ scale.

fields.name: m_PatchZ
fields.doc: The patch's Z coordinate in its map grid; see [`m_PatchX`](Self::m_PatchX).

fields.name: m_StatusBits
fields.doc: Patch lifecycle status bits (`EPatchSystemStatusBits`, the `STATUS_*` constants).

fields.name: m_UserState
fields.doc:
A per-patch state counter the patch's update fragment advances during multi-step
 construction or destruction.

fields.name: m_Lod
fields.doc:
The patch map's LOD level (9..=12 for the base terrain maps; the patch spans
 `1 << m_Lod` world units per side before world scaling).

fields.name: m_VisibilityBits
fields.doc:
Per-frustum visibility bits, written by the patch system's BFBC cull step each update: bit
 `i` is set when the patch's AABB passed the cull for frustum entry `i` of the update's view
 description ([`PatchViewDesc::m_FrustumIDs`] maps entries to frustum ids). For the landscape
 patch system entry 0, and so bit 0, is always the main cull camera
 ([`PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA`]); the last populated bit is its second run
 ([`PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS`]). The patch-update
 fragments read these to decide which render passes receive the patch's render block.

fields.name: m_BFBCOcludee
fields.doc:
The patch's BFBC occludee handle, allocated by `BFBCAdd` when the patch map is created; the
 patch's world AABB is pushed through `BFBCSetAABB` under this handle during construction.

kind.doc:
[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_CONSTRUCTED`): the patch
 is constructed.

[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit
 (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE`): construction has completed.

[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit
 (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_CONSTRUCTION_PENDING`): construction is pending.

[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit
 (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_DESTRUCTION_COMPLETE`): destruction has completed.

[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit
 (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_DESTRUCTION_PENDING`): destruction is pending.

[`m_StatusBits`](Self::m_StatusBits) bit (`PATCH_SYSTEM_STATUS_BIT_INSIDE_WORLD`): the patch
 lies inside the world.

The per-update view description handed to the patch-update fragments: the set of cull frusta
 the patch system's BFBC step ran this update. For the landscape patch system
 (`CLandscapeManager::UpdatePatchSystem`) the entries are: entry 0 = the occluder manager's main
 cull camera ([`FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA)), entries 1..=N
 = the active shadow cascades (the `FRUSTUM_ID_SHADOW_PASS_*` ids), then the two
 reflective-shadow frusta (the `FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_*` ids), and a final second run of
 the same main cull camera
 ([`FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS)); see
 [`PatchFrustumId`]. Partial mapping.

fields.name: m_FrustumIDs
fields.doc:
The frustum id for each entry, indexed by the same entry index as the patch's
 [`PatchHeader::m_VisibilityBits`] bit.

fields.name: m_FrustumCount
fields.doc: The number of frustum entries this update (also the number of populated visibility bits).

kind.doc:
The capacity of the frustum-entry arrays `CLandscapeManager::UpdatePatchSystem` fills: the
 main camera, up to eight shadow passes, two reflective-shadow frusta, and the second main
 camera run.

The [`UpdateTessellatedTriangles`] `metric_type` that derives tessellation from the camera's
 distance beyond the patch bounds. The name is descriptive; the engine uses a bare integer.

The [`UpdateTessellatedTriangles`] `metric_type` that compares each quad's metric against the
 squared `manual_metric_value`. The name is descriptive; the engine uses a bare integer.
A [`CastRayInfoBase`] that resolves the hit material on demand (`CCastRayInfo`).

associated_functions.name: GetHitMaterial
associated_functions.doc:
`CCastRayInfo::GetHitMaterial` (a virtual): the hit shape's game material
 (`EGameMaterialId`), looked up through the physics system's world.

kind.doc:
The result of a ray query (`CCastRayInfoBase`): the hit position, normal, and fraction, the hit
 body and instance, and the hit material's pass flags. Only the methods are bound.

associated_functions.name: Reset
associated_functions.doc: Clears the result for reuse.

associated_functions.name: DidHitBulletPassMaterial
associated_functions.doc:
Whether the hit material lets bullets pass
 ([`BULLET_PASS`](MaterialPassFlags::BULLET_PASS)); false for two special material ids.

kind.doc:
The Havok-facing input of a character proxy (`CPfxCharacterInstance::CCharacterInput`), read by
 the physics step to drive the proxy.

fields.name: gameControledVelocity
fields.doc:
Whether [`wantedVelocity`](Self::wantedVelocity) is game-controlled. The on-foot locomotion
 task sets it when it takes its velocity from the blackboard's code-driven path and clears it
 otherwise.

fields.name: wantedVelocity
fields.doc:
The velocity the proxy should move at (world space). The on-foot locomotion task
 (`NStateTask_MovementLocomotionTask::Update`) writes its solved velocity here every tick,
 including standing idle.

kind.doc: A [`RaycastFilter`] whose ignore mask is set pass by pass (`CIgnoreMaterialFlagFilter`).

associated_functions.name: Construct
associated_functions.doc:
`CRaycastFilter::CRaycastFilter`: constructs the filter with its two material masks, the
 instance to ignore (may be null), and the world (null selects [`PhysicsSystem::m_World`]).

associated_functions.name: SetIgnoreBulletPass
associated_functions.doc: Sets or clears [`BULLET_PASS`](MaterialPassFlags::BULLET_PASS) in the ignore mask.

associated_functions.name: SetIgnoreRayPass
associated_functions.doc: Sets or clears [`RAY_PASS`](MaterialPassFlags::RAY_PASS) in the ignore mask.

associated_functions.name: SetIgnoreCameraPass
associated_functions.doc: Sets or clears [`CAMERA_PASS`](MaterialPassFlags::CAMERA_PASS) in the ignore mask.

kind.doc:
Material pass bits of a [`RaycastFilter`]'s material masks. Game materials carry per-pass
 "holey" flags (a bullet passes foliage, a ray passes glass, and similar); a filter that sets a
 bit in its ignore mask does not stop at materials flagged for that pass.

flags.name: BULLET_PASS
flags.doc:
Materials a bullet passes through. Set by
 [`IgnoreMaterialFlagFilter::SetIgnoreBulletPass`].

flags.name: CAMERA_PASS
flags.doc:
Materials the camera passes through. Set by
 [`IgnoreMaterialFlagFilter::SetIgnoreCameraPass`].

flags.name: RAY_PASS
flags.doc: Materials a ray passes through. Set by [`IgnoreMaterialFlagFilter::SetIgnoreRayPass`].

kind.doc:
`CPfxCharacterInstance`: the character's physics-side body instance (the Havok character proxy),
 owned by `CCharacter` through a `boost::shared_ptr`. Only some members are bound.

fields.name: m_Input
fields.doc: The proxy input the physics step reads; see [`CharacterInput`].

fields.name: m_ProxyState
fields.doc:
The current proxy state (`CPfxCharacterInstance::EProxyState`), which selects the proxy's
 collision shape. Written by [`SetProxyState`](Self::SetProxyState).

fields.name: m_CharacterRigidBody
fields.doc:
The Havok character rigid body (`hknpCharacterRigidBody*`), which holds the body id that
 [`GetCharacterRigidBodyId`](Self::GetCharacterRigidBodyId) reads.

fields.name: m_CharacterRBListener
fields.doc: The character rigid-body listener (`CCustomCharacterRBListener*`).

fields.name: m_Owner
fields.doc:
The owning character (`IPfxCharacter*`). Its `GetSharedPfxCharacterSettings` virtual returns
 the shared settings that hold the per-state shape table.

associated_functions.name: SetOrientation
associated_functions.doc:
Sets the physics body's rotation from the rotation part of `m` (via a quaternion
 conversion) and zeroes the body's angular velocity; the translation part is ignored. The
 swim movement cores ([`UpdateSurfaceMovement`](input::swim::UpdateSurfaceMovement) and
 [`UpdateUnderwaterMovement`](input::swim::UpdateUnderwaterMovement)) apply their computed
 body orientation through this each update.

associated_functions.name: GetVelocity
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the physics body's current linear velocity (world space, 3 floats) via the body's
 Havok transform/velocity chain.

associated_functions.name: SetProxyState
associated_functions.doc:
Switches the proxy to `state` when it differs from [`m_ProxyState`](Self::m_ProxyState):
 stores it, fetches the shared settings through [`m_Owner`](Self::m_Owner), swaps the live
 body's shape to the settings' shape for that state ([`hknpWorld::setBodyShape`]), and
 copies the state's per-shape byte into the rigid-body listener
 ([`m_CharacterRBListener`](Self::m_CharacterRBListener)). The capsule
 dimensions live in those pre-built shapes.

associated_functions.name: GetCharacterRigidBodyId
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the Havok body id of [`m_CharacterRigidBody`](Self::m_CharacterRigidBody) to `out`
 ([`INVALID_BODY_ID`](Self::INVALID_BODY_ID) when there is no body) and returns `out`.

associated_functions.name: BuildDefaultCharacterContext
associated_functions.doc:
Builds the Havok character context for the proxy: a character-state manager with the
 on-ground, in-air, and jumping states registered. It does not set the capsule dimensions.

kind.doc:
Havok's invalid body id, which [`GetCharacterRigidBodyId`](Self::GetCharacterRigidBodyId)
 reports when there is no body.

The physics system (`CPhysicsSystem`), a `Base::CSingle` singleton that owns the Havok world and
 serves the engine's scene queries. The queries are sim-phase calls against the live Havok world.
 Only some members are bound.

fields.name: m_World
fields.doc: The Havok world.

associated_functions.name: CastRay
associated_functions.doc:
The general ray query: casts `ray` (world space, normalized direction) from `min_fraction`
 out to `max_distance` along its direction against collision `layer`, returning whether it
 hit. `info`, when non-null, receives the closest hit; `filter`, when non-null, replaces the
 default hit filter (and can exclude materials or an instance); `flags` is a
 collision-filter-info word, `0` for a plain query. Backed by [`hknpWorld::castRay`].

associated_functions.name: CastRaySimple
associated_functions.doc:
Whether the segment from `start` to `end` is blocked: builds the ray from the two points and
 calls [`CastRay`](Self::CastRay) with no hit info, the default filter, and
 [`QUERY_LAYER`](Self::QUERY_LAYER).

associated_functions.name: CastRayTerrain
associated_functions.doc: A ray query against the terrain only, with the parameters of [`CastRay`](Self::CastRay).

associated_functions.name: CastRayWaterSurface
associated_functions.doc:
Intersects the segment from `start` to `end` with the water surface, writing the hit point
 to `hit` and returning whether there was one.

associated_functions.name: CastSphere
associated_functions.doc:
Sweeps a sphere of `radius` from `start` to `end`, reporting hits to `collector` (an
 `hknpCollisionQueryCollector`).

associated_functions.name: CastShape
associated_functions.doc:
Sweeps an arbitrary Havok shape (`hknpShape*`) with the rotation `rotation` (`hkRotationf`)
 from `start` to `end`, reporting hits to `collector`.

kind.doc:
The collision layer [`CastRaySimple`](Self::CastRaySimple) hardcodes, and the one the
 player's direct-aim query passes to [`CastRay`](Self::CastRay).

`CPhysicsSystem::s_WaterQueryProxy`: the water query singleton buoyancy, water interaction,
 vehicle fin forces, and the water-surface ray query read water heights from.

The ragdoll's proxy phantom (`CRagdollProxyPhantom`), the shape set that stands in for a
 character's ragdoll bodies in hit tests. Only one method is bound.

associated_functions.name: GetHitNameHash
associated_functions.doc:
The name hash of the ragdoll part a ray hit (the hit's shape key matched against the
 phantom's shapes), or `0` when the hit is not one of them. `CCharacter::OnDamage` uses it to
 find the body part a hit struck.

kind.doc:
A ray (`CRay3`): an origin and a direction, both world space when passed to
 [`PhysicsSystem::CastRay`].

fields.name: Direction
fields.doc: The ray direction; the queries expect it normalized.

kind.doc:
The engine's closest-hit ray filter (`CRaycastFilter`, derived from Havok's
 `hknpClosestHitCollector`): collects the closest hit while skipping ignored materials and one
 ignored instance.

fields.name: m_IgnoreMaterialMask
fields.doc: Materials whose pass flags are in this mask do not count as hits.

fields.name: m_ForceMaterialMask
fields.doc: Materials whose pass flags are in this mask always count as hits.

fields.name: m_IgnorePfxInstance
fields.doc: An instance the query never hits (`IPfxInstance*`), such as the caster's own proxy.

fields.name: m_World
fields.doc:
The Havok world the filter resolves bodies in; the physics system's world when constructed
 with null.

associated_functions.name: Construct
associated_functions.doc:
`CRaycastFilter::CRaycastFilter`: constructs the filter with its two material masks, the
 instance to ignore (may be null), and the world (null selects [`PhysicsSystem::m_World`]).

kind.doc:
The water query interface (`CPhysicsSystem::IWaterProxy`) through which physics code reads
 water heights, reached through [`PhysicsSystem_s_WaterQueryProxy`]. Only the first slot is bound.

functions.name: GetWorldSeaLevel
functions.doc:
The world sea level, the height of the open-sea water plane.
 [`PhysicsSystem::CastRayWaterSurface`] tests a segment against it after the water boxes.

fields.name: GetWorldSeaLevel
fields.doc:
The world sea level, the height of the open-sea water plane.
 [`PhysicsSystem::CastRayWaterSurface`] tests a segment against it after the water boxes.

kind.doc: The Havok physics world (`hknpWorld`). Only some members are bound.

associated_functions.name: castRay
associated_functions.doc:
Casts a ray query (`hknpRayCastQuery`) and reports hits to `collector`
 (`hknpCollisionQueryCollector`).

associated_functions.name: setBodyShape
associated_functions.doc: Replaces the shape (`hknpShape*`) of the body `body_id` on the live world.

kind.doc:
`CProfileManager` (a `Base::CSingle` singleton): the player profile, including the upgrade
 table. Only the upgrade lookup is mapped.

associated_functions.name: GetUpgradeInfo
associated_functions.doc:
Binary-searches the upgrade table (sorted by id hash) for `id` and returns its
 [`UpgradeInfo`]. When the id is absent it returns a static, zero-initialized default entry,
 never null, so the purchased and enabled tests read false.

kind.doc:
`SUpgradeInfo`: one gear-mod upgrade's definition and state, as returned by
 `CProfileManager::GetUpgradeInfo`. Only the leading fields are mapped; the id hashes are stored
 bare. The profile manager's sorted table stores each one after its 8-byte key, at a
 0x128-byte stride.

fields.name: m_IsPurchased
fields.doc:
Whether the upgrade is purchased. Gameplay gates test it together with
 [`m_IsEnabled`](Self::m_IsEnabled).

fields.name: m_IsEnabled
fields.doc: Whether the player has the purchased upgrade switched on; set from the comm/skill UI.

kind.doc:
`CSlowMotionManager::s_NormalGameSpeed`: the game speed the slow-motion manager returns the
 clock to when no slow-motion effect is active. Initialized to `1.0`.

 `CSlowMotionManager::Update` (called once per frame from the special-effects update) writes
 [`Clock::m_UpdateSpeed`](clock::Clock::m_UpdateSpeed) every frame as a blend between this value
 and the active effect's game speed, weighted by the effect's eased status. Because the update
 rewrites the clock's speed every frame, this value, not the clock field, sets the normal clock
 rate, and scripted slow-motion effects (the wingsuit near-miss, the death camera, sequences)
 blend against it. `CSlowMotionManager::Reset` copies it straight into the clock.

 The game update divides frame deltas by the resulting clock speed where a real-time quantity
 is needed (health effects, camera collision, the run state's sub-step budget), and every other
 consumer of the clock's scaled delta simply runs slower.

One per-tag spawn budget entry. `CSpawnSystem::Update` iterates these each frame; when the live
 count exceeds the budget, the highest-despawn-rank object is despawned. Partial: only the budget

The maximum number of live objects for this spawn tag. When

kind.doc:
The completion callback for [`Spawn`](SpawnSystem::Spawn): a code pointer with the signature
 `void (*)(const std::vector<boost::shared_ptr<CGameObject>>* spawned_objects, void* userdata)`,
 invoked with the spawned objects and the caller's userdata once the request has been serviced.
 Modeled as a raw pointer because the definition language does not yet express function-pointer
 types.
`CSpawnSystem::CSpawnFactoryImpl`: the factory that vets and performs individual spawns.

associated_functions.name: CheckInternal
associated_functions.doc:
Vets a spawn of `resource` at `transform`: checks mission and encounter state, landscape
 physics residency, world-position validity, the despawn rank, the camera-visibility gate
 (a BFBC frustum test against the camera's box-frustum parameters), and a physics shape
 overlap. Returns whether the spawn may proceed.

kind.doc: An opaque `CSpawnSystem::SResourceDef`: one spawnable resource's definition.

The spawn system: manages streaming (de)spawn of dynamic objects around the player. Each
 frame, [`Update`](Self::Update) builds a BFBC cull frustum from the camera manager's active
 camera and uses it as a "don't (de)spawn while visible" gate in `CSpawnFactoryImpl::CheckInternal`, so
 objects are not spawned or despawned inside the player's view.

 Its resource definitions are loaded at startup from the per-pool spawn definition files
 (`settings/spawn_*_defs.bin`) referenced by `settings/spawn_budget_pools.bin`. Each budget pool
 (aircraft, animals, civilians, combatants, devices, props, road decorations, trains, vehicles,
 weapons, effects, and encounters) names a definition file, and each definition therein carries
 an exported-entity path (`.ee`), a space-separated tag string, a selection weight, and an
 optional debug-menu category. Spawn requests select definitions by matching tags, so the system
 governs the (de)spawn of every tag-addressable dynamic object, not only characters and
 vehicles. World geometry is placed by the location system instead and does not pass through
 here.

fields.name: m_BudgetEntries
fields.doc:
The per-tag spawn budget entries. Each entry tracks the max object count (budget), current
 count, and despawn-rank state for one spawn tag. When the count exceeds the budget, the
 highest-despawn-rank object is despawned.

 [`GetBFBCFrustumParamsForCameraAndTime`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::OccluderCollectionManager::GetBFBCFrustumParamsForCameraAndTime)
 against the active camera.

associated_functions.name: Update
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame spawn update: walks every resource definition, evaluates despawn ranks against the
 view position, and at its tail builds a BFBC cull frustum from the camera manager's active camera
 ([`CameraManager::m_ActiveCamera`](camera::camera_manager::CameraManager::m_ActiveCamera)) via
 [`GetBFBCFrustumParamsForCameraAndTime`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::OccluderCollectionManager::GetBFBCFrustumParamsForCameraAndTime),
 storing the result in [`m_SpawnBFBCParams`](Self::m_SpawnBFBCParams) and
 [`m_SpawnBFBCState`](Self::m_SpawnBFBCState) for the factory's visibility gate.

associated_functions.doc:
Sets the spawn center, view position, and view direction used by the visibility gate. Called
 once per frame by `CGameStateRun::UpdateCenterPosition` with the streaming center and the active
 camera's position and forward direction.

associated_functions.name: Spawn
associated_functions.doc:
Queues an asynchronous spawn request for the resource definitions matching the given tag
 string. Tags are separated by spaces, commas, or pipes; a definition matches when it
 carries every requested tag, and the matching set must belong to a single budget pool. The
 request creates a spawn factory, streams the selected definition's exported entity in if
 needed, and is serviced on a later frame by the spawn thread's update; on success the
 callback fires with the spawned objects and the given userdata. The transform is the
 world-space placement for the spawned object. `flags` is a combination of the
 `EFactoryFlags` constants ([`FF_DEFAULT`](Self::FF_DEFAULT) and friends) controlling which
 spawn checks apply. The callback may be null when the caller does not need the spawned
 objects.

kind.doc: `EFactoryFlags`: mark the spawn as an ambient spawn.
`EFactoryFlags`: automatically place a despawn block on the spawned object.
`EFactoryFlags`: run the debug-check variant of the spawn checks.
`EFactoryFlags`: mark the spawn as a debug spawn.

`EFactoryFlags` combination used for debug spawns (no despawn, line-of-sight,
 player-proximity, or time checks, no debug-loop check, and high-priority load).

`EFactoryFlags`: bypasses none of the spawn checks; the factory performs resource
 requesting, despawn, line-of-sight, player-proximity, spawn-block, time, spawn-pool,
 physics, and landscape checks as configured.
`EFactoryFlags`: stream the definition's resources at high priority.

`EFactoryFlags` combination used for black-market and other high-priority player-facing
 spawns (no despawn, line-of-sight, player-proximity, spawn-block, or time checks, premium
 content allowed, and high-priority load). `CInventory::SpawnSecondaryAttachObject` passes
 this for the player and [`FF_SECONDARY_SPAWN_CHECKS`](Self::FF_SECONDARY_SPAWN_CHECKS)
 otherwise.
`EFactoryFlags`: mark the spawn as mission critical, protecting it from despawn.
`EFactoryFlags`: do not count the spawn against its pool budget.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the spawn-loop debug check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the despawn check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the landscape (ground validity) check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the line-of-sight check that blocks spawning inside the player's view.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the active-physics-area check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the player-proximity check.
`EFactoryFlags`: do not request resource streaming; spawn only if already loaded.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the spawn-block volume check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the spawn-pool budget check.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip taking the system lock.
`EFactoryFlags`: skip the frame time-budget check.
`EFactoryFlags`: allow definitions flagged as premium content.
`EFactoryFlags`: allow definitions flagged as prototype content.

`EFactoryFlags` combination used for secondary attach-object spawns (no despawn,
 line-of-sight, player-proximity, spawn-block, or time checks).

`SUserVM::EContextBitFlag`: the index of a bit in the character's animation context-bit word,
 which game code sets to steer the animation graph. The values are unconfirmed.

`SUserVM::EStateBitFlag`: the index of a bit in the character's animation state-bit words, which
 state tasks in the animation graph set and clear and which game code and graph conditions read.
 Bit `n` lives in 64-bit word `n / 64` at bit `n % 64` (word 0 holds bits 0-63, word 1 bits
 64-127, and so on); the words are stored in
 [`UserVM`](character::control_parameters::UserVM). The values are confirmed at every bit an
 accessor tests: the one-bit predicates on
 [`Character`](character::character::Character) (wingsuit, parachute, free fall, fast fall,
 reeling in, motorbike, swimming, attached parachute, pre-reel, pre-hang), the grapple bits of
 `IsReeledIn` and `IsGrappleHanging`, the aim, drawing, holstering, and pause-aim-timer bits
 `HandleAimingInputNPC` tests, and `SB_DISABLE_SHOOT`. The other values are unconfirmed.

associated_functions.doc: Raw pointer to the row-major data, for passing to engine APIs.

associated_functions.name: as_mut_ptr
associated_functions.doc: Mutable raw pointer to the row-major data.

kind.doc:
The engine's 4x4 matrix, in the D3D convention: row-major storage with row vectors (a point is a
 row vector left-multiplied by the matrix, `clip = p * M`).

 The 16 floats are four rows; a world or camera transform's rows are its basis vectors:
 `data[0..2]` is right (+X), `data[4..6]` is up (+Y), `data[8..10]` is the +Z basis (so forward is
 `-data[8..10]`), and `data[12..14]` is the translation. Right-handed, Y-up.

associated_functions.name: as_ptr
associated_functions.doc: Raw pointer to the row-major data, for passing to engine APIs.

associated_functions.name: as_mut_ptr
associated_functions.doc: Mutable raw pointer to the row-major data.

associated_functions.name: Multiply4x4
associated_functions.doc:
The engine's 4x4 product, `result = a * b` (row-major: result row `i` is `a`'s row `i` times
 `b`). For example, `Multiply4x4(View, Proj, ViewProjection)` gives `VP = View * Proj` and
 `clip = p * View * Proj`. Static.

associated_functions.name: PerspectiveFovInverse
associated_functions.doc:
Builds the inverse of a symmetric perspective projection into `self` (also returned), from a
 vertical field of view, an aspect ratio, and the far and near planes. The screen-space
 reconstruction passes (SSR, deferred clustered lighting, SSAO, screen-space subsurface,
 atmospheric scattering, depth of field) call it to recover a clip-to-view basis, then multiply
 by the render context's camera transform to reach clip-to-world. Its `x`/`y` scale is diagonal
 (`[0][0] = aspect·tan(fov/2)`, `[1][1] = tan(fov/2)`) with no off-center shear, so it cannot
 represent an asymmetric frustum. Its depth block is **reverse-Z**, matching the reverse-Z depth
 buffer the engine renders: `[2][2] = 0`, `[2][3] = (far - near)/(far·near)`, `[3][2] = -1`, and
 `[3][3] = 1/far`, which reconstructs view depth from an NDC `z` of 1 at the near plane and 0 at
 the far plane.

associated_functions.name: CreateOrientation
associated_functions.doc:
Builds a look-at orientation into `self` (also returned): the direction is
 `normalize(eye_pos - at_pos)`, and the basis is completed from `up_dir` by the private
 `CMatrix4f::Orientate`, with `eye_pos` as the translation.

kind.doc: The identity matrix; identical under either the row-major or the column-major reading.
All elements zero.

associated_functions.name: Lerp
associated_functions.doc: Linearly interpolates `self` toward `other` in place: `self += (other - self) * weight`.

kind.doc:
The engine's world up axis, `(0, 1, 0)` (`CVector3f::UP`). `CRenderEngine::SetGlobalShaderConstants`

 (`_Bx`), then the length (`_Mysize`) and capacity (`_Myres`). The string is stored inline in

associated_functions.name: Release

A display object's presentation state, read and written through
 [`ValueObjectInterface::GetDisplayInfo`] / [`SetDisplayInfo`](ValueObjectInterface::SetDisplayInfo).

A `GFx::MouseEvent` (a `GFx::Event` with the mouse payload): the argument
 `CUIManager::SendMouseEvents` builds for [`MovieImpl::HandleEvent`]. `x` and `y` are in
 movie-viewport pixels: window-client pixels minus the centering offset
 `(cached viewport size - movie rectangle size) / 2`, i.e. relative to the top-left corner of
 the centered movie rectangle (see
 [`UIManager::m_MovieScaleWidth`](ui::ui_manager::UIManager::m_MovieScaleWidth)).

fields.name: ScrollDelta
fields.doc:
The wheel amount in Flash line units; the engine sends `lZ / 120 * 3` from the DirectInput
 mouse's z axis.

fields.name: Button
fields.doc:
The button index for down/up events: [`BUTTON_LEFT`](Self::BUTTON_LEFT) or
 [`BUTTON_RIGHT`](Self::BUTTON_RIGHT).

A Scaleform `GFx::MouseState`: one tracked mouse's per-movie state
 ([`MovieImpl::MouseStates`]). `MouseState::UpdateState` fills it while
 [`MovieImpl::ProcessInput`] drains the input-events queue during `Advance`: it copies
 [`CurButtonsState`](Self::CurButtonsState) into
 [`PrevButtonsState`](Self::PrevButtonsState), applies the entry's button/wheel payload,
 sets or clears [`FLAG_MOUSE_MOVED`](Self::FLAG_MOUSE_MOVED) by integer-comparing the
 entry's position against [`LastPosition`](Self::LastPosition), and stores the entry's
 position. `MovieImpl::ProcessMouse` then hit-tests the display tree at that stored position
 directly (`GetTopMostEntity` recurses with each display object's own local transforms) -- no
 further viewport, view-scale, or flag-dependent transform runs between the queue and the hit
 test.

fields.name: TopmostEntity
fields.doc:
`WeakPtr<InteractiveObject>`: the entity under the cursor (the hover target), written
 during `ProcessInput` via `MouseState::SetTopmostEntity`.

fields.name: PrevTopmostEntity
fields.doc: `WeakPtr<InteractiveObject>`: the previous hover target.

fields.name: ActiveEntity
fields.doc: `WeakPtr<InteractiveObject>`: the entity that received the last button press.

fields.name: MouseButtonDownEntities
fields.doc:
`ArrayLH<WeakPtr<InteractiveObject>>` (`{data, size, capacity}`): the per-button press
 targets.

fields.name: CurButtonsState
fields.doc:
The current button bitmask (`MOUSE_BUTTON_*` bits), as last applied from the queue. [`MovieImpl::NotifyMouseState`] diffs its `buttons` argument against this when
 queueing.

fields.name: PrevButtonsState
fields.doc: The button bitmask before the last processed queue entry.

fields.name: LastPosition
fields.doc:
The mouse position in stage twips (`Render::Point<float>`): the authoritative position
 hit-testing uses, i.e. the queued output of the
 [`ViewportMatrix`](MovieImpl::ViewportMatrix)-inverse transform once `Advance` has
 drained the queue. Divide by 20 for stage pixels. Between a
 [`NotifyMouseState`](MovieImpl::NotifyMouseState) call and the next `Advance`, the new
 position exists only in the input-events queue; this field still holds the previous one.

fields.name: PresetCursorType
fields.doc: The cursor type forced via `MovieImpl::ChangeMouseCursorType`, if any.

fields.name: CursorType
fields.doc: The current cursor type.

fields.name: WheelDelta
fields.doc: The wheel delta of the last processed queue entry (zero when it carried no wheel bit).

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc: The `FLAG_*` state bits.

The Scaleform AS3 `MovieRoot` (the `ASMovieRootBase` interface), which `CUIManager::m_Movie`
 points at. The engine drives the movie through this interface's virtuals; the bound
 [`SetVariable`](Self::SetVariable) / [`GetVariable`](Self::GetVariable) /
 [`Invoke`](Self::Invoke) are its concrete implementations. The vtable is `MovieRoot`'s at
 [`VFTABLE`](Self::VFTABLE).

fields.name: pMovieImpl
fields.doc:
The backing `GFx::MovieImpl` (`GetDisplayObjectsTree` reads `pMovieImpl->pMainMovie`
 through it).

associated_functions.name: GetDisplayObjectsTreeImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The `AS3::MovieRoot` implementation of the
 [`GetDisplayObjectsTree`](Self::GetDisplayObjectsTree) virtual: allocates the root
 [`AmpMovieObjectDesc`] from `heap`, names it after the root movie clip, and fills its
 children through `DisplayObjContainer::GetChildDescTree`. Returns null without a root clip.

associated_functions.name: SetVariable
associated_functions.doc:
Sets an AS3 variable by clip path. The path is a dot-separated string like
 `"MCI_hud.MCI_poi_stage._visible"`, resolved from the root timeline. `set_var_type` (one of
 [`SV_NORMAL`](Self::SV_NORMAL), [`SV_STICKY`](Self::SV_STICKY), and
 [`SV_PERMANENT`](Self::SV_PERMANENT)) controls persistence across clip re-creation. Call on
 the capture (game update) thread.

associated_functions.name: GetVariable
associated_functions.doc:
Reads an AS3 variable by clip path into a [`Value`]. Returns false if the path is not
 found. A returned managed value (display object, string) must be released through the
 movie's object interface; plain bool/int/number values need no cleanup.

associated_functions.name: Invoke
associated_functions.doc:
Invokes an AS3 method on the movie's root timeline by name. This is the call path used by
 the engine's `CUIBase::Invoke`. The `args` are a `GFx::Value` array; `result` receives the
 return value (or null). Note the parameter order: `result` comes *before* `args`, unlike
 the engine's `CUIBase::Invoke` wrapper (which also adds a timeout).

functions.name: GetDisplayObjectsTree
functions.doc:
Recursively walks the runtime display tree from the root movie clip: returns a tree of
 [`AmpMovieObjectDesc`] nodes, each carrying the clip's instance name (or `"Unnamed"`)
 and a child array, calling `DisplayObject::GetName` on every child and recursing into
 containers. `heap` is the Scaleform `MemoryHeap*` used for the allocations (e.g.
 [`MovieImpl::pHeap`]); the tree is freed by releasing the root node. The implementation
 is [`GetDisplayObjectsTreeImpl`](Self::GetDisplayObjectsTreeImpl). Call on the capture
 (game update) thread, where the display tree is stable.

kind.doc:
The [`SetVariable`](Self::SetVariable) `set_var_type` (`GFx::Movie::SetVarType`) for a
 plain assignment with no persistence across clip re-creation.
The `set_var_type` that keeps the value for the life of the movie.
The `set_var_type` that re-applies the value when the clip is re-created.

The `AS3::MovieRoot` vtable address (the `ASMovieRootBase` layout, which holds
 [`GetDisplayObjectsTree`](Self::GetDisplayObjectsTree) and the virtuals whose
 implementations are the bound SetVariable/GetVariable/Invoke).

The `GFx::MovieImpl` behind [`UIManager::m_Movie`](ui::ui_manager::UIManager::m_Movie): the
 `GFx::Movie` instance. The rendering-side virtuals live on its own vtable; the AS3 side
 (SetVariable, Invoke, the display tree) lives on [`pASMovieRoot`](Self::pASMovieRoot).

fields.name: pASMovieRoot
fields.doc: The AS3 `MovieRoot` (the [`Movie`] interface): SetVariable, Invoke, and the display tree.

fields.name: pObjectInterface
fields.doc:
The `GFx::Value::ObjectInterface` for this movie: the dispatcher every `GFx::Value`
 display-object/member operation goes through.

fields.name: pHeap
fields.doc: The Scaleform [`MemoryHeap`] the movie allocates from.

fields.name: pMainMovieDef
fields.doc:
The main `MovieDefImpl`. [`UpdateViewport`](Self::UpdateViewport) reads the stage
 frame rectangle (twips) through it; while null, the view scale and offset reset to
 identity.

fields.name: pMainMovie
fields.doc: The root `DisplayObjContainer` (the main movie clip).

fields.name: pRenderRoot
fields.doc:
The movie's render-tree root ([`TreeRoot`]): the entry `CUIManager::Render` draws via the
 display handle. The whole display tree's render nodes hang off it.

fields.name: Viewport
fields.doc:
The movie's current [`Viewport`], as last copied in by
 [`SetViewportImpl`](Self::SetViewportImpl). [`TreeRoot::SetViewport`] takes it
 directly (copying the `Render::Viewport` prefix).

fields.name: PixelScale
fields.doc:
The larger of `1 / ViewScaleX` and `1 / ViewScaleY`, recomputed by
 [`UpdateViewport`](Self::UpdateViewport) (0.005 when a scale is zero).

fields.name: ViewScaleX
fields.doc:
The stage-pixel to view-rectangle-pixel scale on X, derived from
 [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode) by [`UpdateViewport`](Self::UpdateViewport)
 (for `SM_SHOW_ALL`/`SM_NO_BORDER`, the visible-frame to view-rectangle ratio).

fields.name: ViewScaleY
fields.doc: See [`ViewScaleX`](Self::ViewScaleX).

fields.name: ViewOffsetX
fields.doc: [`VisibleFrameRect`](Self::VisibleFrameRect) `x1` in stage pixels (`x1 / 20`).

fields.name: ViewOffsetY
fields.doc: [`VisibleFrameRect`](Self::VisibleFrameRect) `y1` in stage pixels (`y1 / 20`).

fields.name: ViewScaleMode
fields.doc:
The `SM_*` stage scale mode. Constructed as [`SM_SHOW_ALL`](Self::SM_SHOW_ALL); the
 engine never changes it on the main UI movie (`CRenderToTextureUI`/`CDynUI` set it on
 their own movies).

fields.name: ViewAlignment
fields.doc:
The `Align_*` stage alignment used by the `SM_NO_SCALE` mode. Constructed as
 [`ALIGN_CENTER`](Self::ALIGN_CENTER).

fields.name: VisibleFrameRect
fields.doc:
The stage region mapped onto the view rectangle, in twips (`x1, y1, x2, y2`), computed by
 [`UpdateViewport`](Self::UpdateViewport) from the [`Viewport`](Self::Viewport),
 the stage frame rectangle, and the [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode). Under
 `SM_SHOW_ALL` with a view rectangle matching the stage aspect, this is the whole stage.

fields.name: ViewportMatrix
fields.doc:
The stage-to-viewport matrix (`Matrix2x4<float>`, rows `[sx, shx, shy, tx]` and
 `[shx, sy, shy, ty]`; in practice `sx` at `[0]`, `tx` at `[3]`, `sy` at `[5]`, and `ty` at
 `[7]`) the movie sets on [`pRenderRoot`](Self::pRenderRoot) via `TreeNode::SetMatrix`
 whenever the viewport changes. Built by
 [`ResetViewportMatrix`](Self::ResetViewportMatrix) as `sx = Viewport.Width /
 (VisibleFrameRect.x2 - VisibleFrameRect.x1)`, `tx = -VisibleFrameRect.x1 * sx` (and
 likewise for Y), mapping stage twips to pixels relative to the view rectangle's top-left
 corner -- `Viewport.Left`/`Top` are *not* part of the matrix.

 This same matrix, inverted, is the entire mouse-to-stage transform:
 [`HandleEvent`](Self::HandleEvent) and
 [`NotifyMouseState`](Self::NotifyMouseState) run incoming positions through
 `TransformByInverse` before queueing, so mouse coordinates are expected in view-rectangle
 pixels (`stage_twips = (pos - t) / s` per axis).

fields.name: MouseStates
fields.doc:
The tracked mice ([`MouseState`] per index; the engine's main UI movie uses only index
 0). The array ends exactly at [`MouseCursorCount`](Self::MouseCursorCount).

fields.name: MouseCursorCount
fields.doc:
The number of mouse cursors the movie tracks (see
 [`SetMouseCursorCount`](Self::SetMouseCursorCount)); mouse input with an index at or
 beyond it is dropped.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
The movie's `FLAG_*` state bits (`MovieImpl::Flags`), among them
 [`FLAG_NEED_MOUSE_UPDATE`](Self::FLAG_NEED_MOUSE_UPDATE).

fields.name: RenderContext
fields.doc:
The movie's embedded `Render::Context` (the snapshot pipeline: active/pending/displaying
 snapshots, the capture locks, and the once-a-frame consumption latch).

associated_functions.name: CaptureImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The concrete implementation behind the [`Capture`](Self::Capture) virtual: gates on `Context::HasChanges` when `if_changed` is set, suspends the GC, and
 runs `Render::Context::Capture` to publish the frame's display-tree changes as the pending
 snapshot. `CUIManager::PreRender` calls it right after `Advance`, on the game update
 thread with the deferred render lock held -- the only point in the frame where every
 display-tree writer is quiescent.

associated_functions.name: HandleEventImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The concrete implementation behind [`HandleEvent`](Self::HandleEvent). For mouse move/down/up/wheel events it transforms the event's position by the
 inverse of [`ViewportMatrix`](Self::ViewportMatrix) (view-rectangle pixels to stage
 twips) and queues the result on the input-events queue; nothing is stored raw. The next
 `Advance` drains the queue into AS3 mouse processing.

associated_functions.name: NotifyMouseStateImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The concrete implementation behind [`NotifyMouseState`](Self::NotifyMouseState). Transforms `(x, y)` by the inverse of
 [`ViewportMatrix`](Self::ViewportMatrix), queues a mouse move at the resulting stage
 position (twips), then diffs `buttons` against the tracked per-mouse button state and
 queues a button event per changed bit.

associated_functions.name: SetViewportImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The concrete implementation behind the `SetViewport` virtual. When `desc` differs from
 [`Viewport`](Self::Viewport) (a memcmp over the whole [`Viewport`]), copies
 it in, runs [`UpdateViewport`](Self::UpdateViewport), and pushes the new state to the
 render tree ([`TreeRoot::SetViewport`], background color, and `TreeNode::SetMatrix` with
 [`ViewportMatrix`](Self::ViewportMatrix) on [`pRenderRoot`](Self::pRenderRoot)).

associated_functions.name: UpdateViewport
associated_functions.doc:
Recomputes [`VisibleFrameRect`](Self::VisibleFrameRect), the view scales and offsets,
 and [`PixelScale`](Self::PixelScale) from [`Viewport`](Self::Viewport), the
 stage frame rectangle, and [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode), then calls
 [`ResetViewportMatrix`](Self::ResetViewportMatrix). Called only from
 [`SetViewportImpl`](Self::SetViewportImpl); nothing engine-side recomputes the
 viewport per frame.

associated_functions.name: ResetViewportMatrix
associated_functions.doc:
Rebuilds [`ViewportMatrix`](Self::ViewportMatrix) from
 [`Viewport`](Self::Viewport) `Width`/`Height` and
 [`VisibleFrameRect`](Self::VisibleFrameRect) (see the matrix field for the formula).
 Does not push the matrix to the render tree.

associated_functions.name: ProcessInput
associated_functions.doc:
Drains the input-events queue during `Advance`: keyboard entries go to focus handling,
 mouse entries to `ProcessMouse` (which runs `MouseState::UpdateState` and hit-tests the
 display tree at the entry's stage-twips position). Afterwards, for any tracked mouse that
 saw no entry this drain while [`FLAG_NEED_MOUSE_UPDATE`](Self::FLAG_NEED_MOUSE_UPDATE) is
 set and the mouse is [`FLAG_ACTIVATED`](MouseState::FLAG_ACTIVATED), re-resolves the hover
 target from [`MouseState::LastPosition`].

associated_functions.name: GetMouseStateImpl
associated_functions.doc: The concrete implementation behind [`GetMouseState`](Self::GetMouseState).

associated_functions.name: HitTestImpl
associated_functions.doc: The concrete implementation behind [`HitTest`](Self::HitTest).

functions.name: Advance
functions.doc:
Advances the movie by `delta_t` seconds: processes queued
 input, runs the timeline and AS3 frame, and, when `capture` is set, finishes with
 [`CaptureImpl`](Self::CaptureImpl). Returns the time until the next frame is due.

functions.name: Capture
functions.doc:
Snapshots the display tree for the render thread. Must be
 called from the current capture thread (see
 [`SetCaptureThread`](Self::SetCaptureThread)); `if_changed = false` forces a fresh
 snapshot. The next [`NextCapture`](RTHandle::NextCapture) on the render side picks it up.

functions.name: GetDisplayHandle
functions.doc:
Returns the movie's display handle: the pinned
 `DisplayHandle<TreeRoot>` whose `pData` the renderer copies (with an `AddRef`) into a
 stack [`RTHandle`] before consuming the frame's capture.

functions.name: SetCaptureThread
functions.doc:
Reassigns which thread owns the capture. The engine hands
 ownership between the update thread and the render thread this way
 (`RenderOffScreenTextures` does exactly this per frame).

functions.name: ShutdownRendering
functions.doc:
Shuts down the movie's render context: a thunk into
 `Render::ContextImpl::Context::Shutdown` on the embedded
 [`RenderContext`](Self::RenderContext). `wait`
 blocks until the render thread has released the context.

functions.name: HandleEvent
functions.doc:
Routes a `GFx::Event` to the movie. For a
 [`MouseEvent`] the movie records the new mouse state, which the next `Advance`
 processes into AS3 mouse events (hover, press, release). Call on the capture (game
 update) thread. `CUIManager::SendMouseEvents` is the engine's only mouse feeder, and
 only emits a move event on frames where the DirectInput mouse reported a non-zero
 delta.

functions.name: GetMouseState
functions.doc:
Reads one mouse's current state: the position comes
 from [`MouseStates`](Self::MouseStates)`[mouse_index].LastPosition` converted to
 view-rectangle pixels (`(twips * 0.05 - ViewOffset) / ViewScale` per axis, the
 same space [`NotifyMouseState`](Self::NotifyMouseState) takes), and `buttons`
 from [`CurButtonsState`](MouseState::CurButtonsState). Out pointers may be null; a
 `mouse_index` at or beyond [`MouseCursorCount`](Self::MouseCursorCount) leaves
 them untouched.

functions.name: NotifyMouseState
functions.doc:
Directly overwrites one mouse's state: position in
 movie-viewport pixels (the same space as [`MouseEvent`]) plus a button bitmask
 ([`MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT`](MouseState::MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT) and
 [`MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT`](MouseState::MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT)), bypassing the event objects. Processed on the next `Advance`, like
 [`HandleEvent`](Self::HandleEvent).

functions.name: HitTest
functions.doc:
Hit-tests the display tree at a point in view-rectangle pixels: transforms by the inverse of
 [`ViewportMatrix`](Self::ViewportMatrix), then tests each root level's shapes.
 `test_cond` is one of the `HIT_TEST_*` constants, such as
 [`HIT_TEST_SHAPES`](Self::HIT_TEST_SHAPES).

functions.name: SetMouseCursorCount
functions.doc:
Sets how many mice the movie tracks; `0` disables mouse
 processing entirely. `CUIManager::RestoreAfterReset` sets `1` when a DirectInput mouse
 device exists and `0` otherwise.

functions.name: GetHeap
functions.doc: Returns the movie's memory heap, [`pHeap`](Self::pHeap).

kind.doc:
The [`ViewAlignment`](Self::ViewAlignment) that centres the stage (`Align_Center`), the
 constructor default.

The [`Flags`](Self::Flags) bit (`Flag_NeedMouseUpdate`) marking mouse state pending
 re-resolution; [`ProcessInput`](Self::ProcessInput) tests and clears it.
The [`HitTest`](Self::HitTest) `test_cond` (`GFx::Movie::HitTestType`) that tests bounds.
The `test_cond` that tests for button events from `controller_idx`.
The `test_cond` that tests shapes.
The `test_cond` that tests shapes, counting invisible ones.

The [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode) that stretches the stage to the view
 rectangle exactly, ignoring aspect.

The [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode) that fills the view rectangle, preserving
 aspect (cropping as needed).

The [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode) that maps the movie 1:1 at
 [`Viewport::Scale`] with no stretching (the view rectangle crops or pads the stage).

The [`ViewScaleMode`](Self::ViewScaleMode) that fits the whole stage inside the view
 rectangle, preserving aspect (letterboxing as needed). The constructor default.
