kind.doc:
A Scaleform AS3 object (the managed payload behind a display-object [`Value::mValue`]): its type
 [`m_Traits`](Self::m_Traits) classify it, and for a display object its
 [`m_DisplayObject`](Self::m_DisplayObject) is the presentation-side [`DisplayObjectBase`].

fields.name: m_Traits
fields.doc:
The object's type traits (class metadata), used to check it really is a display object
 before reaching [`m_DisplayObject`](Self::m_DisplayObject).

fields.name: m_DisplayObject
fields.doc:
The presentation-side display object, valid once [`m_Traits`](Self::m_Traits) confirm a
 display-object kind.

kind.doc:
A stack `Render::ContextImpl::RTHandle` over a copied
 [`DisplayHandle::pData`] (AddRef'd first, destructed after use).

fields.name: pData
fields.doc: The shared, refcounted handle data.

associated_functions.name: NextCapture
associated_functions.doc:
Consumes the context's pending snapshot into the displaying one (at most once per HAL
 frame: the context's [`NextCaptureCalledInFrame`](ui::scaleform::RenderContext::NextCaptureCalledInFrame)
 latch short-circuits repeats). Returns whether the handle is valid to draw. `notify` is
 the HAL's context notify ([`RenderHAL::GetContextNotify`]); `frame_id` is 0.

associated_functions.name: GetRenderEntry
associated_functions.doc: The handle's root entry in the current displaying snapshot, for `HAL::Draw`.

associated_functions.name: Destruct
associated_functions.doc: The RTHandle destructor (releases the handle data).

kind.doc:
Scaleform [`RefCountImpl`] -- the base class for reference-counted Scaleform objects. Provides
 a vtable pointer and an atomic [`ref_count`](Self::ref_count). `AddRef`/`Release` are
 non-virtual; the virtual [`destructor`](Self::destructor) runs when the refcount reaches zero.

fields.name: ref_count
fields.doc: Atomic reference count. Incremented by `AddRef`, decremented by `Release`.

associated_functions.name: AddRef
associated_functions.doc: Increments the reference count atomically.

associated_functions.name: Release
associated_functions.doc:
Decrements the reference count atomically. When it reaches zero, calls the virtual
 [`destructor`](Self::destructor).

functions.name: destructor
functions.doc: Virtual destructor. Called by `Release` when the refcount reaches zero.

fields.name: destructor
fields.doc: Virtual destructor. Called by `Release` when the refcount reaches zero.

kind.doc:
The Scaleform `Render::ContextImpl::Context`: the display-tree snapshot pipeline between the
 update thread and the renderer. `Capture` (update thread) merges the active snapshot's changes
 into the pending snapshot; [`NextCapture`](RTHandle::NextCapture) (render thread) consumes the pending
 snapshot into the displaying one, at most once per HAL frame. Only some fields are modeled;
 the declared size covers only the modeled prefix.

fields.name: NextCaptureCalledInFrame
fields.doc:
The once-a-frame consumption latch: while set, [`NextCapture`](RTHandle::NextCapture) keeps the current
 displaying snapshot instead of consuming the pending one. Set by the first `NextCapture`
 of a HAL frame and cleared by `HAL::EndFrame` (`EndFrameContextNotify`), so within one
 `CUIManager::Render` call every draw sees the same snapshot.

fields.name: SnapshotFrameIds
fields.doc:
The per-slot snapshot frame ids, indexed like `pSnapshots`: `[0]` the active snapshot
 (incremented by every `Capture`), `[1]` pending, `[2]` displaying, `[3]` finalizing. The
 gap between `[0]` and `[2]` is how far the displayed UI trails the update thread -- a
 growing gap means the render side is not consuming captures.

associated_functions.name: CreateEntryTreeRoot
associated_functions.doc:
Creates a fresh [`TreeRoot`] entry in this context (`Context::CreateEntry<TreeRoot>`):
 allocates its `NodeData` from the context heap and registers the entry. The root starts
 parentless with no viewport; [`TreeRoot::SetViewport`] sets its viewport and
 [`TreeNode::SetMatrix`] its stage matrix. Call on the capture (game update) thread.

associated_functions.name: CreateEntryTreeContainer
associated_functions.doc:
Creates a fresh empty [`TreeContainer`] entry in this context
 (`Context::CreateEntry<TreeContainer>`). Call on the capture (game update) thread.

kind.doc:
The Scaleform `Render::D3D1x::HAL` behind `CUIManager::m_RenderHAL`: the D3D11 rendering
 backend the UI render worker draws through.

fields.name: pDevice
fields.doc: The `ID3D11Device` the HAL was initialized with.

fields.name: pDeviceContext
fields.doc:
The `ID3D11DeviceContext` every HAL draw goes through (possibly a deferred context; see
 the HAL's `UsingDeferredContext` flag). Work recorded on it from the UI render worker is
 ordered with the HAL's own draws.

associated_functions.name: CreateRenderTarget
associated_functions.doc:
Builds a [`RenderTarget`] from D3D color/depth views (`ID3D11RenderTargetView*` /
 `ID3D11DepthStencilView*`); the concrete implementation behind the `CreateRenderTarget`
 virtual.
 `RenderOffScreenTextures` creates one per off-screen draw and releases it afterwards.
 Render thread only.

associated_functions.name: Draw
associated_functions.doc:
Draws a [`TreeRoot`]'s displaying-snapshot subtree into the bound target
 (`Scaleform::Render::HAL::Draw`). Render thread only, within `BeginFrame`/`BeginScene`.

functions.name: SetRenderTarget
functions.doc:
Binds `target` as the frame's display render target. `CUIManager::Render`
 calls it with `m_RenderBuffer` before `BeginFrame`, paired with a trailing
 [`PopRenderTarget`](Self::PopRenderTarget).

functions.name: PushRenderTarget
functions.doc:
Pushes `target` for nested rendering within a frame, as
 `RenderOffScreenTextures` does per off-screen movie. `frame_rect` is `[x0, y0, x1,
 y1]` floats; `clear_color` points at a packed color (0 = transparent).

functions.name: PopRenderTarget
functions.doc: Pops the pushed (or set) render target.

functions.name: BeginFrame
functions.doc:
Begins the HAL frame. `EndFrame` clears every context's once-a-frame
 consumption latch via `EndFrameContextNotify`.

functions.name: EndFrame
functions.doc: Ends the HAL frame.

functions.name: BeginScene
functions.doc: Begins a scene (draw batch) within the frame.

functions.name: EndScene
functions.doc: Ends the scene.

functions.name: GetContextNotify
functions.doc:
The HAL's `Render::ContextImpl::RenderNotify`, passed to
 [`RTHandle::NextCapture`].

fields.name: SetRenderTarget
fields.doc:
Binds `target` as the frame's display render target. `CUIManager::Render`
 calls it with `m_RenderBuffer` before `BeginFrame`, paired with a trailing
 [`PopRenderTarget`](Self::PopRenderTarget).

fields.name: PushRenderTarget
fields.doc:
Pushes `target` for nested rendering within a frame, as
 `RenderOffScreenTextures` does per off-screen movie. `frame_rect` is `[x0, y0, x1,
 y1]` floats; `clear_color` points at a packed color (0 = transparent).

fields.name: PopRenderTarget
fields.doc: Pops the pushed (or set) render target.

fields.name: BeginFrame
fields.doc:
Begins the HAL frame. `EndFrame` clears every context's once-a-frame
 consumption latch via `EndFrameContextNotify`.

fields.name: EndFrame
fields.doc: Ends the HAL frame.

fields.name: BeginScene
fields.doc: Begins a scene (draw batch) within the frame.

fields.name: EndScene
fields.doc: Ends the scene.

fields.name: GetContextNotify
fields.doc:
The HAL's `Render::ContextImpl::RenderNotify`, passed to
 [`RTHandle::NextCapture`].

kind.doc:
A Scaleform `Render::RenderTarget`: the target wrapper `SetRenderTarget`/`PushRenderTarget`
 take. `RenderOffScreenTextures` creates one per draw from D3D views
 ([`RenderHAL::CreateRenderTarget`]) and releases it after the pop.

functions.name: Release
functions.doc: Releases the target (refcounted).

fields.name: Release
fields.doc: Releases the target (refcounted).

kind.doc:
Static clip names placed on the root timeline of `ui/hud.gfx` via PlaceObject2 tags. The root
 movie (`ui/root.gfx`) creates its clips entirely through ActionScript, so it has no static
 PlaceObject2 tags; `hud.gfx` uses a mix of static placement and dynamic creation.

 | Instance name | Depth | Char ID |
 |---|---|---|
 | `MCI_hud` | 1432 | 1548 |
 | `MCI_poi_stage` | 180 | 1066 |
 | `MCI_weapon_selection_wheel` | 182 | 1078 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_center` | 1 | 1065 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_top_left` | 839 | 1538 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_top_middle` | 636 | 1532 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_top_right` | 562 | 1395 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_bottom_left` | 450 | 1330 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_bottom_middle` | 307 | 1286 |
 | `MCI_safe_area_bottom_right` | 246 | 1161 |

 UI movie registry from `root.gfx` maps each `CUIBase` subclass to its `.gfx` file:
 `CSharedLibUI` -> `shared_lib`, `COverlayUI` -> `overlay`, `CHUDUI` -> `hud`, `CIntroUI` ->
 `intro`, `CTitleUI` -> `title`, `CPauseUI` -> `pause`, `CTutorialsUI` -> `tutorials`,
 `CCreditsUI` -> `credits`, `CLobbyUI` -> `lobby`, `CMainUI` -> `main`, `CCommLinkUI` ->
 `comm_link`, `CCommCollectiblesUI` -> `comm_collectibles`, `CCommCommunityUI` ->
 `comm_community`, `CCommMapUI` -> `comm_map`, `CCommSkillUI` -> `comm_skill`,
 `CCommStatsUI` -> `comm_stats`, `CCommBragsFeatsUI` -> `comm_brags_feats`,
 `CCommStoreUI` -> `comm_store`, `CRewardUI` -> `reward`, `CROMUI` -> (none).

The heap data descriptor behind a `Scaleform::String`: an allocated size and a refcount,
 followed by the NUL-terminated character data. Reached from the string's pointer after masking
 off the heap flags ([`HEAP_FLAGS_MASK`](Self::HEAP_FLAGS_MASK)).

fields.name: Size
fields.doc: The allocated size.

fields.name: RefCount
fields.doc: The reference count.

fields.name: m_Data
fields.doc: The first character of the NUL-terminated string data.

associated_functions.name: as_ptr
associated_functions.doc: A pointer to the NUL-terminated character data.

kind.doc: The low bits of a `Scaleform::String` pointer that carry heap flags rather than address.

A Scaleform AS3 object's type traits: the class metadata identifying an [`Object`]'s kind. The
 display-object type-id range and flag values are hard-coded magic in the engine too (the same
 constants appear inline in `Value::ObjectInterface::GetDisplayInfo`); their deeper AS3-builtin-type
 meaning is not recoverable from the stripped Scaleform code, so they are named here by role.

fields.name: m_Flags
fields.doc: Trait flags; see [`FLAG_NON_DISPLAY_OBJECT`](Self::FLAG_NON_DISPLAY_OBJECT).

fields.name: m_TypeId
fields.doc: The traits' AS3 builtin-class type id; see [`is_display_object`](Self::is_display_object).

associated_functions.name: is_display_object
associated_functions.doc:
Whether these traits identify a display object -- the guard `GetDisplayInfo` performs before
 reaching an [`Object`](Object)'s [`DisplayObjectBase`](DisplayObjectBase): a
 [`m_TypeId`](Self::m_TypeId) in the display-object range and without the
 [`FLAG_NON_DISPLAY_OBJECT`](Self::FLAG_NON_DISPLAY_OBJECT) flag.

kind.doc:
The number of type ids in the display-object range (so display objects are
 `FIRST..FIRST + COUNT`).
The first [`m_TypeId`](Self::m_TypeId) of the display-object AS3 builtin-class range.
A [`m_Flags`](Self::m_Flags) bit marking a kind excluded from the display-object check.

A render-tree container node (`Render::TreeContainer`): a [`TreeNode`] whose `NodeData` holds
 a child `TreeNodeArray`. The display side mirrors every `DisplayObjContainer` into one, and
 addresses children by cached numeric index (`GFx::DisplayList`'s `TreeIndex`), so removing a
 child without the display list's knowledge shifts its siblings out of step with their cached
 indices.

associated_functions.name: Insert
associated_functions.doc:
Inserts `node` at `index`, recording
 [`CHANGE_CHILD_INSERT`](TreeNode::CHANGE_CHILD_INSERT): refcounts the node, sets its
 [`pParent`](TreeNode::pParent), and propagates. Capture (game update) thread only.

associated_functions.name: Remove
associated_functions.doc:
Removes `count` children starting at `index`, recording
 [`CHANGE_CHILD_REMOVE`](TreeNode::CHANGE_CHILD_REMOVE): nulls each child's
 [`pParent`](TreeNode::pParent) and drops its refcount (destroying it at zero). Capture
 (game update) thread only.

associated_functions.name: GetAt
associated_functions.doc: The child at `index` of the active snapshot's child array, or null out of range.

associated_functions.name: GetSize
associated_functions.doc: The active snapshot's child count.

kind.doc:
A Scaleform render-tree node: a `Render::ContextImpl::Entry` (a slot in a 0x1000-aligned entry
 page) whose per-snapshot `NodeData` carries the transform, visibility, and bounds.
 [`TreeContainer`] and [`TreeRoot`] share this header; a pointer to either casts to this
 freely. Each write to an entry's `NodeData` records a `Render::TreeChangeConstants` change
 bit (`Change_*`) on the entry.

fields.name: RefCount
fields.doc:
The entry's reference count. [`TreeContainer::Insert`] increments it and
 [`TreeContainer::Remove`] decrements it (destroying the entry at zero), so a node moved
 between containers without an extra count held across the remove is destroyed.

fields.name: pNative
fields.doc: The displaying-snapshot `EntryData` the renderer reads (low bit carries a flag).

fields.name: pRenderer
fields.doc: The renderer's `TreeCacheNode` for this entry, once drawn.

fields.name: pParent
fields.doc:
The parent container entry, or null while detached. [`TreeContainer::Remove`] nulls it;
 a null parent on a node the display side owned means the display list dropped it.

associated_functions.name: SetMatrix
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the node's 2D transform (`Matrix2x4<float>`, 8 floats) through the entry-change
 protocol. Call on the capture (game update) thread.

associated_functions.name: DestroyHelper
associated_functions.doc:
Destroys the entry (`Entry::destroyHelper`): queues its `NodeData` on the context's
 destroyed-nodes list (freed at the next capture) and frees the slot. Call only when
 [`RefCount`](Self::RefCount) reached zero, on the capture (game update) thread.

kind.doc: The change bit for a child insertion (`Change_ChildInsert`).
The change bit for a child removal (`Change_ChildRemove`).
The change bit for a viewport write (`Change_Viewport`).

A render-tree root (`Render::TreeRoot`): a [`TreeContainer`] whose `NodeData` adds the
 viewport and background color. `HAL::Draw` takes one; the engine draws several per frame
 through the same HAL (the UI movie, the off-screen movies, the debug text).

associated_functions.name: SetViewport
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the root's viewport, recording [`CHANGE_VIEWPORT`](TreeNode::CHANGE_VIEWPORT) only
 when the viewport differs. `viewport` is a [`Viewport`] (e.g. [`MovieImpl::Viewport`]);
 the `Render::Viewport` prefix, up to and including [`Flags`](Viewport::Flags), is copied.
 Capture (game update) thread only.

kind.doc:
A Scaleform `GFx::Value`: the tagged union the AS3 interface traffics in. Starts with a
 `ListNode<Value>` (managed values are tracked on the movie's `ExternalObjRefs` list); a
 stack-constructed unmanaged value leaves the list pointers and
 [`pObjectInterface`](Self::pObjectInterface) null.

fields.name: pPrev
fields.doc: `ListNode<Value>::pPrev`; null for unmanaged values.

fields.name: pNext
fields.doc: `ListNode<Value>::pNext`; null for unmanaged values.

fields.name: pObjectInterface
fields.doc: The owning movie's object interface; null for unmanaged values.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: The `ValueType` tag, possibly with `VTC_*` control bits (so not modeled as an enum).

fields.name: mValue
fields.doc:
The value union: `bool` / `i32` / `u32` / `f64` / `*const c_char` / object pointer,
 selected by [`Type`](Self::Type).

fields.name: DataAux
fields.doc: Auxiliary data (e.g. the closure's user pointer).

associated_functions.name: value_type
associated_functions.doc:
The base `VT_*` value-type tag, with the `VTC_*` control bits masked off. The `as_*` accessors
 compare it against the `VT_*` tags.

kind.doc:
The managed bit: set on values owned by the movie (which must be released through the
 object interface, never constructed by hand).

The type tag for a boolean value ([`mValue`](Self::mValue) carries the `bool` in its
 first byte).
The type tag for a display-object value (managed; owned by the movie).
The type tag for an int value.
The type tag for a number (f64) value.
The type tag for a string value (`mValue` is a `*const c_char`).

The mask isolating the base `VT_*` value-type tag in [`Type`](Self::Type) from the `VTC_*`
 control bits (the game compares `Type & VT_TYPE_MASK` against the `VT_*` tags).

The `GFx::Value::ObjectInterface`: the dispatcher for operations on managed values (display
 objects, arrays). One per movie ([`MovieImpl::pObjectInterface`]); a managed [`Value`] carries
 its owning interface in [`Value::pObjectInterface`].

associated_functions.name: GetDisplayInfo
associated_functions.doc:
Reads a display object's [`DisplayInfo`] (position, scale, alpha, visibility). `data` is the
 value's [`mValue`](Value::mValue) payload. Returns false when the value is not a display
 object.

associated_functions.name: SetDisplayInfo
associated_functions.doc:
Writes the `DisplayInfo` fields selected by [`DisplayInfo::VarsSet`] directly at the
 display-object level -- no AVM path resolution and no AS3 property setters.
 `CHUDUI::UpdatePOIs` drives POI positions and visibility through it every frame.

associated_functions.name: ObjectRelease
associated_functions.doc:
Releases a managed value: unlinks it from the movie's external-references list and drops
 the AS3 object reference. Call on the capture thread. `data` is the value's
 [`mValue`](Value::mValue) payload.

kind.doc:
A Scaleform `GFx::Viewport` (a `Render::Viewport` plus `Scale` and `AspectRatio`): the
 description [`MovieImpl::SetViewportImpl`] copies into [`MovieImpl::Viewport`]. `BufferWidth`
 and `BufferHeight` describe the whole output surface; `Left`/`Top`/`Width`/`Height` are the
 view rectangle the movie occupies within it. `CUIManager::SetMovieViewport` builds one as
 `{BufferWidth: vw, BufferHeight: vh, Left: (vw - movie_w) / 2, Top: (vh - movie_h) / 2,
 Width: movie_w, Height: movie_h, Scissor*: 0, Flags: 0, Scale: 1.0, AspectRatio: 1.0}`, where
 `movie_w`/`movie_h` are [`m_MovieScaleWidth`](ui::ui_manager::UIManager::m_MovieScaleWidth)/`Height` at call time (not the
 arguments).

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
`View_*` flags, among them [`VIEW_IS_RENDER_TEXTURE`](Self::VIEW_IS_RENDER_TEXTURE),
 [`VIEW_USE_SCISSOR_RECT`](Self::VIEW_USE_SCISSOR_RECT), and the
 [`VIEW_ORIENTATION_MASK`](Self::VIEW_ORIENTATION_MASK) bits.

fields.name: Scale
fields.doc: The view scale used by the `SM_NO_SCALE` mode; every engine caller passes 1.0.

fields.name: AspectRatio
fields.doc:
The pixel aspect used as an extra horizontal factor by [`MovieImpl::UpdateViewport`];
 every engine caller passes 1.0.

kind.doc: The [`Flags`](Self::Flags) bit for a render-texture target (`View_IsRenderTexture`).
The [`Flags`](Self::Flags) mask for the orientation (`View_Orientation_Mask`).

The [`Flags`](Self::Flags) bit that enables the scissor rectangle
 (`View_UseScissorRect`).

A Scaleform render buffer: what [`UIManager::m_RenderBuffer`] points at. It holds the
 render-target and depth-stencil views the UI HAL renders into; [`UpdateData`](Self::UpdateData)
 rebinds those views, and is not tied to startup.

fields.name: m_BufferWidth
fields.doc:
The render-target buffer width. [`InitPlatformRT`](UIManager::InitPlatformRT) builds the
 buffer square, setting width = height = its side argument.

fields.name: m_BufferHeight
fields.doc:
The render-target buffer height; [`InitPlatformRT`](UIManager::InitPlatformRT) sets it equal to
 the width (a square buffer).

fields.name: m_ViewRectRight
fields.doc: The view rectangle's right edge (x2 = width).

fields.name: m_ViewRectBottom
fields.doc:
The view rectangle's bottom edge (y2); [`InitPlatformRT`](UIManager::InitPlatformRT) sets it
 equal to the width.

associated_functions.name: UpdateData
associated_functions.doc:
Rebinds the buffer's views, releasing the old ones and adding a reference to the new. `self`
 is the render buffer itself ([`UIManager::m_RenderBuffer`]); the call reaches its inner
 view-holder internally. Passing `depth` as null leaves the depth buffer unchanged.

kind.doc:
The screen-position code returned by the UI world-to-screen and marker placement: on-screen, an
 off-screen clamped edge or corner, off-screen in front (no clamp), or off-screen behind.

The Scaleform-backed UI manager, the single concrete instance behind `IUIManager`. It renders the
 HUD into the engine surface. [`InitPlatformRT`](Self::InitPlatformRT) builds its render
 buffer, [`ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`](Self::ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize) sizes the movie
 render rectangle, [`SetMovieViewport`](Self::SetMovieViewport) sets the Scaleform movie
 viewport, and [`ComputeSafeArea`](Self::ComputeSafeArea) derives the UI safe area.

fields.name: m_MouseDeltaX
fields.doc:
The horizontal mouse letterbox offset from the engine's `MovieScaleInfo`
 (`m_MouseDeltaX`), in movie-viewport pixels.
 [`GetMovieSpaceMouseCursor`](Self::GetMovieSpaceMouseCursor) maps a movie-viewport
 mouse position into stage coordinates as `(pos - delta) * scale`.
 [`ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`](Self::ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize) writes it: always
 zero today (only the non-clipping path computes a non-trivial
 [`m_MouseDeltaY`](Self::m_MouseDeltaY)).

fields.name: m_MouseDeltaY
fields.doc:
The vertical mouse letterbox offset from the engine's `MovieScaleInfo` (`m_MouseDeltaY`),
 in movie-viewport pixels. In `ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`'s non-clipping path it is half
 the vertical letterbox, `(movie height - stage height * movie width / stage width) / 2`;
 in the clipping path it is zero.

fields.name: m_MouseScaleFac
fields.doc:
The movie-viewport-pixels-to-stage-coordinates mouse scale from the engine's
 `MovieScaleInfo` (`m_MouseScaleFac`): `stage width / movie rectangle width` in the
 non-clipping path of `ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`, `1.0` in the clipping path.

fields.name: m_MovieScaleWidth
fields.doc:
The movie render rectangle's width, from the engine's `MovieScaleInfo`. The movie is rendered
 into a `m_MovieScaleWidth` x `m_MovieScaleHeight` rectangle, centered within the viewport
 passed to [`SetMovieViewport`](Self::SetMovieViewport).
 [`ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`](Self::ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize) recomputes it from the
 device resolution and the movie stage size.

fields.name: m_MovieScaleHeight
fields.doc: The movie render rectangle's height; see [`m_MovieScaleWidth`](Self::m_MovieScaleWidth).

fields.name: m_CurrentCaptureThread
fields.doc:
The id of the thread that currently owns the Scaleform capture (`m_CurrentCaptureThread`);
 `PreRender` claims it for the update thread each frame via `CUIManager::SetCaptureThread`,
 which writes this field and the movie's capture thread together. `CUIBase::Invoke` runs the
 AVM immediately only when the calling thread matches this field, and queues into the UI's
 command queue otherwise. It does not consult the movie's own capture thread: if the movie's
 capture thread changes without this field, game-thread invokes still run immediately and
 mutate the display list concurrently with the new capture owner.

fields.name: m_MouseX
fields.doc:
The last mouse position's x, in window-client pixels. [`WndProc`] writes it on every
 `WM_MOUSEMOVE` via [`SetMousePos`](Self::SetMousePos) -- the only writer, so the OS
 message stream is the sole source of the UI mouse position (the DirectInput mouse device
 only contributes deltas, buttons, and the wheel).

fields.name: m_MouseY
fields.doc:
The last mouse position's y, in window-client pixels; see
 [`m_MouseX`](Self::m_MouseX).

fields.name: m_GrabScreenTimer
fields.doc:
The grab-screen timer (seconds); `CHUDUI::OnOmniDamage` sets it to
 [`OMNI_DAMAGE_GRAB_SCREEN_TIME`](ui::hud_ui::HUDUI::OMNI_DAMAGE_GRAB_SCREEN_TIME).

fields.name: m_RenderReady
fields.doc:
Whether the render system is initialized. One of the three gates `Render` checks before
 drawing.

fields.name: m_RenderActive
fields.doc: Whether rendering is active (cleared during device resets). The second `Render` gate.

fields.name: m_Steering
fields.doc:
The active `CSteering`, whose action map [`SendMouseEvents`](Self::SendMouseEvents)
 polls for the mouse-button actions ([`MOUSE1`](input::input_action_map::Action::MOUSE1) and
 [`MOUSE2`](input::input_action_map::Action::MOUSE2)).

fields.name: m_DeferredRenderLock
fields.doc:
The lock serializing the UI update (`PreRender`: `Advance` + `Capture`) against the UI
 render (`Render`, `RenderOffScreenTextures`). A Win32 critical section, so re-entrant on
 the owning thread.

fields.name: m_Loader
fields.doc:
The Scaleform `GFx::Loader`, created in `InitializeSystem`. Loads `.gfx` files via
 `Loader::CreateMovie`.

fields.name: m_MovieDef
fields.doc: The `GFx::MovieDef` for `ui/root.gfx` -- the definition object, not the live instance.

fields.name: m_Movie
fields.doc:
The live `GFx::Movie` instance (a [`MovieImpl`]), created by `MovieDef::CreateInstance` in
 `InitializeSystem`. All `CUIBase` subclasses share this single movie. The AS3 side (the
 [`Movie`](ui::scaleform::Movie) interface: SetVariable, Invoke, the display tree) hangs off
 [`MovieImpl::pASMovieRoot`].

fields.name: m_RenderHAL
fields.doc: The Scaleform `Render::D3D1x::HAL` the UI render worker draws through.

fields.name: m_ThreadCommandQueue
fields.doc:
The UI render worker's command queue; `Render` executes it (and stamps its
 [`m_RenderThreadId`](UiThreadCommandQueue::m_RenderThreadId)) at the top of every call.

fields.name: m_TextureManager
fields.doc:
The Scaleform `D3D1x::TextureManager`; `Render` stamps its
 [`RenderThreadId`](UITextureManager::RenderThreadId) at the top of every call.

fields.name: m_RenderBuffer
fields.doc:
The Scaleform render buffer the UI HAL renders into, set up by
 [`InitPlatformRT`](Self::InitPlatformRT). [`RenderTargetData::UpdateData`] rebinds which
 views it renders into.

fields.name: m_IsUsingGamepad
fields.doc:
Whether the player is currently driving the UI with a gamepad. While set,
 [`SendMouseEvents`](Self::SendMouseEvents) parks the Scaleform mouse at
 [`GAMEPAD_PARKED_MOUSE_POSITION`](Self::GAMEPAD_PARKED_MOUSE_POSITION) on both axes and [`MousePointerVisibility`](Self::MousePointerVisibility) hides
 the overlay cursor.

fields.name: m_RenderingEnabled
fields.doc: The third `Render` gate: whether UI rendering is enabled at all.

fields.name: m_CachedStageWidth
fields.doc:
The movie stage's authored width (`m_CachedStageSize.x`), refreshed every frame from the loaded
 movie. The world-to-screen mapping ([`Convert3DCoords`](Self::Convert3DCoords)) maps NDC
 into this.

fields.name: m_CachedStageHeight
fields.doc: The movie stage's authored height; see [`m_CachedStageWidth`](Self::m_CachedStageWidth).

fields.name: m_CachedViewportWidth
fields.doc:
The cached viewport width (`m_CachedViewportSize.x`), refreshed every frame from the graphics
 device's display resolution. [`ComputeSafeArea`](Self::ComputeSafeArea) reads it to expand
 the UI safe area to the viewport's aspect.

fields.name: m_CachedViewportHeight
fields.doc: The cached viewport height; see [`m_CachedViewportWidth`](Self::m_CachedViewportWidth).

fields.name: m_CachedViewportRatio
fields.doc:
The cached viewport aspect ratio (`m_CachedViewportSize.y / .x`, i.e. device height / width),
 refreshed every frame from the graphics device. [`Convert3DCoords`](Self::Convert3DCoords)
 uses it -- not the width/height fields -- to aspect-correct world-to-screen.

associated_functions.name: RenderImpl
associated_functions.doc:
The UI render: takes [`m_DeferredRenderLock`](Self::m_DeferredRenderLock), checks the
 three render gates, retargets the Scaleform render-thread ids, drains the thread command
 queue, binds the display render target, and draws the movie's latest captured display tree
 (`GetDisplayHandle` -> `RTHandle::NextCapture` -> `HAL::Draw`) within a
 `BeginFrame`/`BeginScene` pair. Runs on a CPU-fragment worker (kicked by `StartRender`,
 joined by `SyncRender`).

associated_functions.name: InitPlatformRT
associated_functions.doc:
Binds the UI render target: builds a [`RenderTargetData`] from the engine surface's
 render-target and depth-stencil views via [`RenderTargetData::UpdateData`]. Called at startup
 and on every device or resolution reset; `a2` carries the target side length (the buffer is
 square: width = height = a2). This only creates the render buffer -- the Scaleform movie's
 viewport is set separately by [`SetMovieViewport`](Self::SetMovieViewport).

associated_functions.name: RestoreAfterResetImpl
associated_functions.doc:
Re-runs [`InitPlatformRT`](Self::InitPlatformRT) after a device or resolution reset. Also
 recomputes the movie size, sets the movie viewport, and recomputes the safe area. Gated by an
 internal reset counter: it does nothing unless the counter is at 1.

associated_functions.name: ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize
associated_functions.doc:
Recomputes the movie render rectangle ([`m_MovieScaleWidth`](Self::m_MovieScaleWidth) /
 [`m_MovieScaleHeight`](Self::m_MovieScaleHeight)). It first refreshes the cached stage and
 viewport sizes from the live device resolution (via an internal `UpdateCachedValues`), then
 sizes the movie rectangle from them, so the rectangle always reflects the device aspect.

associated_functions.name: SetMovieViewport
associated_functions.doc:
Sets the Scaleform movie's viewport to `width` x `height`, centering the movie (of size
 [`m_MovieScaleWidth`](Self::m_MovieScaleWidth) x
 [`m_MovieScaleHeight`](Self::m_MovieScaleHeight)) within it at offset
 `((width - m_MovieScaleWidth) / 2, (height - m_MovieScaleHeight) / 2)`. This is the viewport the
 Scaleform HAL renders into.

associated_functions.name: ComputeSafeArea
associated_functions.doc: Computes the safe-area rectangle from the current movie viewport.

associated_functions.name: ComputeGameViewArea
associated_functions.doc: Computes the game view area from the current movie viewport.

associated_functions.name: Convert3DCoords
associated_functions.doc:
World-to-screen: projects `world` through `vp`, divides by w, aspect-corrects, and maps NDC to
 pixels. Returns false when the point is behind the camera.

associated_functions.name: Convert3DCoordsDefault
associated_functions.doc:
The default-VP world-to-screen wrapper `CHUDUI::UpdateGrappleReticle` uses for the grapple
 reticle (its only callers): fetches the render camera's view-projection internally and
 forwards to [`Convert3DCoords`](Self::Convert3DCoords).

associated_functions.name: Get2DInfo
associated_functions.doc:
Marker placement: [`Convert3DCoords`](Self::Convert3DCoords) with the supplied `vp`, plus
 an on-screen test and an off-screen edge-clamp via [`ClampToScreen`](Self::ClampToScreen).
 Gameplay markers route through here.

associated_functions.name: ClampToScreen
associated_functions.doc:
Clamps an off-screen point to the screen-rect edge or corner and sets the position code.
 Static.

associated_functions.name: StartRenderImpl
associated_functions.doc: Begins the UI render job, posting to the async render thread.

associated_functions.name: SyncRenderImpl
associated_functions.doc: A barrier that spin-waits until the async UI render job has finished.

associated_functions.name: SubmitImpl
associated_functions.doc: The final commit: submits the render HAL's output under a graphics scoped lock.

associated_functions.name: RenderStaticBackGroundImpl
associated_functions.doc: Draws the pause / menu static background.

associated_functions.name: RenderOffScreenTexturesImpl
associated_functions.doc: Renders Scaleform UI to offscreen textures for in-world screens. This is not the HUD.

associated_functions.name: IsUsingStaticBackGround
associated_functions.doc: Whether a static background is being shown.

associated_functions.name: PreUpdate
associated_functions.doc:
The per-frame UI input step: computes gamepad use, runs
 [`MousePointerVisibility`](Self::MousePointerVisibility), dispatches the
 highest-input-priority `CUIBase`'s input management, then calls
 [`SendMouseEvents`](Self::SendMouseEvents) and drains the queued key events.

associated_functions.name: SetMousePos
associated_functions.doc:
Stores a window-client-pixel mouse position into [`m_MouseX`](Self::m_MouseX) /
 [`m_MouseY`](Self::m_MouseY) and immediately runs
 [`SendMouseEvents`](Self::SendMouseEvents). Called by `WndProc` on `WM_MOUSEMOVE`
 with the `lParam` client coordinates.

associated_functions.name: GetMousePos
associated_functions.doc: Reads back [`m_MouseX`](Self::m_MouseX) / [`m_MouseY`](Self::m_MouseY).

associated_functions.name: SendMouseEvents
associated_functions.doc:
Feeds the frame's mouse state to the Scaleform movie. Converts
 [`m_MouseX`](Self::m_MouseX) / [`m_MouseY`](Self::m_MouseY) to movie-viewport
 pixels by subtracting the centering offset
 `(m_CachedViewportSize - m_MovieScale size) / 2`, then sends
 [`MouseEvent`](ui::scaleform::MouseEvent)s through
 [`MovieImpl::HandleEvent`](ui::scaleform::MovieImpl::HandleEvent): a move event only when
 the DirectInput mouse reported a non-zero x or y delta this frame (also repositioning the
 overlay cursor sprite via `COverlayUI::SetMouseCursorPosition`), a wheel event from the z
 delta, and down/up events from the steering action map's
 [`MOUSE1`](input::input_action_map::Action::MOUSE1) /
 [`MOUSE2`](input::input_action_map::Action::MOUSE2) effector states
 ([`Clicked`](input::input_action_map::EffectorState::Clicked) for the pressed edge,
 [`Released`](input::input_action_map::EffectorState::Released) for the released edge). When
 [`m_IsUsingGamepad`](Self::m_IsUsingGamepad) is set it instead parks the mouse at
 [`GAMEPAD_PARKED_MOUSE_POSITION`](Self::GAMEPAD_PARKED_MOUSE_POSITION) on both axes. Returns false without the movie, the steering, or a mouse device.

associated_functions.name: GetMovieSpaceMouseCursor
associated_functions.doc:
Maps a movie-viewport-pixel mouse position into movie stage coordinates:
 `out = (pos - m_MouseDelta) * m_MouseScaleFac` per axis (see
 [`m_MouseDeltaX`](Self::m_MouseDeltaX)).

associated_functions.name: MousePointerVisibility
associated_functions.doc:
Shows or hides the overlay mouse cursor from the frame's UI state: visible only when the
 overlay UI is active, no gamepad is in use, and no cursor-hiding HUD state or message box
 applies (via `COverlayUI::ShowMouseCursor` / `HideMouseCursor`).

associated_functions.name: UpdateCachedValues
associated_functions.doc:
Refreshes [`m_CachedStageWidth`](Self::m_CachedStageWidth) /
 [`m_CachedStageHeight`](Self::m_CachedStageHeight) from the loaded movie and
 [`m_CachedViewportWidth`](Self::m_CachedViewportWidth) /
 [`m_CachedViewportHeight`](Self::m_CachedViewportHeight) /
 [`m_CachedViewportRatio`](Self::m_CachedViewportRatio) from the graphics device.
 First step of [`ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize`](Self::ComputeMovieSizeOnViewSize).
