kind.doc:
A vehicle seat identifier (`NVehicle::ESeat`): an index into [`Vehicle::m_Seats`], with the
 seat categories laid out in bands (driver, passengers, gunners, stunt positions, scripted).

variants.name: ENoSeatIdentifier
variants.doc: No seat: returned by [`Vehicle::GetSeat`] for a character that is not seated in the vehicle.

kind.doc:
A vehicle (`CVehicle`). Like other game objects it carries its `CGameObject` base at the same
 offset as a character does
 ([`Character::GAME_OBJECT_BASE_OFFSET`](character::character::Character::GAME_OBJECT_BASE_OFFSET)),
 and the vtable there serves RTTI and the transform virtuals. Only some members are bound.

fields.name: m_Seats
fields.doc: The vehicle's seats, indexed by [`Seat`].

fields.name: m_LocalPlayerSeat
fields.doc:
The seat the local player occupies, or [`Seat::ENoSeatIdentifier`]. The game's input
 contexts test it against [`Seat::EDriverSeat`] to decide whether driver controls apply.

fields.name: m_AimingTargetPosition
fields.doc:
The world-space point the vehicle's weapons aim at, written by
 [`SetAimTargetPosition`](Self::SetAimTargetPosition).

fields.name: m_AIVehicleWeaponAimTimeout
fields.doc:
How long, in seconds, AI-controlled vehicle weapons keep an externally supplied aim target.
 [`SetAimTargetPosition`](Self::SetAimTargetPosition) sets it to `-1` when the local player
 drives and to `2` otherwise.

fields.name: m_PfxVehicle
fields.doc:
The vehicle's physics body (`CPfxVehicle*`). [`IsMech`](Self::IsMech) tests its strafing
 wheel-steering controller.

fields.name: m_VehicleTypeNameHash
fields.doc:
The hash of the vehicle's type name (`HashString` of names such as
 `v1706_boat_na_rocketboat`), compared by [`IsRocketBoat`](Self::IsRocketBoat).

associated_functions.name: SetAimTargetPosition
associated_functions.doc:
Sets [`m_AimingTargetPosition`](Self::m_AimingTargetPosition) and refreshes
 [`m_AIVehicleWeaponAimTimeout`](Self::m_AIVehicleWeaponAimTimeout).

associated_functions.name: GetSeat
associated_functions.doc:
Returns the seat `character` occupies: the index of the seat whose graph node is the
 character's current interaction-graph node, or [`Seat::ENoSeatIdentifier`].

associated_functions.name: IsMech
associated_functions.doc: Whether the vehicle is a mech: its physics body has a strafing wheel-steering controller.

associated_functions.name: TeleportVehicle
associated_functions.doc:
Moves the vehicle to `transform` directly (through the `CGameObject` transform setter),
 invalidates its collision caches, and detaches any player grapple wire attached to it.
 Seated characters follow through their attachment.

associated_functions.name: GetWeaponTurretCurrentYawAngle
associated_functions.doc:
The current yaw angle of the vehicle's weapon turret, read from the powered hinge controller
 of the turret part; `0` when the vehicle has no turret.

associated_functions.name: IsRocketBoat
associated_functions.doc:
Whether the vehicle is the rocket boat: [`m_VehicleTypeNameHash`](Self::m_VehicleTypeNameHash)
 equals the hash of `v1706_boat_na_rocketboat` (computed once and cached). The sea-vehicle
 input, water-contact, and player action contexts use it. IDA labels this address
 `CWeaponBase::MarkNextWeaponComponentForFire`, but every caller passes a vehicle; the name
 here is descriptive.

kind.doc: The number of entries in [`m_Seats`](Self::m_Seats).

One seat of a vehicle (`CVehicle::CSeat`). It is interaction-graph metadata (the graph node the
 seated character occupies, the door slot, the window part, and whether the player may use it)
 and carries no transform: a seated character's pose comes from its own attach bone and offset.

fields.name: m_GraphNode
fields.doc:
The interaction-graph node a character occupies while in this seat.
 [`Vehicle::GetSeat`] matches a character's current node against it.

kind.doc:
The engine's vehicle classification (`NVehicle::EVehicleType`), stored on a vehicle as
 `CVehicle::m_VehicleType` and returned by `CVehicle::GetVehicleType`, which is inlined at every
 use in this build. Jetskis classify as [`EBOAT`](Self::EBOAT). The field's offset is not mapped.

The water patch manager (`CWaterPatchManager`, a `Base::CSingle` singleton): owns the water
 reflection pipeline (the distant backdrop, atmosphere, cloud, mesh, and distant-light
 reflection passes, their dedicated reflection camera, and the distant/full reflection
 textures), the top-down foam and wake textures, and the CPU-side wave table, and drives the
 per-frame WaveWorks simulation step via `DoWaveWorksSimulation` from the game update.

fields.name: m_ReflectionCamera
fields.doc:
The camera the water reflection passes render from. `UpdateThread` rebuilds its transform
 each frame by mirroring the active camera across the water plane, and
 `UpdateReflectionCamera` copies the active camera's FOV, near, far, and aspect onto it; the
 reflection pre-passes (`PRE_RP_REFLECTION_PRE` through `PRE_RP_REFLECTION_POST`) then draw
 the mirrored backdrop, atmosphere, clouds, meshes, and distant lights from it into the
 distant/full reflection textures.

fields.name: m_EnableScreenSpaceWaterReflection
fields.doc:
Whether the water uses the screen-space water reflection path. When set,
 `CNvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw` re-binds the water's fragment reflection slot to the
 distant (backdrop) reflection texture in place of the full reflection texture, and
 `CNvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Setup` bakes the flag into the fragment constants for the
 shader's reflection-path select.

functions.name: AIMechFireGravityGun
functions.doc:
A behavior-tree action callback (`AIMechFireGravityGun`), dispatched from
 `BtCallbackHandler`: fires the gravity gun (the magnet weapon component) of the mech the AI
 entity drives. It picks nearby physics objects and bodies to attract (restricting the magnet
 component to them) using perception, faction relations, and the mech's turret yaw. `tree` is the
 `STreeInstance`, `registry` the `SAiEntityRegistry`, and `target` the target position; the
 return value is the behavior-tree node result.

functions.name: AiGetClosestEntityInRange
functions.doc:
`_AiGetClosestEntityInRange`: finds the AI entity of `entity_type` (1-based category) closest
 to `point` within `range`, accepted by `faction` (and, with `alive_only`, alive), skipping
 `ignore_entity` and the entity owned by `owner_go`. Writes the found entity handle to
 `found_entity` (0 when none) and returns whether one was found. IDA labels this
 address `CAIPerception::GetCharacterWithMentalState`; it is `_AiGetClosestEntityInRange`.

functions.name: NAutoAimToTarget_Update
functions.doc: The character-state task that overrides the aim direction toward a locked target.

functions.name: NAimIKTask_Update
functions.doc:
The per-frame update of the aim IK task (`NAimIKTask::Update`): the animation state task that
 orients the upper body toward the aim target while aiming a weapon or the grapple, queuing axis
 rotation targets (the chest end among them) weighted by [`AimIKUtil::GetIKWeightValue`].

functions.name: NGrapplingFireArmIK_Update
functions.doc:
The per-frame update of the grapple-fire arm IK task (`NGrapplingFireArmIK::Update`): poses the
 left arm toward the grapple target: reads the hook's last target position against the left
 shoulder and hand and publishes the result through the character blackboard.

functions.name: NLookAtIKTask_Update
functions.doc: The per-frame update of the look-at IK task (`NLookAtIKTask::Update`).

functions.name: NLocoIKTask_Update
functions.doc:
The per-frame update of the locomotion IK task (`NLocoIKTask::Update`), which queues positional
 effector targets through [`HumanIK::AddEffectorTargetPosition`].

functions.name: NHandIKTask_Update
functions.doc: The per-frame hand-IK driver. Sources its targets from weapon grip positions.

functions.name: SetListenerTransform
functions.doc: Sets the 3D audio listener pose and velocity. Free function.

functions.name: Character_GetRenderTransform
functions.doc:
`CCharacter::GetRenderTransform`, a `CGameObject` virtual reached through the
 [`GAME_OBJECT_BASE_OFFSET`](Character::GAME_OBJECT_BASE_OFFSET) subobject (`game_object` is the
 character plus that offset): writes the render transform, the lerp of
 [`m_WorldMatrixT0`](Character::m_WorldMatrixT0) to [`m_WorldMatrixT1`](Character::m_WorldMatrixT1)
 by `dtf`, into `out`, and returns true.

functions.name: Player_UpdatePostCamera
functions.doc:
`CPlayer::UpdatePostCamera`, the player's override of the `CAvatar::UpdatePostCamera` virtual;
 `avatar` is the player's [`Avatar`] base. Runs the aim control's post-simulation update, then
 publishes its weapon aim point to the character (the control parameters' aim target and
 [`Character::UpdateWeaponAiming`]) and its grenade aim point
 ([`Character::UpdateGrenadeAiming`]), and, when the player sits in a vehicle's driver seat, to
 the vehicle ([`Vehicle::SetAimTargetPosition`](vehicle::vehicle::Vehicle::SetAimTargetPosition)).

functions.name: Player_UpdateMentalState
functions.doc:
`CPlayer::UpdateMentalState`, the player's override of the `CAvatar` virtual; `avatar` is the
 player's [`Avatar`] base. After the base update it sets the character's mental state:
 relaxed while [`Character_ForceNonCombat`](character::character::Character_ForceNonCombat) is
 set, combat while [`Character_ForceCombat`](character::character::Character_ForceCombat) is
 set, relaxed while the character is holstering (or a further character state check holds), and
 combat while it has weapon input, throws a grenade, wields a heavy weapon, or aims a weapon
 outside explosive planting. Otherwise combat decays to relaxed once the combat hold expires.

functions.name: CpuFragmentWaitUntilSignalIsNonZero
functions.doc:
Spin-wait (pumping other ready fragments) until `*signal` is non-zero -- one of Avalanche's CPU
 job-fragment primitives, the engine's drain for an outstanding async fragment. For example the
 draw-dispatch fragment signals completion at
 [`m_DrawThreadWorkSignal`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::GraphicsEngine::m_DrawThreadWorkSignal). It
 returns immediately when the signal is already non-zero, and otherwise spins until the matching
 fragment raises it. Below two primary threads ([`CpuPrimaryCount`]) the draw work runs inline and
 never raises its signal, so a wait on that signal never returns.

 The wait is work-stealing: while the signal is zero, the underlying `CpuFragmentWait` loop pops
 queued fragments off the global sync queue and runs them (`CpuFragmentRun`) on the calling
 thread. A fragment run on a thread the fragment system does not know (neither a registered worker
 nor the primary thread) faults on the fragment system's per-thread state.

functions.name: CpuPrimaryCount
functions.doc:
The number of primary job-worker threads. The engine only dispatches the async draw fragment (and
 only waits on its signal) when this is greater than `1`; at or below it the draw runs inline and the
 completion signal is never raised.

functions.name: send_event_msg_impl
functions.doc:
`NEvent::CSendEvent::SendMsg(const char*, void*)`: fires a named engine event to every
 subscribed receiver, with an optional message payload (null for fire-and-forget). This is the
 engine's own idiom for global events (`CDialogue::Play` fires `on_play_dialogue` through it).
 Systems subscribe named events in their `Init`; `CWeatherController` subscribes the weather
 events (`weather_sunny`, `weather_rain`, `weather_snow`, `weather_restore`, `weather_instant`,
 `cloud_base`, and `cloud_height`).

functions.name: UpdateTeleport
functions.doc:
`CGameWorld::UpdateTeleport`: advances the deferred-teleport state machine a
 [`GameWorld::TeleportPlayer`] request armed (fade, optional load state, character placement,
 fade back in). Called from `CGameWorld::UpdatePostSim` each sim tick. `game_world` is the full
 `CGameWorld` object, which embeds the [`GameWorld`] interface subobject (the singleton) after
 its own leading members, so the singleton pointer is not the start of the object.

functions.name: BFBCCalculateCameraFrustum
functions.doc:
Builds a six-plane camera cull frustum into `out` from a row-major view matrix and projection
 matrix: it multiplies them and extracts the planes from the product (Gribb–Hartmann), so the
 result is independent of the projection's handedness and depth convention.

functions.name: BFBCCalculateOccluderFrustums
functions.doc:
Builds the occluder frustums for a cull: selects occluder candidates from `collection` with
 `settings`, then builds a frustum per chosen occluder into `out_frustums`. Returns the number of
 frustums built.

functions.name: GetMasterContext
functions.doc: Returns the master context, the wrapper around the D3D11 immediate context. `device` is unused.

functions.name: GetDeviceInfo
functions.doc:
Copies the device's [`m_DeviceInfo`](Device::m_DeviceInfo) into `out` (a plain `memcpy` of the
 whole descriptor).

functions.name: GetDeviceSurface
functions.doc:
Returns one of the device's presentable surfaces. Only [`BackBuffer`](DeviceSurface::BackBuffer)
 resolves (to [`Device::m_BackBuffer`]); the other selectors return null on this non-stereo device.
 [`CreateRenderSetups`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::GraphicsEngine::CreateRenderSetups) uses it
 to alias `BackBufferLinear` and the back-buffer render setups onto the live swapchain surface.

functions.name: ResizeBuffers
functions.doc:
Resizes the DXGI swapchain's buffers. Unbinds render targets, releases and recreates the back
 buffer's texture/RTV/SRV via `IDXGISwapChain::ResizeBuffers`, and updates
 [`Device::m_DeviceInfo`]'s display dimensions and [`Device::m_WasResized`]. This is the swapchain
 half of a resize, distinct from re-creating the scene render targets in
 [`CreateRenderSetups`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::GraphicsEngine::CreateRenderSetups).

functions.name: DrawIndexed
functions.doc: An indexed draw.

functions.name: Draw
functions.doc: A non-indexed draw.

functions.name: DrawInstanced
functions.doc:
A non-indexed instanced draw: takes the context mutex, flushes the pending render state, and
 issues `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawInstanced` (vtable slot 21).

functions.name: DrawIndexedWithBoundState
functions.doc:
The `(context, first_index, index_count)` overload of `Graphics::DrawIndexed`, which draws with the
 already-bound primitive type and index buffer: takes the context mutex, flushes the pending render
 state, and issues `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexed` (vtable slot 12). The overload that also sets
 the primitive type and buffers is [`DrawIndexed`].

functions.name: DrawIndexedNoMutex
functions.doc:
An indexed draw without the context mutex: flushes the pending render state and issues
 `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexed` (vtable slot 12).

functions.name: DrawIndexedInstancedNoMutex
functions.doc:
An indexed instanced draw without the context mutex: flushes the pending render state and issues
 `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstanced` (vtable slot 20).

functions.name: DrawIndexedInstanced
functions.doc:
An indexed instanced draw: takes the context mutex, flushes the pending render state, and issues
 `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstanced` (vtable slot 20).

functions.name: DrawIndexedInstancedIndirectNoMutex
functions.doc:
A GPU-driven indexed instanced draw without the context mutex: flushes the pending render state
 and issues `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect` (vtable slot 39) with the argument
 buffer of `draw_params` at byte `offset`.

functions.name: DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect
functions.doc:
A GPU-driven indexed instanced draw: takes the context mutex, flushes the pending render state,
 and issues `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect` (vtable slot 39) with the argument
 buffer of `draw_params` at byte `offset`.

functions.name: DrawInstancedIndirect
functions.doc:
A GPU-driven non-indexed instanced draw: takes the context mutex, flushes the pending render
 state, and issues `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawInstancedIndirect` (vtable slot 40) with the argument
 buffer of `draw_params` at byte `offset`.

functions.name: DrawIndexedInstancedMultiIndirect
functions.doc:
`draw_count` GPU-driven indexed instanced draws under one hold of the context mutex: issues
 `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect` (vtable slot 39) once per draw, advancing the
 argument offset by one 20-byte argument record each time.

functions.name: Dispatch
functions.doc:
A compute dispatch of `x` by `y` by `z` thread groups.

 Unlike its neighbours above, this one's demangled symbol agrees with the disassembly: the body
 takes exactly four arguments in `rcx`/`edx`/`r8d`/`r9d`, flushes the pending render state through
 `Graphics::SetupRenderStates`, and forwards the three group counts to the backend's dispatch entry
 under the context's critical section.

 A dispatch is not rasterization, so none of the rasterizer state applies to it: neither the
 viewport nor the scissor rectangle ([`SetScissorEnable`]) restricts which texels a dispatch's
 threads address. The addressed region is decided entirely by the group counts passed here and by
 the compute program's own mapping from `SV_DispatchThreadID` to texel.

functions.name: DispatchIndirect
functions.doc: A GPU-driven compute dispatch.

functions.name: SetRenderSetup
functions.doc: Binds a render setup, the render-target configuration a pass draws into.

functions.name: Clear
functions.doc:
Clears the currently-bound render setup. `flags` is a [`ClearFlags`] mask; `color` is a 4-float
 RGBA pointer and may be null.

functions.name: SetStencilTestEnable
functions.doc:
Stages the stencil-test enable into [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`]; applied
 at the next draw's state flush.

functions.name: SetStencilFunc
functions.doc:
Stages the stencil comparison function and read mask into
 [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`] and the reference value into
 [`HContext_t::m_StencilRef`].

functions.name: SetStencilMask
functions.doc: Stages the stencil write mask into [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`].

functions.name: SetStencilOp
functions.doc:
Stages the stencil fail, depth-fail, and pass operations into
 [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`].

functions.name: CopySurfaceToTexture
functions.doc:
Copies one surface into another texture: a whole-resource `ID3D11DeviceContext::CopyResource`
 of `src`'s D3D11 resource into `dst`'s, issued under the context mutex. IDA
 misplaces this function's name onto [`EndDraw`] and labels this address
 `NGraphicsEngine::CGPUProfiler::BeginScope`; the body is unambiguous.

functions.name: EndDraw
functions.doc:
Submits the frame's recorded command work: under the context's critical section it indexes the
 context's command-slot ring and submits the two prebuilt command objects for the current slot
 through the backend. It takes no arguments beyond the context.

 IDA labels this address `Graphics::CopySurfaceToTexture`; the two
 names are swapped (see [`CopySurfaceToTexture`]).

functions.name: ResolveSurface
functions.doc: Resolves an MSAA surface.

functions.name: SetScissorEnable
functions.doc:
Sets the scissor-enable bit of the context's current rasterizer-state key, which becomes `D3D11_RASTERIZER_DESC::ScissorEnable` when the state object for that key is
 created. The key is looked up (and the object created on first use) by the render-state flush that
 precedes every draw, so the change takes effect from the next draw on. Only the enable flag lives
 in the key: the rectangles themselves are passed straight through to the context's
 `RSSetScissorRects` by a separate wrapper and are ignored while the flag is clear.

functions.name: GetRTVFromSurface
functions.doc: Returns the surface's render-target view.

functions.name: GetDSVFromSurface
functions.doc: Returns the surface's depth-stencil view.

functions.name: CreateFragmentProgram
functions.doc:
The leaf fragment-program creator: it wraps `ID3D11Device::CreatePixelShader` over
 `params.m_Code`/`params.m_Size`. `CreatePixelShader` copies the bytecode, so `params.m_Code` need
 not remain valid past the call, and the returned holder retains no bytecode of its own. Static (no
 `this`); the first argument is the graphics device.

functions.name: CreateVertexProgram
functions.doc:
The leaf vertex-program creator: it wraps `ID3D11Device::CreateVertexShader` over
 `params.m_Code`/`params.m_Size`. Unlike [`CreateFragmentProgram`], the returned holder also
 retains a heap copy of the bytecode (used later for input-layout creation), so both the D3D
 object and the retained copy reflect whatever bytecode was passed in. Static (no `this`); the
 first argument is the graphics device.

functions.name: CreateHullProgram
functions.doc:
The leaf hull-program creator: it wraps `ID3D11Device::CreateHullShader` (vtable slot 16) over
 `params.m_Code`/`params.m_Size`. `CreateHullShader` copies the bytecode, so `params.m_Code` need not
 remain valid past the call; unlike [`CreateVertexProgram`], the returned holder is a bare shader
 pointer with no retained bytecode copy. Static (no `this`); the first argument is the graphics
 device.

functions.name: CreateDomainProgram
functions.doc:
The leaf domain-program creator: it wraps `ID3D11Device::CreateDomainShader` (vtable slot 17) over
 `params.m_Code`/`params.m_Size`. `CreateDomainShader` copies the bytecode, so `params.m_Code` need
 not remain valid past the call; like [`CreateHullProgram`], the returned holder is a bare shader
 pointer with no retained bytecode copy. Static (no `this`); the first argument is the graphics
 device.

functions.name: SetFragmentProgramConstants
functions.doc:
Stages `count` float4 constants into the given fragment constant buffer slot, starting at
 `start_offset`, writing to the context's per-slot staging buffer and setting the dirty flag. The
 actual GPU upload happens at the next state flush.

 The staging buffer is a single 512-row `float4` array per shader stage, held in the graphics
 context (the fragment one follows the vertex one); the
 four slots of a stage carve their windows out of it, each starting at the row
 [`SetFragmentProgramConstantBufferSize`] recorded for it. The write is therefore bounded by that
 window and by the pooled buffer the slot is bound to, not by `count` alone. A row-level redundancy
 check skips rows byte-identical to what is already staged, and a call that skips every row leaves
 the dirty flag alone.

functions.name: SetFragmentProgramConstantBufferSize
functions.doc:
Declares how large a fragment constant-buffer slot is for the draws that follow, and where in the
 stage's shared staging array its window begins.

 `count` is a number of `float4` rows. It is not stored as-is: the engine rounds it **up** to the
 next entry of [`constant_buffer_size_classes`] and binds the pre-created `ID3D11Buffer` of that
 size to the slot (a
 `PSSetConstantBuffers` call, skipped when the size class is unchanged). The rounded size class,
 not `count`, is what [`SetupRenderStates`] later uploads, so the constant buffer the shader sees is
 the rounded one and the rows between `count` and the size class are uploaded as whatever the
 staging array happens to hold. `start_offset` is recorded as the slot's base row within the
 stage's 512-row staging array; every call passes `0`, so at most one staged slot per stage
 is live at a time. Passing `count = 0` unbinds the slot and clears its dirty flag.

 The function stores only the bound buffer, the size class, and the base row. It does not keep
 `count`, and [`SetFragmentProgramConstants`] performs no bounds check against it.

functions.name: SetVertexProgramConstantBufferSize
functions.doc:
The vertex analogue of [`SetFragmentProgramConstantBufferSize`], over the vertex staging array and
 the vertex slots' pooled buffers.

functions.name: SetupRenderStates
functions.doc:
Flushes the graphics context's deferred state to D3D11 ahead of a draw: for each of the four slots
 of each shader stage whose dirty flag is set, maps its bound constant buffer with
 `D3D11_MAP_WRITE_DISCARD` and copies `16 * size_class` bytes into it from the stage's staging array
 starting at the slot's base row — the **rounded** size class from
 [`SetFragmentProgramConstantBufferSize`], not the requested row count — then resolves the
 depth-stencil, blend, and rasterizer state objects from their cached descriptors.

functions.name: SetVertexProgramConstants
functions.doc:
Stages `count` float4 constants into the given **vertex** constant buffer slot, starting at
 `start_offset` (in float4 rows), writing to the context's per-slot staging buffer and setting the
 dirty flag; the GPU upload happens at the next state flush. The vertex analogue of
 [`SetFragmentProgramConstants`]. `cb_index` is the vertex-shader constant-buffer slot (e.g. `1`
 for `cb1`). A row-level redundancy check skips rows byte-identical to what is already staged.

functions.name: SetGeometryProgramConstants
functions.doc:
Stages `count` float4 constants into the given **geometry** constant buffer slot, starting at
 `start_offset` (in float4 rows), writing to the context's per-slot staging buffer and setting the
 dirty flag; the GPU upload happens at the next state flush. The geometry analogue of
 [`SetFragmentProgramConstants`]. The clustered deferred-lighting pass is the volume user: it
 stages the light-assignment geometry shader's `ProjMatrix` here as four rows on `cb0`.

functions.name: SetupRenderStates
functions.doc:
The pre-draw pipeline-state flush at the top of every draw wrapper: for each dirty state category
 (samplers, depth-stencil, blend, rasterizer) it decodes the packed state index staged on the context
 -- creating and caching the D3D state object on first use ([`CreateDepthStencilState`]) -- binds it,
 and clears the dirty flag. The depth-stencil bind reads
 [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`] / [`HContext_t::m_StencilRef`] and issues the sole
 `OMSetDepthStencilState`, only when the index or ref changed since the last draw.

functions.name: CreateDepthStencilState
functions.doc:
Decodes a packed depth-stencil state index (see [`HContext_t::m_DepthStencilStateIndex`]) into a
 `D3D11_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC` and creates+caches the `ID3D11DepthStencilState`. Called by
 [`SetupRenderStates`] on the first bind of each distinct index.

functions.name: SetRenderSetup
functions.doc:
Binds a render setup as the active output on the context and sets the viewport. Applies the setup's
 render-target views and depth-stencil (`OMSetRenderTargets`), then sets the rasterizer viewport:
 [`HRenderSetup_t::m_Viewport`] when [`HRenderSetup_t::m_HasCustomViewport`] is set, otherwise a
 synthesized viewport covering the full render target (`0, 0, width, height, 0, 1`). It is the single
 viewport write on the render-setup path -- the passes that draw after it inherit this viewport.
 `force` re-applies the setup even when it matches the currently-bound one; its exact effect is
 unconfirmed.

functions.name: CreateTimeStampQuery
functions.doc:
Creates a `D3D11_QUERY_TIMESTAMP` query on the device (device vtable `CreateQuery`); raises the
 graphics critical-error path on failure.

functions.name: DestroyTimeStampQuery
functions.doc: Releases a timestamp query.

functions.name: SetTimeStampQuery
functions.doc:
Records a timestamp on the context (`ID3D11DeviceContext::End` on the query), under the context
 mutex when present.

functions.name: QueryTimeStamp
functions.doc:
Reads a timestamp query's tick value (`GetData`, non-blocking). Returns `0` while the result is
 still pending.

functions.name: CreateTimeStampDisjointQuery
functions.doc:
Creates a `D3D11_QUERY_TIMESTAMP_DISJOINT` query on the device; raises the graphics
 critical-error path on failure.

functions.name: DestroyTimeStampDisjointQuery
functions.doc: Releases a timestamp-disjoint query.

functions.name: BeginTimeStampDisjointQuery
functions.doc:
Begins the disjoint interval (`ID3D11DeviceContext::Begin`), under the context mutex when
 present.

functions.name: EndTimeStampDisjointQuery
functions.doc:
Ends the disjoint interval (`ID3D11DeviceContext::End`). The body is
 identical-code-folded with [`SetTimeStampQuery`] (both call `End` under the context mutex), so
 this shares its address. IDA places this name on an unrelated
 two-instruction stub.

functions.name: QueryTimeStampFrequency
functions.doc:
Reads a disjoint query's result (`GetData`, non-blocking): writes the GPU tick frequency to
 `out_frequency` (`0` while pending) and returns the interval's status.

functions.name: BeginScopeMarker
functions.doc:
The developer scope-marker begin: opens a named instrumentation scope on the context. Compiled
 to an empty function, but its call sites and name strings survive
 throughout the renderer -- the frame stages in `CGraphicsEngine::HandleDrawThreadTask`
 (`"Frame setup"`, `"CopyEffectTextures"`, `"Debug UI"`), the post-effect stack (SMAA, FXAA,
 depth of field, motion blur, lens flare, glare, tone mapping), deferred lighting, SSAO, SSR,
 environment reflections, water, terrain restores, and the per-render-block-type runs opened by
 [`RenderPass::ChangeRenderBlockType`](graphics_engine::render_pass::RenderPass::ChangeRenderBlockType)
 (named by each type's
 [`GetTypeName`](graphics_engine::render_engine::RenderBlockTypeBase::GetTypeName)). Scopes nest
 per context and are closed by [`EndScopeMarker`]; the RAII wrapper `Graphics::CScopeMarker`
 calls the pair from its constructor and destructor.

functions.name: EndScopeMarker
functions.doc:
Closes the innermost scope opened by [`BeginScopeMarker`] on the context. Compiled to an empty
 function; the call sites survive.

functions.name: graphics_flip
functions.doc: The low-level present.

functions.name: HandleDrawThreadTaskProxy
functions.doc:
The fragment-job trampoline `CGraphicsEngine::DispatchDraw` posts when the draw runs on a worker:
 loads the graphics engine singleton and tail-calls
 [`HandleDrawThreadTask`](GraphicsEngine::HandleDrawThreadTask) with `param`.

functions.name: GetViewProjInverse
functions.doc:
Builds the depth-of-field chain's clip-to-world basis into `out`, which is also returned.

 It rebuilds the clip-to-view inverse from the post-effect render context's vertical field of view,
 aspect ratio, and far/near planes via [`Matrix4::PerspectiveFovInverse`](types::math::Matrix4), then
 multiplies that by the context's camera transform with the translation row replaced by
 `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, so the result maps clip space to a camera-relative world direction. Being rebuilt
 from a field of view and an aspect ratio, it can only describe a symmetric frustum, whatever
 projection the context actually carries.

 Its one caller is [`DownScale2x2PackFocus::Apply`], which uploads the result as vertex constants
 1..4 of the packing draw that ends the bokeh downscale prepass.

functions.name: DrawWaterBoxSurface
functions.doc:
Draws every registered water box's surface grid, under the water-box manager's critical section:
 for each box, frustum-culls it against `CCameraManager::GetRenderCamera()`, stages the box
 transform — `CMatrix4f::Scaling` by the box half-extents, with the translation set to the box
 centre minus the render context's camera world position — on **vertex constant-buffer bank 2,
 registers 0..3**, and issues the grid as a plain [`DrawIndexed`] (162 primitives, or 6 in the
 manager's simplified mode). Inlined from
 [`WaterBoxRenderBlock::DrawSurface`](WaterBoxRenderBlock::DrawSurface), whose doc records the
 clip path the `waterboxsurface` shader builds from it. Called by
 [`NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw) once the ocean quadtree is
 down.

functions.name: SetupWaterBoxSurface
functions.doc:
Binds the water-box surface state ahead of [`DrawWaterBoxSurface`](DrawWaterBoxSurface): under the
 same critical section, and only when at least one box is registered, it fetches the shared
 [`WaterBoxRenderBlockType`](WaterBoxRenderBlockType) off the first box's render block and forwards
 to [`SetupSurface`](WaterBoxRenderBlockType::SetupSurface).

functions.name: WaveWorksSimulationStep
functions.doc:
Advances the WaveWorks ocean simulation one step and blocks until its displacement readback is
 available (`GFSDK_WaveWorks_Simulation_Simulation` — a helper in the game's own image, named by
 its telemetry zone, not an export of `gfsdk_waveworks.win64.dll`).

 Sets the simulation time, then loops `WaitStagingCursor` + `KickD3D11` until the staging cursor
 reports the readback is no longer in flight, and archives the resulting displacement snapshot —
 which is what the CPU-side wave-height and buoyancy queries
 (`GFSDK_WaveWorks_Simulation_GetArchivedDisplacements`) read. Finally restores the D3D state the
 kick changed from the shared savestate.

 Called once per frame from [`NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw`](NvWaterHighEndRenderBlock::Draw).
 It is not idempotent: each call archives another displacement snapshot and can block on the
 staging cursor.

functions.name: GetRenderPassName
functions.doc:
The debug name for a render-pass id, from the engine's pass-name switch (the ground truth the
 [`RenderPassId`] values are verified against). Returns `"NONE"` for unnamed indices.

functions.name: GetRenderPassCategory
functions.doc:
Maps a render-pass id to its coarse category (`ERenderPassCategory`, 30 values: terrain,
 shadows, GBuffer, lighting, water, particles, post effects, UI, ...). The crash-telemetry
 metrics aggregate per-pass GPU times by this grouping.

functions.name: GetRenderPassCategoryName
functions.doc: The display name for a render-pass category, or null for out-of-range values.

functions.name: TerrainPatchSystemUpdate
functions.doc:
The once-per-frame terrain patch system update (called from `CLandscapeManager::UpdateRender` in the
 sim phase). When [`STerrainPatchSystem::m_UpdateCamera`] is set it copies the LOD camera
 ([`m_ActiveCamera`](camera::camera_manager::CameraManager::m_ActiveCamera)) into [`STerrainPatchSystem::m_TerrainCamera`] and points every
 terrain render pass's frustum camera at it. `ctx` carries the source camera.

functions.name: GetRenderPassInfo
functions.doc:
Returns the display name of render pass `pass` and writes its category (`ERenderPassCategory`) to
 `out_category` and the name to `out_name`; unknown ids give `"NONE"` and category 0.

functions.name: CalculateOffsetViewProjectionMatrix
functions.doc:
Copies `src` (a view matrix), zeroes its translation row, and multiplies by `proj`, writing the
 translation-free offset view-projection into `dst`. This is the view-projection that camera-relative
 opaque geometry actually uses; the camera world position is supplied separately. Static.

functions.name: CalculateOffsetWorldViewProjectionMatrix
functions.doc:
Copies the world matrix `world` into `dst`, makes its translation row relative to
 [`RenderContext::m_CameraPosition`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_CameraPosition)
 (with `w = 1`), and multiplies it by
 [`RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::RenderContext::m_OffsetViewProjection):
 the camera-relative world-view-projection the render blocks bake into their constant buffers
 (`CRenderBlock::CalculateOffsetWorldViewProjectionMatrix`). Static.

functions.name: Create2DTexture
functions.doc:
Creates a 2D texture: allocates the `0x58`-byte texture handle, creates the D3D11 resource
 from `params`, and creates the views the usage implies (a shader-resource view for
 non-staging textures, plus an unordered-access view when the params ask for one). A creation
 failure routes through the graphics critical-error path rather than returning null.

 A texture is not by itself drawable: a render target is obtained from it with
 [`GetRenderTarget`].

functions.name: Destroy2DTexture
functions.doc: Releases a texture's D3D11 resource and views and frees its handle.

functions.name: GetRenderTarget
functions.doc:
Returns a render-target surface over a slice of `texture`: a texture handle carrying the
 render-target (or depth-stencil) view for the selected mip level, cube face, and array range.
 This is the second half of the engine's standard scene-target construction —
 [`Create2DTexture`] for the storage, then `GetRenderTarget` for the surface bound as a render
 setup's target.

functions.name: CreateSurfaceAlias
functions.doc:
Creates a second surface over an existing surface's D3D11 resource at a different format: it
 copies the source handle wholesale, **takes a D3D11 reference on the source resource**, and
 creates fresh shader-resource, render-target, and depth-stencil views at the requested
 format. No pixels are copied, and writes through the alias land in the source resource.

 Because the alias holds a reference on the underlying resource, a swapchain buffer that is
 aliased cannot be resized until the alias is destroyed — `IDXGISwapChain::ResizeBuffers`
 fails while any reference to buffer 0 outstands.

 When the source is the device back buffer and the requested format already equals the back
 buffer's format, the shader-resource view is skipped and the alias' own view is left null.

functions.name: DestroySurface
functions.doc:
Releases a surface's D3D11 views and frees its handle. In this build no active/inactive
 bookkeeping survives, so destroying a surface twice is an unguarded use-after-free rather
 than a trapped assertion.

functions.name: CreateRenderSetup
functions.doc:
Creates a render setup, the render-target configuration a pass binds with
 [`SetRenderSetup`](graphics_engine::graphics_engine::SetRenderSetup): it allocates the
 setup, copies the depth target and the three target/UAV arrays
 verbatim, and derives each array's count by scanning for the first null. It reads no width or
 height — the setup's dimensions come entirely from its bound targets, which is why
 `SetRenderSetup` can synthesize a full-target viewport from them.

functions.name: DestroyRenderSetup
functions.doc:
Frees a render setup. If it is the device's currently-bound setup it is unbound first (via
 `SetRenderSetup(context, null, false)`), so destroying a bound setup is safe. The targets the
 setup referenced are not touched.

functions.name: CalculateMidAndBrightPointForHistogram
functions.doc: Computes the histogram mid and bright points, the per-frame eye-adaptation lerp.

functions.name: UpdateFallSteering
functions.doc:
Air-steer helper: computes the airborne desired facing and steered velocity for a character from
 its stick input and the camera input matrix (`GetInputMatrix`). `out_facing` defaults to the
 character's current world-forward (`-m_WorldMatrixT1` third basis row) and is overwritten with the
 camera-relative steer direction only under meaningful stick input. `out_velocity_norm` /
 `out_speed` carry the steered velocity. Called from
 [`NStateTask_MovementJumpTask::Update`](NStateTask_MovementJumpTask::Update) (jump ascent) and
 `NAirMovement::UpdateAirPhysics` (fall), so it governs body facing across the whole airborne arc.
 The return is a leaked `out_facing` pointer the callers discard.

functions.name: UpdateParachutePhysics
functions.doc:
The parachute flight/steering core, called per frame by
 [`NStateTask_MovementParachuteTask::Update`]. Computes the parachute steering values, the
 wanted character yaw/pitch/roll, and the camera-relative look steer via
 [`GetParachuteSteeringValues`], then drives the parachute velocities and the character/
 canopy orientation through the parachute action params' proxy matrices.

functions.name: GetParachuteSteeringValues
functions.doc:
The parachute steering helper, called from [`UpdateParachutePhysics`]. Computes the steering
 values for the desired character yaw/pitch/roll from the input vector and the *camera input
 matrix* (`GameCameraManager::GetInputMatrix`): the stick input is mixed through
 `m_XInputYawPitchRollAmount`/`m_YInputYawPitchRollAmount`, while the camera-relative look is
 shaped by `m_LookSteer*` (deadzone, max yaw, exponential) into `look_steer_out` and blended in.
 Also computes the velocity-alignment steering toward the horizontal velocity.

functions.name: UpdateParachutingTransforms
functions.doc:
Slerps the character and canopy proxy orientations in the parachute action params toward the
 wanted orientation. Called from [`UpdateParachutePhysics`].

functions.name: ApplyConventionalParachuteVelocities
functions.doc:
Computes the conventional (physics-driven) parachute velocity from the steering values, the
 orientation, and the current velocity. Called from [`UpdateParachutePhysics`].

functions.name: ApplyAnimationVelocityWithSteering
functions.doc:
Computes the parachute velocity from the animation root velocity with steering applied. Called
 from [`UpdateParachutePhysics`].

functions.name: UpdateSurfaceMovement
functions.doc:
The surface-swim movement core, called per frame by
 [`NStateTask_MovementSurfaceSwimTask::Update`] for the player. Computes buoyancy and the swim
 velocity, and applies the body orientation: the heading slerps from the latched animated-turn
 base direction to the target direction with the interpolant driven by the local time of the
 angle-correction animation segment (`ang_corr_seg_id`), is held at the current forward outside
 the steering segment (`steering_seg_id`), is blended with the water-surface plane for roll, and
 is written through [`PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation`] -- so the heading changes in
 act-sized steps rather than continuously. `warping_seg_id` drives the position warp toward a
 grapple or planted-explosive target. The segment ids are the task's loaded properties, passed
 as `idstring<SSegmentIdTag>` references.

functions.name: UpdateUnderwaterMovement
functions.doc:
The underwater-swim movement core, called per frame by
 [`NStateTask_MovementUnderWaterSwimTask::Update`]. Same orientation structure as
 [`UpdateSurfaceMovement`] -- segment-gated animated-turn slerp applied through
 [`PfxCharacterInstance::SetOrientation`] -- with the pitch following the three-dimensional swim
 direction instead of the surface plane.

functions.name: UpdateSurfaceMovementNPC
functions.doc:
The surface-swim movement core for NPCs, called by
 [`NStateTask_MovementSurfaceSwimTask::Update`] when the character is not the player.

functions.name: TerrainPatchUpdate
functions.doc:
The per-patch CPU fragment for the base VolumetricTerrain patch maps (registered against the
 [`TerrainPatchUpdate`] hash by `OldTerrainPatchSystem::TerrainPatchSystemCreateLayers`). It
 advances patch construction and destruction (creating or destroying the patch's
 [`RenderBlockTerrain`](graphics_engine::render_block::RenderBlockTerrain) constant buffers,
 updating the global terrain mask, and adjusting per-LOD memory statistics), and for constructed
 patches it updates the block's alpha fade, sort id, and tessellated index count, then submits
 the block to one render pass per set [`PatchHeader::m_VisibilityBits`] bit:
 [`FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA) routes to the color passes
 (the near-detail pass for base-LOD tiles within one tile of the camera, the near pass for other
 tiles at the context's high-detail LOD, and the far pass otherwise), the
 `FRUSTUM_ID_SHADOW_PASS_*` ids to the static shadow passes (only when the terrain type renders
 to shadow maps), the `FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_*` ids to the reflective shadow passes, and
 [`FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS) to the depth prepass.

functions.name: TerrainPatchSystemFragment
functions.doc:
The per-patch CPU fragment for the volumetric-patch terrain maps (the
 `CRenderBlockTerrainPatch` system — the terrain renderer active in the game world; the
 [`TerrainPatchUpdate`] maps are dormant there). Structurally parallel to [`TerrainPatchUpdate`]:
 it advances patch construction and destruction, and for constructed patches updates the block's
 alpha fade and tessellated index count, then submits the patch's render blocks to one render
 pass per set [`PatchHeader::m_VisibilityBits`] bit with the same frustum-id routing
 ([`FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_MAIN_CAMERA) to the color passes, the
 `FRUSTUM_ID_SHADOW_PASS_*` ids to the shadow passes, the ids from
 [`FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_0`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_REFLECTIVE_SHADOW_0) up to
 [`FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS`](PatchFrustumId::FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS), exclusive, to the
 reflective shadow passes, and `FRUSTUM_ID_DEPTH_PREPASS` to the depth prepass). Base-LOD (9)
 patches within the camera's 2x2 quadrant additionally submit per-quadrant sub-blocks to the
 near/tessellation passes.

functions.name: TreeDataPatch
functions.doc:
A per-patch CPU fragment with no per-patch work (`TreeDataPatch`; identical
 bodies may share this address): it only completes pending lifecycle transitions, finishing a
 pending destruction (clearing [`PatchHeader::m_DynamicSize`] and setting
 [`STATUS_DESTRUCTION_COMPLETE`](PatchHeader::STATUS_DESTRUCTION_COMPLETE)) or a pending
 construction (setting
 [`STATUS_CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE`](PatchHeader::STATUS_CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE)).

functions.name: TerrainPatchSystemCreateLayers
functions.doc:
The base VolumetricTerrain patch system's construction-time setup
 (`OldTerrainPatchSystem::TerrainPatchSystemCreateLayers`): for each of the four base LODs it
 allocates the map's `CRenderBlockTerrain` array in constant memory, creates the blocks, and
 registers the `terrain_patch_lod%d` patch map (fragment [`TerrainPatchUpdate`]) with a
 dependency on the previous layer.

functions.name: UpdateTessellatedTriangles
functions.doc:
Computes a streamed terrain patch's tessellated triangle count for the camera at `cam_pos`
 (`patch` is the `STerrainStreamPatch`): with `metric_type`
 [`TESSELLATION_METRIC_DISTANCE`] it scales each quad's tessellation by the camera's distance
 beyond the patch bounds divided by `tess_factor_edge`; with
 [`TESSELLATION_METRIC_MANUAL`] it compares each quad's metric against `manual_metric_value`. The
 terrain patch update stores the result on the patch's render block.

functions.name: SweptSphereCast
functions.doc:
`SweptSphereCast`: a free-function sphere sweep that fills `result` (`CCastResult`). The
 meaning of its scalar parameters is not established.

functions.name: SlerpAroundAxis
functions.doc:
Rotates `from` toward `to` by the fraction `t` of the angle between them (about the axis of the
 shortest-arc rotation), writing the result to `out`. When the two directions are within the
 `0.99` dot-product threshold it writes `to` unchanged. The swim movement cores call it.

functions.name: DoRotate
functions.doc:
Rotates `from` toward `to` along the shortest arc, writing the result to `out`. It takes the
 rotation from `from` to `to` as an angle-axis pair and applies
 `min(angle / 0.2617994, 1) * rate` of it, so the step eases out as the two directions converge.
 Note that the step is **not** clamped to the remaining angle: a `rate` above 0.2617994 radians
 (15 degrees) overshoots the target, and one above twice that diverges. It logs `"UHOH!"` when
 the two directions are more than about 162 degrees apart, where the rotation axis is
 ill-conditioned.

 The swim locomotion family calls it from two places per frame, for two different quantities:

 - [`UpdateSurfaceMovement`](input::swim::UpdateSurfaceMovement) and
   [`UpdateUnderwaterMovement`](input::swim::UpdateUnderwaterMovement) rotate the character's
   current forward toward the desired direction (the world move direction from
   [`ControllerUtility::TransformInputDirToWorldDir`](input::controller_utility::ControllerUtility::TransformInputDirToWorldDir)
   while moving, the aim-target direction while aiming, the grapple target while reeling, or the
   current forward when the stick is neutral). The result is the `direction` argument to
   `CMatrix4f::CreateOrientation`, so **this call is what turns the body**.
 - [`ProcessMotion`] slerps the character's current velocity direction toward the wanted one.

functions.name: ProcessMotion
functions.doc:
Turns a wanted velocity into the velocity actually applied this frame: it slerps the direction
 of `current_vel` toward the direction of `wanted_vel` through [`DoRotate`], limited to
 `slerp_delta_angle` radians, then rescales the result to the horizontal magnitude of
 `wanted_vel`. Either direction falls back to the character's world-matrix forward when it is
 degenerate, and `xz_only` flattens both onto the ground plane first. `dt` is unused: the
 magnitude comes from `wanted_vel`, not from integration. The surface swim movement core uses it
 to keep a swimmer's motion from snapping direction when the stick swings.

functions.name: CreateObjectsAsync
functions.doc:
`CResourceLoaderRuntimeContainerHandler_CreateObjectsAsync`: the background job body that turns a
 loaded runtime container into game objects. It walks the container's objects, creates each
 through its registered game-object creator, applies the set-properties batches (attached
 effects, physics parameters, events, model lookups), builds the hierarchy transforms, and hands
 the result to `CGameWorldLoaderRC::OnLoaded`. `job_data` is the handler's job context; the
 return value is the job status.

functions.name: GetFrameProfilerInputs
functions.doc:
Reads the frame profiler's input actions into the out flags (creating the
 [`SteeringFrameProfiler`] on first use): up and down as held, left, right, close, change-sorting,
 show-empty-timers, and pause as clicked, and `toggle_input_focus` set on the frame both focus
 buttons become held together.

functions.name: FrameProfilerOverridePlayerInputs
functions.doc:
Resets the player and debug steerings' input action maps, so input consumed by the frame
 profiler does not also drive the player.
